author: shayanabedi
body:
## Summary

Documentation-only change to `docs/implement-connection-portal.md`, clarifying which window messages the Connection Portal emits and who is responsible for closing what.

- Documents **`CLOSE_MODAL`** explicitly — it was previously only referenced indirectly, despite being the signal the `snaptrade-react` SDK uses to close the modal.
- Corrects **`CLOSED`**: it's a plain string, iframe-only, and a best-effort abandonment signal sent after the retry screen — not simply "the user closed the OAuth window".
- Corrects **`ABANDONED`**: it was described as "functions the same as `CLOSE_MODAL`", which conflated the iframe and non-iframe exit signals.
- Adds a **"Who closes the window?"** section with a table of what SnapTrade closes vs. what the integrating app must close, per integration method (React SDK, iframe, new tab, mobile in-app browser).
- Links the new section from the iframe key-considerations list, and notes in the new-tab section that the portal never closes its own tab.

## Test plan

Docs only — no code or SDK changes. Verify the rendered page and that the `#implement-connection-portal-who-closes-the-window` anchor resolves in the docs portal preview.

author: lireland7
body:
## Summary

Two big additions this session: the **game replay recorder** (foundation for visual playback) and an **HSReplay-style deck & legend stats** overhaul.

### Replay recorder
A replay is just the semantic tracker event stream persisted per game — no pixels, no DOM — so a full game is a few KB gzipped.
- Captures **board frames** (card id + zone + owner + face + position) on change, deduped, plus deck/draw/recycle/remove events, into a gzipped `.rrz` file under `Documents/RiftReplay/replays/`.
- Starts on `deck-snapshot`, finalizes on game end; safety nets finalize on the next game's snapshot and on app quit so a game is never stranded in memory.
- **Broadened the game-end signal** to `has left the game` / `conceded` / `forfeited` / `Connection lost with`. This fixes the earlier bug where the auto record-prompt and replay-save missed the `…has left the game voluntarily` wording.

### New per-game capture (card-level stats)
- `kept_cards` (opening hand kept = hand − mulliganed) and `played_cards` (`Name@turnPlayed@turnsHeld`), with draw-turn tracking for "turns held".
- New CSV columns are appended last, with **automatic header migration** so existing `matches.csv` keeps working.

### Deck library
- `decks.json` stores each deck's decklist and appends a new version only when it changes between games → powers the decklist panel and the +/− change history.

### Rebuilt Deck Stats tab (gated on selecting a deck)
- **Decklist panel** with card art, **dated change history** (+added / −removed), and a **per-card grid**: Kept WR, Kept %, Drawn WR, Played WR, turns Held, Turn played.
- Sideboard-draw W/R now **excludes game 1** (no sideboarding there).

### Legend stats
- **Matchup matrix**: your legend (rows) × opponent legend (columns), populated with legend art. Runs on existing history.
- Record-form legend fields are now **searchable image dropdowns**, still auto-filled with the detected legend.
- **Legend canonicalization by champion**: Unit forms and art variants (`Viktor, Leader` / `Viktor, Herald of the Arcane`) fold into one legend, fixing duplicate matrix rows/columns and dropdown entries — **retroactive** for existing data.

## Reviewer notes
- Most card-level columns (Kept/Played/Held/Turn) and the decklist/history are **new data that only fills in for games recorded after this ships**; Drawn WR and the matchup matrix work on existing history immediately.
- Card art and the legend list load from the card-DB CDN when the Stats/Record windows open; everything degrades gracefully (names + placeholder tiles) if that request is blocked.
- No version bump here — this is code only; the next release will bump and publish.

## Test plan
- [x] Board frames capture; `.rrz` saved on game end (opponent leaving)
- [x] Auto record-prompt fires on "has left the game"
- [ ] Play/record games, confirm per-card grid + decklist + change history populate
- [ ] Matchup matrix merges same-champion legend forms into one row/column
- [ ] Record-form legend dropdown shows images and canonicalizes the detected form

author: hissado
body:
## Objet

Correction de la **duplication de navigation** constatée en production (capture d'écran) : les modules qui disposent d'un panneau détaillé propre (`ModuleShell`) affichaient **deux** navigations simultanées — la barre latérale globale (bleue) *et* le panneau du module (blanc) —, organisées différemment (rubriques répétées, sous-modules mal positionnés). Audit §J.

## Principe appliqué

Pour chaque module ayant un panneau détaillé : **barre bleue = lanceur**, **panneau blanc = détail** (hiérarchie Module → Rubrique → Sous-rubrique en un seul endroit). Cross-check anti-orphelin systématique : toute page retirée de la barre bleue doit rester présente dans le panneau.

## Par module

**RH** (`450edea`)
- Barre bleue réduite à 2 lanceurs (« Mon espace » pour tous, « Ressources Humaines » pour les gestionnaires — **gating par rôle préservé**).
- 4 pages qui n'étaient que dans la barre bleue ajoutées au panneau `HrShell` : Présence & absence (`/presences`), Kiosques (`/kiosques`), Avances sur salaire (`/rh/avances-salaire`), Intelligence RH (`/rh/intelligence`).

**Comptabilité** (`29d5c5f`)
- Barre bleue : section « Comptabilité » réduite à un lanceur (`→ /comptabilite`).
- Panneau `AccountingShell` complété par les états financiers (Bilan, Compte de résultat, Balance) et la Clôture des périodes, jusque-là seulement dans la barre bleue.

**Marketing / Achats** — aucun changement nécessaire
- Marketing : la barre bleue n'a déjà qu'un lanceur (`/marketing`), le détail (13 pages) est dans le panneau.
- Achats : `_shared.tsx` = utilitaires (badges de statut), pas une navigation ; le module n'a pas de panneau secondaire → pas de duplication.

## Vérifications

- Cross-check anti-orphelin : **aucune page orpheline** (chaque chemin retiré de la barre bleue reste présent dans le panneau).
- Typecheck frontend **24 = base** (zéro nouvelle erreur).
- `check-routes` : **488 fichiers, 200 routes, aucun lien cassé**.

## À valider en préproduction

- **Rendu visuel** de la navigation (impossible à produire ici) : vérifier d'un coup d'œil qu'il n'y a plus deux menus RH/Comptabilité côte à côte, et que le panneau du module couvre bien tous les parcours.

author: ronenmars
body:
## Problem and root cause

A managed agent PTY was owned by the streamer process and, indirectly, by whichever WebSocket clients happened to be subscribed to it.
Agent work was therefore only as durable as a phone's socket and the streamer's uptime.

**1. The last subscriber leaving killed the agent.**
`handleWsClose` armed a grace timer when a session's subscriber set emptied; after `ptyGracePeriodMs` (default 4.5 min) it called `putOnHold`, which is a euphemism — it `SIGINT`s the agent, disposes the render screen, and deletes the session.
A `running` session deferred up to `GRACE_MAX_DEFERS` (4) times, so a long turn survived at most ~22 minutes before being killed mid-response anyway.
In practice: a phone that backgrounds, loses signal, or switches Wi-Fi to cellular drops its socket, and a long agent task is on a countdown to termination.

**2. Nothing about a managed session was persisted.**
There was no sessions table. `SessionsRepository` said so in its own docstring: "Sessions live in-memory in SessionStore."
A restart lost `startedAt`, `promptCount`, `sessionName`, `projectId`, `boundConversationId` (the Codex placeholder-to-rollout binding), and `failureReason`.
Sessions did not come back as recoverable — they ceased to exist, reappearing at best as external processes with no managed metadata.

**3. The status vocabulary could not express any of it.**
`idle` meant finished, killed-to-save-resources, and externally-discovered all at once.

## Design decisions

**Phase 1 — disconnect no longer kills.**
A socket closing is not a request to stop the agent, so `handleWsClose` arms nothing.
Explicit `hold_session` still terminates: that one is a real user intent.
The resource bound moves to an idle reaper that measures *agent* silence rather than subscriber absence, and never considers a `running` session at any age.

**Phase 2 — durable registry.**
Migration `010` adds `managed_sessions`, written at spawn, on every status transition, and at shutdown.
`close()` now stamps live sessions before `dispose()` kills them, so the next boot can tell a deliberate restart from a crash.
Deliberately not stored: the PTY ring buffer and xterm screen — their authoritative copy is the provider's JSONL, so persisting 64 KiB of ANSI per chunk would be a write storm to duplicate what we can re-read.

**Phase 3a — boot reconciliation.**
On startup every non-terminal row is probed and classified: `attached`, `detached`, `orphaned`, `resumable`, `completed`, `failed`.
Two rules keep it safe. A stored status is never trusted over a live probe, since a `SIGKILL`ed streamer never ran its exit writes and can leave a row claiming `running` forever.
And liveness is never treated as identity: a live pid whose argv does not carry the recorded token is reported `orphaned` and never signalled, because pids get recycled and the alternative is killing an unrelated user process.
The reconciler probes and classifies; it never signals anything.

## A measurement that reshaped the task

node-pty spawns with `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID`, so every agent is already a session leader in its own process group.
It is tempting to conclude agents would survive a restart if we simply stopped calling `kill()`.
They do not — verified directly:

> A parent spawns a node-pty child running a 20-second heartbeat, then exits after 1.5 s **without** killing it. The heartbeat stops at 1.5 s.
> The identical probe with `trap '' HUP` in the child runs all 20 seconds, ~10 s after the parent is gone.

The mechanism is the controlling terminal: closing the last PTY **master** fd makes the kernel `SIGHUP` the foreground process group, and `setsid` is what elects the agent to receive it.
So restart survival needs the master fd to outlive the streamer — the daemon follow-up (Phase 3b), scoped out here with the measurement as its justification.
`__tests__/pty-parent-exit-hangup.test.ts` pins this so a node-pty upgrade cannot silently change it.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope: PTY lifetime vs subscribers, session persistence, boot reconciliation, the lifecycle axis.

Not in scope: semantic state confidence (C3), multi-client input ordering (C4), auth/capabilities (C5), and Phase 3b master-fd relocation.

## Test evidence

Full suite on this branch: **150 files, 1207 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures.**
`tsc --noEmit` clean; biome clean on all changed files.

New coverage:
- `__tests__/reconcile-sessions.test.ts` — 11 classification cases, including recycled-pid and unreadable-argv both resolving to `orphaned`, and a dead pid never inheriting a stored `running`.
- `__tests__/session-registry-persistence.test.ts` — 4 restart scenarios across a real reopen of the DB, including crash vs clean shutdown.
- `__tests__/managed-sessions-repository.test.ts` — 6 registry tests.
- `__tests__/pty-parent-exit-hangup.test.ts` — the SIGHUP regression above.
- Idle-reaper, lifecycle-overlay, and argv-token tests in the existing suites.

One pre-existing load artifact was observed: `server-shutdown.test.ts` "releases :PORT…" failed once under full parallelism and passed 3/3 in isolation and on a full re-run.

## Security and migration considerations

Migration `010` is additive — a new table, no existing table altered, nothing backfilled. A streamer on a pre-010 database creates it empty, indistinguishable from a first run.

Every registry write is best-effort behind a null repo: if the cache DB fails to open, persistence degrades to the current in-memory behaviour rather than refusing to start agents.

The reconciler never signals a process. `orphaned` is a report, not a cleanup trigger.

No credentials, paths, or session content are added to any log or response beyond what was already emitted.

## API contract

`SessionResponse` gains `lifecycle`, `lifecycleSource`, `lifecycleUpdatedAt` — all additive and optional.
`ptyAttached` is unchanged and still means `lifecycle === "attached"`, so a client that ignores the new fields behaves exactly as before.

`contracts/*.schema.json` is deliberately **untouched**: per the coordination protocol that needs the API-contract lock first. The shape is recorded in the shared registry for mobile U4.

## Commits

- `9e828c5` — stop killing agent PTYs when the last subscriber disconnects
- `050887a` — persist a durable managed-session registry
- `392e223` — reconcile sessions left behind by previous streamer runs

## Target integration branch

`integration/missing-prs-2026-07-23` — also the base of this PR.

author: artyhoo
body:
## Summary

- The agent container runs the **consumer repository's own** hooks and pre-commit gates, but the image ships neither `jq`, `python3` nor `gh` — and those gates do not fail without them, they **SKIP**. A skipped check is indistinguishable from a passing one: the hook stays registered in `.claude/settings.json`, so any audit of the configuration reports it as active while it enforces nothing.
- `/home/node/.npm` is created **root-owned** by the `npm i -g` in the agent stage, so `npx` fails with `EACCES` for the `node` user the agent actually runs as.

## Changes

Two commits, both touching only the `agent` stage — `api`/`mcp`/`web` run no consumer gates.

**1. Install `jq`, `python3`, `gh`** (one added argument to the existing `apt-install` wrapper).

Why each is needed inside this image: `jq` parses the hook stdin payload (nearly every `PostToolUse` hook shells out to it), `python3` backs the pre-commit JSON + YAML validity checks, `gh` backs spec validation. All three are in the base image's own Debian bookworm repositories, so no external apt repository or keyring setup is required.

**2. `chown -R node:node /home/node/.npm`** (folded into the existing `install -d` line).

Without it, a consumer's pre-commit hook prints `markdownlint violations — fix before commit` on *every* commit touching `*.md`, because `npx markdownlint-cli2` cannot spawn — the rejection reason is npm cache permissions, not any lint finding. An agent that does not know the workaround is permanently blocked on noise.

**How this was found:** a mechanism-parity audit run live *inside* this image on 2026-07-23 (one dispatched task auditing its own container) reported `jq/gh/python3: MISSING`, and a deliberately violating edit produced total silence from the gate that should have caught it.

## AI Model

- [x] Claude Opus (latest) — authored the npm-cache commit, the verification runs and this description
- [x] Claude Fable (latest) — earlier analysis in the same session that produced the dependency commit

## Test Plan

- [ ] ~~Tests pass (`npm test`)~~ — **N/A**: the diff is `.docker/Dockerfile` only, no JS/TS is touched, so the workspace suite does not cover this change.
- [ ] ~~Lint passes (`npm run lint`)~~ — **N/A**: same reason.
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable) — the rationale for each package is inline in the Dockerfile, where the next reader of that `RUN` line will see it.
- [x] Manually verified the change works as expected:

The exact install line was run through the real `.docker/apt-install.sh` wrapper in a clean `node:22-slim`:

```
apt-install rc=0
jq:      jq-1.6
python3: Python 3.11.2
gh:      gh version 2.23.0 (2023-02-27 Debian 2.23.0+dfsg1-1)
git:     git version 2.39.5
gosu:    1.14
```

Then the agent image was rebuilt and the container recreated. Inside the new container:

```
jq       jq-1.6
gh       gh version 2.23.0
python3  Python 3.11.2
node     v22.23.1
--- npm cache owner ---
drwxr-xr-x 1 node node 4096 Jul 24 00:08 /home/node/.npm
```

Before the change, the same commands reported `jq: MISSING`, `gh: MISSING`, `python3: MISSING` and `drwxr-xr-x 1 root root ... /home/node/.npm`.

## Note on scope

This is an outside contribution from a downstream user of `aif-handoff`; the fix is already running locally. Happy to split the two commits, drop either one, or close this if the packages are deliberately excluded from the agent image for size reasons — in that case a documented note about the skipping gates would be just as valuable.

author: exkazuu
body:
## Summary

Pairs with WillBooster/reusable-workflows#472. wbfy now generates a `wbfy.yml` caller workflow in every WillBooster/WillBoosterLab repository, so each repository applies wbfy to itself nightly via GitHub Actions — replacing the self-host-utils fan-out that required an org-wide SSH key on a self-hosted machine.

### Generator (`packages/wbfy/src/generators/workflow.ts`)

- New `wbfy` kind in the workflows template map: nightly `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`, calling `reusable-workflows/.github/workflows/wbfy.yml@main` with the `WBFY_GH_TOKEN` and `VERDACCIO_TOKEN` secrets and `permissions: contents: read` (the reusable workflow pushes with the PAT in a separate trusted job; the job token stays read-only because wbfy runs dependency lifecycle scripts). Stale `NPM_TOKEN` / deprecated `GH_BOT_PAT` entries are dropped from existing callers.
- **Deny-list based** (`wbfyWorkflowDenyList`): every repository gets the caller except the ones where wbfy is known not to work, external-facing repositories, and forks — mirroring the exclusions in self-host-utils `scripts/process-repos.sh`. On a deny-listed repository an existing generated caller is deleted (only when the file solely calls the reusable wbfy workflow, via the conservative content check shared with the gen-pr cleanup as `jobsAllCallReusableWorkflow`).
- **Staggered schedule**: the cron slot is derived deterministically from the repository name across 16:00–17:59 UTC starts (01:00–02:59 JST), so the organization does not hit GitHub/npm/Verdaccio at one instant; with the 30-minute job timeout every run finishes by 18:29 UTC, leaving ~30 minutes of schedule-delay slack before the 19:00 UTC (04:00 JST) self-hosted Ubuntu runner reboot and well before the 20:00 UTC wbfy-merge PR opener. The schedule is re-asserted after merging with existing content so a stale slot never wins.
- **Visibility-safe**: a failed GitHub metadata lookup no longer collapses to "private" for this feature — `PackageConfig.isRepoVisibilityKnown` gates generation, so an offline/rate-limited run cannot emit a caller that would schedule a public repository onto self-hosted runners. `requestRepoInfo` now selects the owner's PAT (case-insensitively) and re-fetches complete metadata after a rename redirect.

### Secret provisioning (`packages/wbfy/src/github/secret.ts`)

- The push PAT secret is named `WBFY_GH_TOKEN` (NOT the historical `GH_BOT_PAT`, which released wbfy versions delete as deprecated during `wbfy --env`).
- WillBooster (paid org): `wbfy --env` verifies the organization secret is visible to each non-denied repository and flags shadowing repository-level copies, plus remaining assignment on deny-listed repositories.
- WillBoosterLab (free plan): `wbfy --env` uploads it per repository from the dedicated `WBFY_GH_TOKEN_FOR_WILLBOOSTERLAB` env var — a least-privilege fine-grained PAT (Contents + Workflows write only), never the org-admin bot PAT. Deny-listed repositories get the secret revoked unconditionally, before any fnox/Verdaccio validation can abort the run.
- Known accepted risk (deferred to #1077): the same least-privilege PAT value reaches every allowed repository; per-repository short-lived GitHub App tokens are the follow-up.

## Test plan

- `packages/wbfy`: full vitest suite passes (284 tests, incl. `wbfyWorkflow.test.ts` covering public/private generation, cron determinism/window, stale-cron rewrite, secret cleanup, deny-list deletion vs. custom-file preservation, unknown-visibility skip).
- tsc / oxlint / oxfmt clean.
- E2E: the generated caller was exercised against `WillBooster/minimal-promise-pool` with the reusable workflow branch (see WillBooster/reusable-workflows#472) — wbfy ran and the `wbfy` branch was force-pushed; all test artifacts were cleaned up.
- Multi-agent review (/review-fix, 6 rounds): all findings fixed except the shared-PAT blast radius, deferred to #1077; public-repo 60-day schedule disablement deferred to WillBooster/self-host-utils#47.

## Summary

Implements [ENG-47](https://linear.app/corvi-io/issue/ENG-47/build-the-triad-studio-service-fulfillment-visual-prototype) on top of merged ENG-46 and applies the bounded verifier/review fix batch.

- keeps queue and fulfillment in the existing service-desk lifecycle/source
- deduplicates exact add/remove/reassign/notes/finish retries with stable operation IDs at the memory boundary
- rejects source-clock regression before session writes and preserves the prior snapshot
- preserves allowlisted queue scenario/filter context across child-route return
- seeds deterministic sessions once per generation/session so board round-trips preserve user mutations
- canonicalizes parent and child URLs to exactly six validated technical search keys
- distinguishes missing sessions from recoverable load failures with shared Alert/retry
- handles every mutation promise with pending suppression and concise PII-free pt-BR Sonner feedback
- uses accepted SelectGroup anatomy and semantic modal-layer stacking
- expands deterministic, retry, failure, reload, responsive, keyboard/focus, and axe coverage
- aligns durable Studio docs and ENG-47 PRD/plan evidence

No API, IDP, site, persistence, browser storage, HTTP, polling, realtime, public environment variable, payment, price editing, discounts, commissions, cash, Agenda/Dashboard presentation, or unrelated Playwright infrastructure changes.

author: brettbergin
body:
Fixes the field report — which is also good news: the 0.1.4 install ladder **worked** (venv creation succeeded on the client's template for the first time), and the run advanced to pip, which then refused our wheel:

```
ERROR: Invalid wheel filename (wrong number of parts): 'sdxloop_worker'
```

## Cause
pip validates the `name-version-python-abi-platform` structure of the wheel **filename itself**. `install()` staged the wheel renamed to `/tmp/sdxloop_worker.whl`, making it uninstallable by definition. Now staged as `/tmp/<canonical-name>.whl`.

## Why tests missed it, and the fix for that
Every install test scripted the pip exec instead of running it. Added **`TestRealPipInstall`**: real venv + real pip against the real workspace wheel, through the fake sbx (hermetic via `--no-deps` + `--system-site-packages`), asserting the worker imports from the sandbox venv at the lockstep version. That test fails on the old code with pip's exact field error.

**Tests**: 256 passing, 93% coverage.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |

| [crossplane](https://crossplane.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane)) | HelmChart | patch | `2.3.3` → `2.3.4` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>crossplane/crossplane (crossplane)</summary>

### [`v2.3.4`](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/releases/tag/v2.3.4)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/compare/v2.3.3...v2.3.4)

`v2.3.4` is a patch release scoped to fixing issues reported by users of Crossplane `v2.3` and fixing security related issues in Crossplane and its dependencies.

### 🎉 Highlights

- **Fixed repeated owner updates for composed Usages ([#​7597](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7597), originally [#​7591](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7591)):** The Usage controller only checked the *first* `ownerReference` when deciding whether the `spec.by` resource already owned the Usage. A Usage created by a Composition already has the composite as its first owner, so `spec.by` ended up as a later owner and the controller issued an unnecessary update on every reconciliation — repeatedly re-triggering composition reconciliation and eventually opening the XR circuit breaker. It now checks all owner references.
- **`crossplane render` fixes ([#​7599](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7599), originally [#​7544](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7544)):** `render` no longer overwrites the input XR's UID when one is already set, and now validates observed resources before proceeding with the render.
- **Vulnerability-scannable images ([#​7574](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7574)):** Container images are now built with `buildGoModule` (replacing `gomod2nix`), so published images can be scanned by standard vulnerability tooling.
- **Dependency security updates:** Bumps `grpc` / `golang.org/x/net` / `golang.org/x/text` ([#​7618](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7618), [#​7614](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7614), [#​7615](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7615)) and the sigstore stack — `cosign` ([#​7559](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7559)), `rekor` ([#​7560](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7560)), `timestamp-authority` ([#​7570](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7570)), `sigstore-go` ([#​7583](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7583)) — to pick up upstream CVE fixes. See `## What's Changed` for the full list.

#### What's Changed

## Summary

These are just mental overhead at this point more than anything, this does increase the possibility that we accidentally end up adding an option to more places than intended, but I don't think the changes here are particularly susceptible to that _and_ I'm pretty certain we already have this bug somewhere (I'll find some by the next next breaking release).

Another option may be to split things up at the option level, and then use those as atoms for each CLI, but I'm also not sure it's worth it... I think there may be better (more automated) ways to fix the problem in the long term.

author: sfaqer
body:
## Зачем

Всё, что при построении дерева символов опирается на типы, считается **один раз** и кэшируется в дереве. Раньше конфигурационные типы регистрировались по завершении `populateContext` — то есть заведомо позже всех деревьев, — поэтому запоздавшая регистрация уже ничего не исправляла: результат оставался неверным до первой правки файла.

Ветка переносит регистрацию раньше построения деревьев во всех режимах и попутно чинит несколько давних багов, вскрывшихся по дороге.

## Что сделано

### Порядок загрузки

- **LSP** — регистрация на `WorkspaceAddedEvent` c `@Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)`: `configurationRoot` (= URI workspace) там уже известен, то есть регистрация проходит до клиентского `didOpen`. Явный порядок нужен, чтобы не ждать соседнего слушателя `OScriptLibraryIndex` — он делает полный обход дерева workspace'а (замерил на корне ERP: **~13,5 с**), а друг от друга эти слушатели не зависят.
- **CLI/MCP** (`analyze`/`format`/MCP) — там `configurationRoot` задаётся уже **после** `addWorkspace`, поэтому ранняя регистрация видит пустую конфигурацию. Добавлено событие **`ServerContextPopulatingEvent`** (AOP `@Before populateContext`) — общий для всех «голов» чокпоинт «конфигурация готова, но ни одно дерево ещё не построено».
- Платформенные типы (СП/HBK) прогреваются параллельно через `workspaceServiceExecutor`, а не голым `CompletableFuture.runAsync`: воркеры `ForkJoinPool.commonPool` в исполняемом fat-jar получают чужой `contextClassLoader`, из-за чего `ClassPathResource`-загрузка встроенных JSON-описаний падает с `FileNotFoundException`.

### Исправленные баги

- **Второй `TypeRef` на то же имя.** `registerConfigurationType` безусловно интернировал новый `CONFIGURATION`-ref, даже если имя уже занято каноническим типом (например, платформенной специализацией `ОтчетОбъект.<Имя>`). Второй ref перекрывал первый в `aliasIndex`, а member-source'ы разъезжались по двум ref'ам: `getMembers` собирает источники строго по своему ref. В итоге события и встроенные реквизиты платформенного типа становились недостижимы после того, как модуль объекта до-регистрировал свои члены (проявлялось на отчётах). Теперь resolve-or-intern — как уже делает `registerSpecialization`.
- **Отчёты и обработки не получали членов объектного типа.** `registerObjectAndRefTypes` обрабатывал только MDOType с обеими обёртками. У отчёта и обработки ссылочного типа нет, поэтому они целиком выпадали из регистрации: их реквизиты и табличные части не заводились нигде и не резолвились ни в completion, ни в hover, ни в инференсе.
- **`Ссылка` объекта справочника не была помечена read-only.** Метка `accessMode` стояла в отдельной записи с тем же именем, которую специализация `СправочникОбъект.<Имя>` не наследует, — до резолвленного члена конкретного справочника она не доходила.

## Тесты

- `ConfigurationTypesRegisteredBeforeSymbolTreesTest` — фиксирует ключевой инвариант: к моменту построения первого дерева типы уже зарегистрированы.
- `registerConfigurationTypeReusesRefAlreadyTakenByAnotherKind` / `...KeepsMembersRegisteredOnExistingRef` — одно имя → один ref, члены не теряются.
- `tryRegister_withReportChild_registersObjectTypeWithoutRefType` — отчёт получает объектную обёртку и **не** получает ссылочную.
- `catalogObjectReferenceAttributeIsReadOnlyOnSpecialization` — read-only-метка доходит до специализации.

Полный прогон тестов зелёный; каждый коммит собирается отдельно (проверено `git rebase --exec`).

## Заметки для ревью

- Коммиты разложены по смыслу, ветка перебазирована на актуальный `develop`.
- Первым коммитом идёт чистка 12 неиспользуемых импортов в `ConfigurationTypesProvider` — они остались от кода, уехавшего в `ServiceModuleEventRegistrar`, и компилятором не ловятся.
- `ServerContextPopulatedEvent` не тронут — им продолжают пользоваться остальные подписчики, изменился только слушатель `ConfigurationTypesProvider`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Configuration types are now registered earlier during workspace analysis, improving type resolution before symbol information is built.
  - Prevented duplicate type definitions by reusing existing resolved type references when names collide with platform types.
  - Corrected object/reference type wiring: unsupported wrappers are skipped, and reference wrappers are only added where applicable.
  - Report object wrappers no longer expose an unsupported reference wrapper.
  - Catalog object reference properties are now correctly marked read-only, including across specializations.
  - Improved workspace initialization flow for CLI and MCP analysis so configuration updates apply in the right order.

## #3 Participant reopen — see the prior account

Reopening a completed check-in already worked (the **"Continue this session to correct it"** button on `GroundParticipantPage` → `startSelfCorrection` → a safe new correction session; the endpoint is participant-capable). But the person **couldn't see what they'd said before** — the correction session is a fresh session and the real engine only rehydrates *that* session's turns (#73), so it was empty. Correcting blind.

### Change
- `getTranscript` returns the prior (corrected) session's turns as `priorTurns` (+ `priorSessionNumber`) when the check-in is a self-correction. Same participant → no cross-party content crosses; the HARD RULE holds and the isolation suite still passes. The original session's record is never edited.
- ChatPage renders `priorTurns` **read-only** above the live conversation, labelled *"From your earlier session N · read-only"* with *"recorded as an update, not a replacement."*

Composes with the existing reopen button (#9) and transcript rehydration (#73).

### Guard (bite-checked red→green)
`ChatPage.reopenPriorTurns.spec.tsx`: a correction-session transcript renders the prior turns, the earlier-session label, and the update-not-replacement note. Removing the rendering makes the earlier account invisible → red.

Conversation + isolation + transcript suites **142/142**; api `tsc` clean. Built on current main (`609ccda`).

author: mpge
body:
## Problem (P1 — org lockout)

`Order` and `PurchaseOrder` use `SoftDeletes`, but `generateOrderNumber`/`generatePONumber` read `MAX()` through the **default scope** (excludes trashed) while the `(organization_id, number)` **unique index counts trashed rows**.

Soft-deleting the highest-numbered order/PO of the day — the most common thing to delete — breaks **all further creation for that org that day**:
1. generator reads `MAX(non-trashed)` → returns the just-freed number,
2. insert collides with the still-present trashed row,
3. `SequenceNumberRetry` re-runs, but a fresh read *still* can't see the trashed row → regenerates the same number → after 5 attempts throws.

It only self-heals at the date rollover (or if the row is restored/force-deleted). Reproducible with "create order, delete it, create another".

## Fix

Read with `withTrashed()` in both generators so the next number is always past every existing number, trashed or not.

## Tests (TDD — red → green)

`test_order_number_generation_accounts_for_soft_deleted_orders` and `test_po_number_generation_accounts_for_soft_deleted_purchase_orders`: soft-delete the highest-numbered order/PO of the day, then create another — succeeds with a fresh number. Both red before (500 / `RuntimeException` from exhausted retries), green after.

body:
## Summary

Hardens the OMN-14951 fail-loud Infisical secret gate built in #2407 (open,
not yet merged — this PR stacks on top of its head branch,
`jonah/omn-14951-infisical-fail-loud-gate`, rather than duplicating its
machinery). Closes the two gaps a live verifier drove and reproduced:

**Gap 1 — required keys could still silently fall back.** With
`require_infisical_for_required_secrets=False` (a documented opt-out) and
`enable_convention_fallback` at its `True` default, a name in
`required_secrets` resolved via convention/env fallback instead of failing —
reintroducing exactly the silent-miss OMN-14951 exists to kill. Fixed at two
independent enforcement points so it is structurally impossible, not just
documented, regardless of any flag combination:

* `ModelSecretResolverConfig._validate_required_secrets_route_through_infisical`
  (`src/omnibase_infra/runtime/models/model_secret_resolver_config.py`) — the
  missing-mapping check is now **unconditional**. The flag previously
  short-circuited the entire validator when `False`; now it only narrows
  *which* `source_type` an explicit mapping may use (`infisical`-only vs
  any) — an explicit mapping is mandatory either way.
* `SecretResolver._get_source_spec`
  (`src/omnibase_infra/runtime/secret_resolver.py`) — the single choke point
  every resolution path (`_resolve_secret` sync/async, `get_secret_async`)
  funnels through. A name in `required_secrets` never reaches convention
  fallback, unconditionally. This holds even if the config were mutated
  post-construction (`frozen=False`) or built via `model_construct()`,
  bypassing the validator entirely.

The opt-out flag (`require_infisical_for_required_secrets`) **survives** —
it retains a legitimate use (a required key may still have an explicit
non-Infisical mapping, e.g. `source_type="file"` for a K8s secrets-volume
lane) once the leak is closed; it can no longer be used to skip declaring a
mapping at all.

**Gap 2 — missing static CI gate (OMN-14951 scope item 2/3).** Extended the
existing `scripts/check-env-reads.sh` (not a second parallel scanner) with a
name-aware check: `os.environ[...]` / `os.environ.get(...)` / `os.getenv(...)`
/ `get_secret(...)` reads of secret-ish names (`KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|
PASSWD|CREDENTIAL|CERT|PRIVATE|DSN`) in the same boundary-file set Check 1
already targets now fail unless the name is on the finite, named bootstrap
allowlist or self-declared as a `required_secrets`/`bootstrap_secrets` list
element in the same file. `tests/` and `scripts/` stay exempt (test
doubles/tooling, not a deployable's consumed env surface — consistent with
Check 1's existing exemption).

Wired as a **real** gate in this same PR:
* Pre-commit hook entry point is unchanged (`check-env-reads` already
  existed, OMN-11069) — now runs the extended script.
* **New CI workflow** `.github/workflows/check-env-reads-gate.yml` — the
  script previously had **zero CI mirror**, only the local pre-commit hook
  (verified live: no `check-env-reads` reference anywhere in `ci.yml`).
  Mirrors `receipt-honesty.yml`'s base/head SHA resolution pattern
  (pull_request + merge_group). **Not yet added to branch protection's
  required-status-check set** — flagged as a follow-up, since a code PR
  mutating live branch protection is out of scope here.

## Proof (RED before fix, GREEN after)

**Gap 1 RED proof** — ran the new tests against the pre-fix `#2407` source
(temporarily reverted via `git checkout --`, tests kept the fix), then
restored the fix and re-ran:

```
tests/unit/runtime/models/test_model_secret_resolver_config_required_secrets.py::TestRequiredSecretsGap1LeakyFlagComboRedProof::test_leaky_flag_combo_raises_naming_the_key FAILED
tests/unit/runtime/models/test_model_secret_resolver_config_required_secrets.py::TestRequiredSecretsGap1LeakyFlagComboRedProof::test_leaky_flag_combo_with_bootstrap_default_also_raises FAILED
tests/unit/runtime/models/test_model_secret_resolver_config_required_secrets.py::TestRequiredSecretsOptOutEscapeHatch::test_opt_out_does_not_waive_the_explicit_mapping_requirement FAILED
tests/unit/runtime/test_secret_resolver_required_secrets.py::TestValidateRequiredSecretsGap1ResolverChokePoint::test_convention_fallback_never_fires_for_a_required_key FAILED
  AssertionError: assert SecretStr('**********') is None
   +  where SecretStr('**********') = get_secret('payments.stripe.secret_key', required=False)
4 failed, 1 passed in 0.32s
```

That last failure is the literal live reproduction: the resolver returned
the ambient env value (`"leaked-via-convention"`, wrapped `SecretStr`)
instead of `None` for a declared-required key with no Infisical mapping.
After restoring the fix: `22 passed` (full Gap 1 test set).

**Gap 2 RED proof** — same technique against pre-fix `check-env-reads.sh`:

```
tests/unit/runtime/test_check_env_reads_gate.py::TestCheckEnvReadsSecretNameDeclarationGate::test_blocked_on_undeclared_secret_ish_name FAILED (assert 0 == 1)
tests/unit/runtime/test_check_env_reads_gate.py::TestCheckEnvReadsSecretNameDeclarationGate::test_blocked_on_undeclared_name_via_os_environ_bracket FAILED (assert 0 == 1)
tests/unit/runtime/test_check_env_reads_gate.py::TestCheckEnvReadsSecretNameDeclarationGate::test_blocked_on_undeclared_name_via_get_secret FAILED (assert 0 == 1)
3 failed, 6 passed in 1.92s
```

The pre-fix gate exits `0` (silent pass) on an undeclared
`os.environ.get("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY")` in a boundary file. After restoring
the fix: `21 passed` (full check-env-reads suite).

## Local verification

* `tests/unit/runtime/` full suite: **5190 passed, 5 skipped** (pre-existing
  skips, unrelated to this change) — no regressions.
* `uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/` / `ruff check src/ tests/` —
  clean.
* `uv run mypy` on both modified source files — clean.
* `uv run pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all hooks pass
  (including the modified `check-env-reads` hook dogfooding itself against
  this PR's own diff).
* `uv run --no-project --with pyyaml scripts/validation/validate_precommit_fail_loud.py`
  — clean (no false-green / stages-coverage regression from the new
  workflow).

## Scope / honesty notes

* No lane's `required_secrets` is populated by this PR (same as #2407) —
  mechanism only.
* Branch-protection required-status-check addition for
  `check-env-reads-gate` is **not** done here — flagged as a follow-up.
* `occ-preflight` / OCC-dependent checks are expected red per dispatch scope
  (OCC untouched, Codex lane).

body:
## Summary
- `100-move_to_utf8.sql`: the `name` column's `MODIFY` statement dropped the redundant explicit `CHARACTER SET utf8mb4` clause, keeping only `COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci`. MySQL 8 only echoes `CHARACTER SET` in `SHOW CREATE TABLE` when it was explicitly set on the column itself; the checker's expected output only shows the `COLLATE` clause, so the column-level charset must stay implicit (inherited from the table default)
- `101-avg_temperatures.sql`, `102-top_city.sql`, `103-max_state.sql`: the checker's actual `temperatures` table names its data column `value`, not `temperature` as I'd assumed — causing `Unknown column 'temperature' in 'field list'`. All three queries now reference `value`
- `README.md`: corrected the documented column name

## Test plan
- [x] `100-move_to_utf8.sql` re-run against a local MySQL-compatible server with an `id/name/score` fixture (matching the checker's actual table shape) — conversion still succeeds and `name` ends up on `utf8mb4`/`utf8mb4_unicode_ci`. Note: MariaDB doesn't track "explicitly set column attribute" the same way MySQL 8 does, so I can't get a byte-identical local repro of the exact `SHOW CREATE TABLE` string, but the statement change directly targets the reported diff (dropping the extra `CHARACTER SET utf8mb4` clause)
- [x] `101`/`102`/`103` re-run against a `temperatures` table using `value` instead of `temperature` — all three execute successfully with correct `GROUP BY`/`AVG`/`MAX`/`ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` results

author: tiltwind
body:
Why: 当意图的“意图会话”(intentSessionId,如当前这个起草对话)或“Spec 会话”(specSessionId)正有一个 turn 在执行时,意图列表对应行没有任何可见指示——用户必须逐条点开详情才能确认某条意图当前是否有 AI 正在处理,协作效率低,也容易误判为该意图已停滞。现有的 runStatus(running/dangling)只覆盖 lastWorkSessionId 且仅在 status==='in_progress' 时生效,draft/todo 状态下正被讨论/写 spec 的意图完全没有指示。

What: 为每条意图新增一个派生布尔态——“intentSessionId / specSessionId / lastWorkSessionId 三者中任一当前有 turn 在执行”——服务端在 intents 广播时复用既有的 isRunning(sessionId) 判活(与 session-registry 心跳/对账口径一致)计算得出;意图列表行据此渲染一个闪动绿点(复用 .req-run-status.running 已有的 status-pulse 动画),不受意图 status 限制。绿点与既有的 .req-status 状态徽标、.req-run-status(dev 工作会话 running/dangling 文字标签)共存,互不替代——dev 工作会话原有语义不变,新绿点是“任一关联会话此刻有 turn 在跑”的独立叠加信号。

Trade-offs / Non-goals: 不区分绿点具体来自哪个会话(意图会话/spec 会话/工作会话对用户呈现为同一个信号,不做文案区分),后续如有需要再拆分;不改变现有 dangling/idle 判定逻辑;不新增额外心跳或轮询,直接复用现有 intents 广播时机,可能有秒级刷新延迟,本次不做专门实时性优化。

Acceptance:
- [ ] shared/src/protocol.ts 的 Intent 增加派生字段(如 sessionActive: boolean),注释说明计算口径及与 runStatus 的关系
- [ ] 服务端在 intents 广播/enrich 环节,对 intentSessionId / specSessionId / lastWorkSessionId 任一 isRunning() 为真时置位该字段;单测覆盖三个会话各自单独触发、多会话同时触发、均不存在/不在跑
- [ ] IntentList.vue + intent-list-view.ts 按该字段渲染绿点,复用 status-pulse 动画,与现有 .req-status/.req-run-status 共存不冲突;draft/todo/in_progress 各状态下均验证显示正确
- [ ] pnpm allcheck 通过

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
`Terminus`/`Terminus2` run terminal-bench's `perform_task` **host-side** via `await asyncio.to_thread(_run_sync)`, which uses the event loop's *default* `ThreadPoolExecutor` (sized `min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4)`). Each concurrent trial's `_run_sync` occupies one of those threads for the trial's entire lifetime. On modest hosts (few vCPUs) with several concurrent Terminus trials, that shared pool is exhausted — which also starves the loop's own `loop.getaddrinfo` and other `run_in_executor` work (Daytona API calls, sandbox keepalives, DNS) that every concurrent trial depends on. This surfaced concretely in the internal eval-service worker (control-plane `claim`/`heartbeat` calls timing out under concurrency while CPU was idle); the same starvation is latent for any concurrent Terminus use here (e.g. local `presidio run -c N`).

Fix: run host-side Terminus on a dedicated executor so it never consumes the loop's shared default pool.

```py
# module-level, lazy, lock-guarded; PRESIDIO_TERMINUS_MAX_WORKERS (default 32)
_get_terminus_executor() -> ThreadPoolExecutor  # thread_name_prefix="terminus-agent"

# in _BaseTerminusAgent.run():
- result = await asyncio.to_thread(_run_sync)
+ result = await loop.run_in_executor(_get_terminus_executor(), _run_sync)
```

`loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()` already exists in that method; the `os.environ` save/update/restore around the call is unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced by the embedding provider dispatch refactor.

Previously, `EMBEDDING_PROVIDERS` stored direct function references. This prevented test monkeypatching from replacing provider implementations because the registry continued pointing to the original function object.

This change resolves providers dynamically at runtime, allowing monkeypatched provider functions to be used during testing while preserving existing runtime behavior.

## Changes

- Resolve embedding providers at runtime.
- Preserve existing provider dispatch behavior.
- Restore compatibility with provider monkeypatching in tests.

- `df1f` (robotsix-auto-mail)
- `8c17` (robotsix-central-deploy)
- `d396` (robotsix-mill)

## Expected behaviour

The guard exists to prevent wasteful re-implementation when a RETRY would run against an unchanged spec. It should only fire when a prior implement attempt exists for the same spec hash (retry_attempt > 0 or a recorded prior attempt fingerprint). On a first attempt there is no prior result to duplicate, so the guard must not fire.

## Fix

Gate the fingerprint check on the existence of a prior implement attempt for this ticket: only compare/enforce the spec fingerprint when at least one earlier implement attempt was recorded. First attempts always proceed.

## Verification

- Unit test: ticket with no prior implement attempt and a stored spec fingerprint (or none) proceeds to implement.
- Unit test: retry with unchanged spec fingerprint still blocks; retry with changed fingerprint proceeds.
- After deploy: resume-blocked df1f / 8c17 / d396 and confirm they enter implement instead of re-blocking.

author: dx2102
body:
## Summary

`torch.rand`, `torch.randn`, `torch.normal`, `Tensor.normal_`, and `torch.multinomial` currently drop the user-supplied `generator=` argument when routed through FlagGems. A `torch.Generator` is a per-instance RNG state (its own seed and offset). Right now FlagGems silently ignores it and sampling falls back to the default generator anyway. This PR wires `generator=` through to the underlying kernels.

The plumbing is actually already there. `philox_backend_seed_offset` in `src/flag_gems/utils/random_utils.py` uses the caller-supplied generator when given one, and falls back to the current device's default only when the argument is `None`:

```python
def philox_backend_seed_offset(increment, generator=None):
    if generator is None:
        device = torch_device_fn.current_device()
        generator = torch_device_fn.default_generators[device]
    state_copy = generator.get_state()
    ...
```

All the ops touched by this PR already end up calling this helper. They were just dropping the argument (or never accepting it) on the way in, so the `if generator is None` branch was always taken.

## Details

### 1. rand / randn have no `generator=` in the signature

`src/flag_gems/ops/rand.py` and `randn.py` do not accept the argument at all:

```python
def rand(size, *, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, pin_memory=None):
    ...
    philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset(increment)
```

Upstream `torch.rand(..., generator=g)` and `torch.randn(..., generator=g)` do accept it. Sibling ops in this repo (`randint`, `randperm`, `bernoulli`, `uniform_`) already handle it correctly.

### 2. normal.* accept `generator=` but never forward it

`normal_tensor_tensor`, `normal_tensor_float`, `normal_float_tensor`, and `normal_` all declare `generator=None` in the signature but never pass it down. `normal_` even hard-codes it to `None`:

```python
def normal_(self, mean=0, std=1, *, generator=None):
    ...
    self = normal_distribution(shape, device, generator=None, out=self)  # hard-coded
```

Signature looks right, behavior is wrong. User passes a custom generator, result silently uses the default one.

### 3. multinomial uses `gen=` instead of `generator=`

The aten schema is `multinomial(Tensor self, int num_samples, bool replacement=False, *, Generator? generator=None)`. The dispatcher passes kwonly arguments by name, and FlagGems' Python impl declares `gen=None`, so this crashes:

```
>>> torch.multinomial(probs, 2, generator=g)
TypeError: multinomial() got an unexpected keyword argument 'generator'
```

Two changes here, both about actually honoring `generator=`:

1. Rename `gen` to `generator` in the Python signature so the dispatcher's kwarg call can reach the impl at all.
2. `multinomial` has several internal code paths. One of them draws random noise via `torch.empty(...).exponential_(1.0)` without forwarding the generator, so that path always uses the default one. Forward `generator` into that `.exponential_(...)` call as well.

## Upstream API check

Checked upstream PyTorch 2.6.0 by introspection to see which factory / in-place RNG APIs actually accept `generator=`:

| API                                                                                             | accepts `generator=` |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------:|
| `torch.rand` / `randn` / `randint` / `randperm`                                                 | yes                  |
| `torch.rand_like` / `randn_like` / `randint_like`                                               | no (TypeError)       |
| `torch.normal` (all four overloads)                                                             | yes                  |
| `torch.bernoulli` / `multinomial` / `poisson`                                                   | yes                  |
| `Tensor.normal_` / `uniform_` / `bernoulli_` / `cauchy_` / `exponential_` / `geometric_` / `log_normal_` | yes           |

Which means:

* `rand`, `randn`, `normal.*`, `multinomial`: upstream supports it, FlagGems should too. Fixed here.
* `rand_like`, `randn_like`, `randint_like`: upstream explicitly rejects `generator=` (raises `TypeError`). FlagGems does not add it either, on purpose. Not part of this PR.

## Changes

Host-side glue only. No Triton kernels touched.

* `src/flag_gems/ops/rand.py`, `randn.py`: add `generator=None` to the signature and forward it to `philox_backend_seed_offset`.
* `src/flag_gems/ops/normal.py`: the four call sites now forward `generator=generator` instead of dropping it or hard-coding `None`. `normal_tensor_float` also gains a `std=1.0` default value (see note below).
* `src/flag_gems/ops/multinomial.py`: rename `gen=` to `generator=` to match the aten schema, and forward it to the internal `exponential_(...)` call in the without-replacement path.

The pattern matches how `randint.py` and `bernoulli.py` already handle `generator=`.

### Note: normal_tensor_float now defaults std to 1.0

The new generator test for `normal_tensor_float` uses the most common calling shape, `torch.normal(mean, 1.0, generator=g)` (unit-variance sampling, which is what people actually write). That shape happens to trigger a second, independent bug in FlagGems that has nothing to do with `generator=` per se; the test would otherwise crash before it could verify anything, so this PR fixes that bug too.

The second bug: aten schema is `normal.Tensor_float(Tensor mean, float std=1., *, Generator? generator=None)`. The dispatcher elides positional arguments whose value equals the schema default, so `torch.normal(mean, 1.0, generator=g)` reaches the Python impl as `args=(mean,), kwargs={'generator': g}`. The old signature `def normal_tensor_float(mean, std, *, generator=None)` cannot fill in `std` and raises `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'std'`. Adding `std=1.0` as the Python default matches the schema default and fixes it. No existing test called with `std=1.0`, which is why the bug lived undetected.

## Tests

There is currently no test that verifies `generator=` is actually honored. The existing `test_rand.py` / `test_randn.py` / `test_normal.py` only check distributional properties (value range, mean, std), so a silently-dropped `generator=` would never trigger a CI failure and this whole class of bug can regress freely. This PR adds `tests/test_rng_generator.py` to close that gap.

For every op touched, the new file asserts two things:

* Two calls with same-seeded generators produce bit-exact identical output.
* Two calls with differently-seeded generators produce different output.

The equality assertion is what catches "generator= silently dropped": in that case both calls end up on the default generator, whose offset advances between calls, so the outputs differ and the assert fires.

Local results (Nvidia CUDA, PyTorch 2.6.0):

* new tests: 7/7 pass
* existing `test_rand.py` / `test_randn.py` / `test_normal.py`: 21/21 pass, no regressions

author: trishorts
body:
Fixes #7. Documents #8 and mzLib #1109, #1110, #1111, #1112.

A biologist-persona bake-off run against the Rust binding surfaced defects and documentation gaps. They live in **mzLib's behaviour, not in any one language**, so they apply here verbatim — wording that rescues a Rust user rescues a Python user too.

## The bug — `Peptide.intensity()` could return `None` (#7)

This module documents peptide intensities as *"0.0 when missing, never None"* in three places. But `_from_wire` stored the wire value verbatim and `intensity()` only defaulted a missing **key**. The bridge routes every double through a finite check, so a NaN peptide intensity arrives as `null` and passed straight through.

**The fixture shipped in this repo triggers it.** `flashlfq_small.json` carries `"run_4": null` for `ACDEFR`:

```python
>>> peptide.intensity("run_4")
None          # documented as impossible
```

The existing test covered only `intensity("never_seen")` — the missing-key case — and used `peptides[0]`, never `peptides[1]` whose null the fixture provides.

It matters because `None` is the signal callers are told to branch on to find proteins FlashLFQ could not resolve. A peptide that also returns `None` erodes exactly that signal, and arithmetic on it raises `TypeError` on a value the type hints promise is a float.

Nulls are now resolved to `0.0` at the boundary, so the invariant holds by construction. **`ProteinGroup` is deliberately untouched** — `None` there is meaningful and hard-won.

## The documentation

| what | why |
|---|---|
| **`ModificationCensus.explain()`** | Stated a reason that is **false**. It said the excluded annotations *"have no defined chemical composition"*, but 22 of albumin's 24 are `N-linked (Glc) (glycation) lysine`, which UniProt's own `ptmlist.txt` defines with `CF C6H10O5` / `MM 162.052823`. Excluding them is still right — glycation is a labile, heterogeneous adduct and **14 of the 22 are annotated `in vitro`** — but a trap-disclosure stating a wrong reason is worse than none. It now says what actually happens, why that is usually correct, and that a census can only give you a count. mzLib#1112 |
| **`dissociation`** | ETD returns **c, zDot and y** — three series, not two. The y ions are spurious and about a third of every ETD fragment list, so `fragment_count` over-counts by that much. mzLib#1109. Also notes z• is suppressed N-terminal to proline while the complementary c ions are not. mzLib#1110 |
| **`max_threads`** | Not only a performance knob. At `-1` the FlashLFQ roll-up nondeterministically drops MBR intensities, so protein numbers vary run to run on identical inputs — unquantifiable in 5 of 6 runs, quantified in the 6th. **Pin to 1 for anything you publish.** mzLib#1111 |
| **`mbr_rescued_peptide_count`** | Now states the exact predicate. Prose and implementation diverge: 140 vs 135 on the K562 pair, the difference being peptides with both an MBR peak and a zero-intensity `MSMS` peak in the same run |
| **`total_size_bytes`** | Reports PRIDE's number, which is the **decompressed** size for some compressed files (16,448,103 reported, 5,984,662 downloaded) and is summed over an incomplete manifest |
| **`list_files`** | Returns what PRIDE's API publishes: **8** files for PXD000001 where the FTP tree holds **13**, the five omitted including the two largest (450 MB mzML, 472 MB mzXML) |
| **`protease`** | The trypsin-vs-`trypsin|P` difference on albumin is **7** peptides, not 37. The warning was right; the number was stale by 5×, and it is the kind of figure a reader quotes |

## Evidence these fixes work

The bake-off's biologist arm on the Rust binding, which carries the same wording, logged **zero external lookups** on the quant task and named the doc comment that stopped them reporting 169 peptides instead of 257 — the exact mistake a FlashLFQ user makes by reaching for `QuantifiedPeptides.tsv`. They set `max_threads=1` *because the docs warned them*.

## Tests

The census test now pins the corrected reason instead of the false one, and a new test covers the null-intensity case the fixture always had. **154 passed.**

author: iamwhatever
body:
## Problem
`redact_credentials()` correctly replaces raw credentials in the *returned text*, but the warning it appends alongside each plaintext redaction embedded the raw match verbatim:

```python
warnings.append(f"Redacted credential pattern: {matched[:20]}...")
```

`matched` is the entire matched credential substring, and `_CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` matches the secret **values** themselves (not just labels). Because each provider token has a short fixed-length prefix, the 20-char cap exposed a meaningful slice of the real secret in plaintext:

| Token class | Prefix | Raw secret chars in `matched[:20]` |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub `ghp_` | 4 | ~16 |
| Slack `xoxb-` | 5 | ~15 |
| Anthropic `sk-ant-` | 7 | ~13 |
| OpenAI `sk-proj-` / Stripe `sk_live_` | 8 | ~12 |
| DB URI `postgresql://` | 13 | start of embedded `user:pass` |

## Why it matters
The returned `warnings` list is a redaction-subsystem output that callers treat as safe to log, emit to telemetry, or surface in the UI. Leaking a 12-16 char prefix of a high-entropy API key both fingerprints exactly which secret matched and, for shorter tokens, discloses a substantial fraction of the value — defeating the purpose of the redactor for any sink that records these warnings.

## Fix (symptoms → root cause → change)
- **Symptom:** a partial plaintext secret appears in `warnings` even though the same secret is redacted in the returned text.
- **Root cause:** the warning string was built from the raw match bytes (`matched[:20]`), unlike the sibling branches in the same function — the base64 branch logs `({len(chunk)} chars)` and the bare-secret branch logs `({len(run)} chars)`. Only the plaintext branch emitted secret material, confirming this was an oversight rather than intent.
- **Change:** emit non-sensitive metadata only, mirroring the sibling branches:
  ```python
  warnings.append(f"Redacted credential pattern ({len(matched)} chars)")
  ```
  Length is not secret-bearing and is already the established convention here. A pattern-identity hint was considered but not adopted: `_CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` is a single large alternation with no named groups, so recovering "which alternative matched" would require invasively threading named groups through the whole regex for marginal benefit — length-only is the minimal, consistent fix.

## Tests
- Added `TestRedactCredentials::test_warning_does_not_leak_secret_prefix` — a parametrized regression test over the worst-case high-entropy prefixes (`ghp_`, `sk-ant-`, `sk-proj-`, `sk_live_`, `xoxb-`). It asserts neither the full secret **nor its first-20-char slice** (the old leak window) appears in any warning, while still confirming the redaction is reported with a length.
- Existing `TestRedactCredentials` suite continues to pass (67 passed locally), locking in that redaction of the returned text and warning counts are unchanged.

## Manual verification
N/A — unit coverage is sufficient; the change is a pure string-construction fix on an in-process function and the regression test exercises the exact leak vector across all affected token classes.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox (agent-sandbox)</summary>

### [`v0.5.3`](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/releases/tag/v0.5.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/compare/v0.5.2...v0.5.3)

### 🚀 Announcing Agent Sandbox v0.5.3!

We're excited to announce the release of Agent Sandbox v0.5.3! This release brings significant advancements in core stability, controller performance, and introduces a robust suite of observability and stress testing tools. Key highlights include improved controller leadership handover, enhanced resource management with informer cache optimizations. We've also made strides in operator deployment readiness and enriched our documentation and examples.

##### ⚠️ Breaking Changes / Action Required

- **Immutable `Sandbox.spec.volumeClaimTemplates` ([#​858](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/858)):** The `Sandbox.spec.volumeClaimTemplates` field is now immutable after creation (instead of previously being immutable implicitly). Attempts to add, modify, or remove this field during an update will be rejected by the API server with a validation error. This prevents potential data drift or reconciliation issues. Existing objects and no-op updates are unaffected.

##### Key Highlights

##### API & Core Enhancements

- **`safe-to-evict` Annotation Support ([#​615](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/615)):** The `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict` annotation is now exempted from restricted-domain validation in `SandboxClaim`'s `spec.additionalPodMetadata`, allowing for more flexible autoscaling behavior for claimed sandboxes.

##### Controller Performance & Stability

- **Faster Leader Election Handover ([#​1249](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1249)):** The controller manager now gracefully releases its leader-election Lease on shutdown, significantly reducing the leaderless window during rolling updates from \~15s (lease expiry) to \~0.7-1.7s. This ensures smoother controller transitions and improved availability.
- **Optimized Informer Caches ([#​1253](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1253)):** Controller performance is improved by stripping `metadata.managedFields` and unnecessary Pod spec fields from informer caches, reducing memory footprint and CPU usage. An opt-in `--cache-label-selectors` flag is introduced for server-side scoping of Pod and Service watches to sandbox-labeled objects.
- **Reduced Sandbox Status Churn ([#​1225](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1225)):** The controller now avoids writing sandbox status updates for nodeName-only changes during initial Pod scheduling, consolidating updates and reducing API server load.
- **Efficient Warm Pool Adoption ([#​1245](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1245), [#​1118](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1118)):** The SandboxClaim controller is optimized to prevent SandboxWarmPool status updates from re-enqueuing every referencing claim. Additionally, warm-pool adoption now finalizes in a single reconcile pass, improving efficiency and reducing no-op reconciles and retry loops.
- **Increased Concurrent Workers ([#​1220](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1220), [#​1221](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1221)):** The default value for `sandbox-concurrent-workers` has been increased from 1 to 100, enabling better parallel processing of Sandbox reconciles.
- **Accurate Claim Creation Metrics ([#​1114](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1114)):** Fixed a bug that caused SandboxClaim creation latency metrics to be re-recorded and skewed after suspend/resume cycles, ensuring more accurate reporting.
- **Metric Cardinality Reduction ([#​1073](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1073)):** The `warmpool_name` label has been removed from `ClaimStartupLatency` and `ClaimControllerStartupLatency` histograms to reduce metric cardinality.
- **Optimized `NameHash` Function ([#​1193](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1193)):** The internal `NameHash` function has been optimized using bit-manipulation, resulting in faster execution and reduced memory allocations.

##### Operator & Deployment Enhancements

- **OperatorHub Publication Readiness ([#​363](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/363), [#​1260](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1260)):** Significant work has been done to prepare the Agent Sandbox for Kubernetes OperatorHub publication. This includes new OLM bundle assets, versioned operator releases, sample CR files, and expanded ClusterServiceVersion (CSV) descriptions.
- **Configurable Webhook Certificates ([#​1255](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1255)):** The `agent-sandbox-controller` now supports configurable webhook certificate filenames (`--webhook-cert-name`, `--webhook-key-name`) and automatically falls back to a single `cert.pem` file if standard names are not found.

##### Documentation & Examples

- **Comprehensive SDK Documentation ([#​780](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/780)):** New, comprehensive Go and Python SDK reference documentation has been added, along with enhanced generation workflows.
- **SSH-Native Sandbox Example ([#​1185](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/1185)):** A new `containarium-ssh-sandbox` example demonstrates running Containarium's `agent-box` runtime as a Sandbox via SSH, providing a secure, token-free access method for AI agents.
- **Mutating Admission Webhook Example ([#​761](https://redirect.github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/issues/761)):** A complete example and guide for a Mutating Admission Webhook is included, showcasing how to inject nanosecond-precision timestamp annotations for accurate latency measurements.

author: sanjeetkhangura
body:
## What this changes

Three fixes from going through the app.

### Mission pages were bare

A mission with little data had almost nothing on its page. SWOT is the worst case: no patch, no description, no crew, no payloads and no links, so all you saw was a name, a date and two lines of text.

The page now shows:

- Generated mission art when there is no patch image, instead of blank space.
- A live countdown for upcoming missions.
- A quick facts row (date, flight number, outcome, rocket).
- The rocket and the launch site as cards you can click through, with real numbers on them (height, mass, success rate, mission counts, coordinates).
- "More missions on this rocket" and "More missions from this site".
- An honest line when there is no description, rather than an empty gap.

Those last two sections use the reverse relations. The schema now accepts a `limit` on `Rocket.launches`, `Launchpad.launches` and `CrewMember.launches`, so the page pulls a handful instead of all 195 Falcon 9 missions.

### Starship was labelled Retired

It has never flown in this dataset, so calling it retired is wrong. The status now uses the launch count as well as the `active` flag:

- active, so **Active**
- not active but has flown, so **Retired** (Falcon 1, five flights)
- not active and never flown, so **In development** (Starship)

### The launch sites plot was unclear

It only labelled latitude, so it was not obvious what the grid meant. It now labels longitude as well, explains both axes underneath, and anchors site names inward so Kwajalein is no longer clipped at the right edge.

## How I tested it

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (39 passing, up from 32) and `npm run build` all pass.
- New tests cover the rocket status rules, including the case that caused the bug, and the new `limit` argument on related launches.
- Checked the SWOT page, the rockets list and the sites page in the browser against the production server. Console is clean.

author: karmachoi
body:
## Summary

Two DFTB input-policy changes: MRSF-TDDFTB keeps the tuned DTCAM-TB operator as its default, and the DFTB response families become selectable at the top level.

> Note: the branch name (`feat/dftb-conventional-default`) is legacy — this PR now **keeps** DTCAM-TB as the MRSF default rather than switching to the conventional protocol.

### 1. DTCAM-TB stays the MRSF default; dftb+ is opt-in
`DFTB_MODEL_DEFAULT_MRSF` remains `"dtcam-tb"`: an un-modelled MRSF-TDDFTB run uses the tuned operator that restores the ionic-bright / covalent-dark crossing the plain protocol misses. The other open-shell DFTB routes (SF, open-shell ground) default to the conventional dftb+ protocol (LC-DFTB2, SPC=0.5). Either operator is selectable explicitly with `[dftb] model=dtcam-tb` or `model=dftb+`.

The DTCAM-TB operator vector itself is the reparametrized ref≠response fit — see the companion openqp-dftb PR (preset `openqp_dftb_apply_dtcam_tb_preset`).

### 2. Top-level `[input] method` shortcuts
Add `method=mrsf-tddftb | sf-tddftb | tddftb`. `expand_dftb_method_alias()` (run before validation) expands each to `method=dftb` plus the canonical `[dftb]/[tdhf]` type and the reference each family needs (ROKS triplet for the spin-flip families, closed-shell RHF for plain TD-DFTB).

## Verification
Validated end-to-end on butadiene (native backend):
- `method=mrsf-tddftb`, no model → `preset: dtcam-tb` (S1/S2 = 6.058/6.435 eV, restored crossing).
- `method=mrsf-tddftb`, `model=dftb+` → conventional dftb+ protocol, SPC 0.5.
- `method=sf-tddftb` → SF, dftb+.
- `method=tddftb` → closed-shell TD-DFTB (TDA).

Tests (`tests/test_dftb_model_default.py`): `test_mrsf_defaults_to_dtcam_tb`, `test_mrsf_dftb_plus_is_opt_in`, the alias+default test expecting dtcam-tb, and five `expand_dftb_method_alias` tests — 15/15 pass. SF and open-shell-ground default tests keep asserting dftb+.

author: waveai-company
body:
Fecha #43 (N4-b). Segunda peça do **corpus de pesquisa** (ADR-0030), sobre a N4-a (#42, mergeado).

## O que entra (`packages/wave-corpus`)
- **`Provenance`** — a **tétrade** (ADR-0030 / doc 31 §12): `git_commit`, `dataset_version` (id imutável do dataset), `engine_version`, `hyperparameters`. Construção **fail-closed**: sem as quatro, não persiste. `computation_id()` é a identidade **determinística** (dataset × engine × params — o commit é auditoria, não identidade).
- **`ResearchResult` + `CorpusIndex.add_result`** — persiste um resultado **só** com a tétrade completa. `artifact_by_hash` habilita a ingestão idempotente.
- **`ingest_frame` + CLI `research ingest`** — move um dataset sintético/autocaptação (ADR-0028) para o corpus (store content-addressed + índice), **idempotente por conteúdo**.
- **`LocalRemote`** — remote DVC **sempre local/descartável**; recusa nuvem/rede (autocaptação nunca é empurrada — ADR-0028). `DvcLocalRepo` embrulha o binário `dvc` (extra opcional `[dvc]`); o resto do corpus funciona sem ele (a identidade imutável já vem do hash de conteúdo).

## Aceite (testes sintéticos)
1. **`Result` sem um dos 4 campos → erro** e não persiste (`test_result_sem_tetrade_nao_persiste`).
2. **ingestão cria id imutável e é idempotente** por conteúdo (mesma sessão, 1 parquet).
3. **determinismo**: mesma entrada + `engine_version` + params → mesmo `computation_id`; muda se qualquer um mudar.
4. **remote DVC local/descartável**: `LocalRemote` recusa `s3://`, `https://`, `gdrive://`, etc.

Rodei local: **22 passed, 1 skipped** (integração `dvc` pula sem o binário — não está nas deps do CI para evitar peso/flakiness; extra `[dvc]` para operar de verdade). CLI verificada ponta a ponta (ingestão + idempotência + tétrade).

## Nota de escopo
O binário `dvc` fica em extra opcional (`.[dvc]`), fora do CI. O contrato de segurança que importa (ADR-0028) — **remote local, autocaptação nunca empurrada** — é enforçado por `LocalRemote` e testado. Wire do `dvc push` no CI, se desejado, é follow-up.

body:
## What this PR does

Removes the **Serverless** deployment mode and all Knative Serving integration from OME. Serverless was never the default (RawDeployment ships in every config) and is unused in practice; autoscaling is already served by RawDeployment + HPA/KEDA. This deletes the Knative code path, its API surface, dependencies, and docs.

73 files changed, +341 / −6003, 10 files deleted. knative.dev/serving and knative.dev/networking are dropped from go.mod; knative.dev/pkg is retained — it's used by ~40 files for apis.Condition/apis.URL/network.* and is unrelated to Serverless.
## What change

**Deleted files**

- `reconcilers/knative/ksvc_reconciler.go` — Knative Service reconciler
- `strategies/serverless_strategy.go` — Serverless ingress strategy

author: jdrumgoole
body:
## Record what step 1's extra index hop actually costs

Step 1 (#613) kept the index-entry format as `id_key`, so an IXSCAN fetch pays
`id_key → _id index → RecordId → doc`. The plan already predicted that hop and
scheduled its removal in step 2 — this records **what it costs**, so step 2 has a
before-number to beat instead of a vague "optimised away."

### Measured
A/B of `b90b5490` (step 1) vs its parent `397b03aa`, both built and run **back to
back in one detached worktree** on an idle machine (load < 2 before each leg,
`./inv compare-servers --no-mongod --reps 9`, n=10000):

| workload | parent | step 1 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **find_indexed_range** | 7.14 ms | **8.19 ms** | **+14.7%** ← the hop |
| find_all (scan) | 20.28 ms | 17.71 ms | −12.7% |
| aggregate `$group` | 12.55 ms | 10.44 ms | −16.8% |
| aggregate multistage | 17.45 ms | 15.36 ms | −12.0% |
| delete_many_half | 32.51 ms | 29.89 ms | −8.1% |
| insert | 82.07 ms | 79.55 ms | −3.1% |
| update_many_half | 49.89 ms | 51.39 ms | +3.0% (noise) |

**Noise floor ≈ ±3%**, established by the *Python* server as an untouched control in
the same runs — step 1 is Rust-only, and Python moved 0.7–2.7% between the two legs.
That is what makes +14.7% a real regression and `update_many`'s +3.0% not.

**Step 1 is net positive:** everything that walks the doc table sequentially (scan,
both aggregates, delete) got 8–17% faster because the table is now in RecordId
(insertion) order. Only the indexed-read path pays.

### What this adds to the plan
- The measured hop cost, next to the step-1 note that predicted it.
- A concrete **step-2 target**: return `find_indexed_range` to ≈7.1 ms; ≥7.6 ms means
  the hop is still being paid somewhere — plus the caveat that step 1's sequential-scan
  gains must not regress while chasing the read number.
- A note that the **published benchmark figures were deliberately not refreshed**:
  against mongod the Rust server measured 1.4×–2.6× after step 1 (was 1.5×–2.5×), but
  step 2 moves the read number again, so publish once after it lands rather than twice.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
davidallada
body:
## Problem

Dify **advanced-chat (chatflow)** apps intermittently failed on **tool-calling turns** — Home Assistant spoke *"Sorry, I could not reach the assistant right now."*

Root cause (confirmed from live HAOS logs):
```
backends/_sse.py: BackendStreamError: SSE line exceeded 65536 bytes without a terminator
```
A Dify chatflow streams verbose `node_finished` / `agent_log` frames as single SSE lines. A busy **agent** node's frame was measured at **130–145 KB** — over the reader's 64 KB per-line cap — so the reader raised and the whole turn aborted. It only bit chatflow apps whose big frame precedes the answer deltas; agent-chat apps (small frames) were unaffected, which is why it looked intermittent (~25% of tool turns in testing).

## Fix

The SSE reader now **drains an over-cap line to its terminator and skips it** instead of raising. An over-cap line is verbose node metadata the Dify adapter already discards (it only reads `message` / `message_end` frames), never a content delta — so dropping it is lossless for HA. Memory stays bounded (the cap's original purpose: stop buffering past the cap) and the stream continues to the answer.

This is a **strict improvement for every backend**: an oversized frame that previously killed the turn is now survived.

## Validation

- `just test` — full suite green (**258 passed**); `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `basedpyright` (strict) all clean.
- New/updated unit tests in `test_sse.py` (drain-and-skip, continuation, cross-chunk drain) and the three adapter oversized-line tests updated from the old "raises" contract to the new "drains, then the next frame still streams".
- **Replayed a real New Jarvis chatflow stream** (137 KB agent frame) through the fixed reader: no `BackendStreamError`, the `message` event frames and the full answer assembles.

Don't recompute runahead in the main loop if nothing is changing.

Follow-up #7237 (see last paragraph of https://github.com/cylc/cylc-flow/pull/7237#issuecomment-5054012951 )

-----
UPDATE: close #7359
   - adapt, instead of shim, tests to the new parentless spawning implementation
   - by superseding #7374 for [reasons](https://github.com/cylc/cylc-flow/pull/7374#issuecomment-5434718147) )
   - (see the [description of 7374](https://github.com/cylc/cylc-flow/pull/7374#issue-4843131885))
----

I did not think that calling `compute_runahead` once per main loop would be a significant efficiency hit in inactive workflows because the method returns early if the base point hasn't changed. So in inactive workflows it really only does this:

```python
base_point = min(self.active_tasks)
```

author: antfor7717
body:
## Problem

Production pipeline parsing still loads `pdf-parse` on the server, which is correct. However, `pdf-parse` wraps `pdfjs-dist`, and pdfjs evaluates `new DOMMatrix()` at module load. The Vercel Node runtime does not provide `DOMMatrix`, causing:

```
Failed to load external module pdf-parse-*: ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined
```

## Approach

- Remove the static `pdf-parse` import from the PDF parser module.
- Install a minimal 2D `DOMMatrix` shim before dynamically importing `pdf-parse`.
- Keep `pdf-parse` server-side only in the workflow parser path.
- Keep the existing `serverExternalPackages` config for `pdf-parse` / `pdfjs-dist`.
- Avoid adding another native runtime dependency.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec eslint src/features/estimate-extraction-pipeline/document/parse.ts`
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- Runtime smoke check: imported `parse.ts` and called `parsePdfFromUrl()` with an invalid PDF data URL; confirmed parser loaded and failed with `Invalid PDF structure`, not `DOMMatrix is not defined`.

## Notes

Per request, I did not run `pnpm build`. Final confirmation should happen in Vercel production after deployment.
