author: thediamonddealer
body:
## Summary
PR-2 of the Pressure Board rollout — the **AI news tagger** (spec §4.1). This is the "news cards light up" PR: unstructured GDELT/conflict headlines get directional asset-impact chips (Gold ↑, oil ↓) tagged by Claude against PR-1's closed asset vocabulary.

- **`scripts/tag_impacts.py`** — batches new GDELT-radar + conflict-watch items to **`claude-haiku-4-5`** via raw `urllib` (stdlib only, matching every existing collector — no new deps). Append-only + idempotent: only items not already tagged are sent; tags never flap; re-runs are no-ops.
- **`scripts/validate_impact_tags.py`** — drops any tag whose `assetId` is outside the registry, `direction` ∉ {up,down,mixed}, `confidence` ∉ {high,medium,low}, or `mechanism` is blank. Malformed model output for an item → `tagFailed` (retried next run, capped at **3 attempts** → honest `unavailable`).
- **`site/data/impact-tags.json`** — self-contained rolling **7-day** ledger (item copy + validated tags), so the week view can render from this one file. Byte-budgeted in `scripts/audit_static_site.py`.
- **UI** — GDELT News-radar cards render the tags as `tier-ai` chips (reusing PR-1's chip component: dashed border + "AI" badge, `conf-low` dimming, `href:''` so **no dead links**), additive to the existing GDELT hint tags, with honest `AI tagging pending` / `AI tagging unavailable` states and a page-level degraded note.
- **CI** — a tagger step in the hourly GDELT workflow (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from repo secrets), committing the ledger alongside the radar snapshot.

## ⚠️ Operator prerequisite (only you can do this)
Add the **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`** GitHub Actions secret (repo **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**). The tagger is **fail-open** — until the secret exists, every run/build still succeeds and news cards simply show "AI tagging pending". Cost once enabled: ~cents/day (~50–60 items, one batched Haiku call/run).

## Fail-open honesty (AGENTS.md)
A missing key, network error, non-200, or bad JSON **never crashes the run**: the tagger prints a notice, leaves items untagged (without burning per-item attempts on a whole-batch outage), writes a valid ledger, and exits 0. Verified live: a no-key run processed the real 61 GDELT+conflict items, degraded cleanly, and exited 0 with a valid ledger.

## Conscious design choices
- **Single writer:** the tagger runs only in the GDELT hourly workflow but reads *both* `gdelt-radar.json` and `conflict-watch.json`, so conflict-watch items are tagged there too — one writer of `impact-tags.json`, no cross-workflow commit race. (Spec says "the existing scheduled workflows"; this is the safe single-writer reading.)
- **Testable by injection:** `tag_pending(..., caller=...)` takes an injectable API caller so the 27 unit tests never touch the network (they cover validator enum/vocab drops, 7-day prune, retry→3-cap→`unavailable`, and good/malformed/outage model responses).
- **Empty tags are valid** — "no clear asset impact" is a stored, expected answer; those cards render no extra chips (not clutter).

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` → 242 pass + the **1 pre-existing** date-fragile `freshness-registry` test (unrelated to this PR — it fails on `main` too, tied to the clock, see PR #43 notes).
- `python scripts/audit_static_site.py` → exit 0 (ledger byte budget added). `node --check` clean on the changed page.
- Contract tests: 27 tagger unit tests; a source-string UI contract test; a workflow-contract test pinning `validate → tag → commit` order + the secret env.

## Deferred to PR-3 / PR-4
- The curated **Verified-tier** chips on the Impact Feed and the **Today/Week board** that aggregates these AI tags land in PR-3 (surfaces).
- New GDELT topics / USDA / RBA sources land in PR-4.

First-of-remaining from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-trader-pressure-board-design.md` (on the `plan/trader-pressure-board` docs branch). Depends on PR-1 (merged: asset registry + engine + chip component).

body:
## TEC-76 — Full vulnerability triage audit + dev-only-CVE policy

Closes #248 (TEC-76).

Reconciles `npm audit` against the actual **Dependabot Security tab** (the scope item the planning PAT couldn't reach — HTTP 403) and resolves the divergence.

### The divergence, explained
- Dependabot showed **16 open alerts** (incl. `runtime`-scoped `hono` ×8, `body-parser`, `brace-expansion`); local `npm audit` showed **8 dev-only / 0 prod**.
- Root cause: **the committed lockfile was stale** — it pinned older *in-range* transitives than a fresh install resolves. `npm audit` reads the freshened tree; Dependabot reads the committed lockfile. So the bulk of the alerts are *fixable by refreshing the lockfile*, not by ignoring.

### Changes
| Action | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Override** | `@hono/node-server` → `^2.0.5` (resolves 2.0.11), fixing GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9. Transitive under `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (`^1.19.9`); the vulnerable `serve-static` path is never loaded (server is **stdio-only**), so the major override is safe. Restores `npm audit --omit=dev` to **0**. |
| **Lockfile refresh** | in-range `npm update` → `hono` 4.12.31, `body-parser` 2.3.0, `brace-expansion` 5.0.8, `js-yaml` 3.15.0, `@babel/core` 7.29.7. **Fixes 13 Dependabot alerts** incl. 3 runtime-scoped ones (`brace-expansion` is reachable via `glob`→`minimatch`). No `package.json` range changes. |
| **dependabot.yml** | Widened the `vite`/`esbuild`/`tmp` ignore ranges to the **current** advisory ranges and documented the rationale. |
| **Policy** | New `.claude/rules/dependency-security.md`: the dev-only-CVE assessment policy, why the two scanners disagree, and the full reconciled triage table. Cross-linked from `SECURITY.md`. |

### Deviations from the ticket (documented in the policy)
- **"Add vitepress + mcpb lows to the ignore list" is unnecessary** — those are `npm audit` *path echoes* of the `vite`/`tmp` advisories, not independent Dependabot alerts (Dependabot keys on the root vulnerable package). Ignoring `vite`/`tmp` clears them.
- **The `jest` cluster the ticket described is already gone** (resolved in an earlier release).

### Triage outcome
- Dependabot **16 → 3**; the 3 remainders (`vite` ×2, `tmp`) are dev-only, need *major* bumps locked behind dev-tool parents, and are already in the ignore list.
- Every alert is now **fixed** or **ignored-with-rationale**; the two agree.

### Verification
- `npm audit --omit=dev` → **0** (regression guard) · full audit → 8 (all dev-only)
- `npm run typecheck` · `npm run lint` · `npm run build` → clean
- `npm test` → **659 passed** (35 suites, 21 todo)

author: uygary
body:
Fixes #9460

### Description of Change

Resolving lock order violation in the background thread inside `OggStreamer`.
The main thread locks `stopMutex` and then `prepareMutex`.
However the background thread can end up invoking `Stop()` inside the `prepareMutex` lock, attempting to lock `stopMutex` later.
Moving the `stream.FinishedAction` invocation outside the `prepareMutex` lock will resolve the issue.

We're also now skipping the `lock (stream.stopMutex)` call further down in this case, just to reduce lock contention, since it will short-circuit anyway.

author: kaihao-zhao
body:
## Overview

The alert rule list view previously fetched both Prometheus and Ruler API data to render Grafana-managed rules. This PR removes the Ruler API dependency from the list view, relying solely on `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` (Prometheus API data) for rendering and permission checks.

### Key Changes

**`GrafanaGroupLoader` simplification** — the component no longer fetches ruler group data or performs ruler/prom rule matching. It now renders directly from Prometheus response data, eliminating the `matchRules` helper and the "Creating/Deleting" operation states that depended on ruler data.

**New `GrafanaRuleListItem` component** — extracted from the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, this component renders a Grafana rule list item from a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` alone, without requiring a `RulerRuleDTO`.

**Ability hooks for `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`** — introduces `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` that derive permissions from prom rule data (folder-based access control) rather than ruler rule data. A `skipToken` sentinel allows callers to conditionally skip the hook.

**`RuleActionsButtons` and `AlertRuleMenu`** — both components now accept an optional `rule` (`RulerRuleDTO`) and fall back to prom-rule-based ability checks via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/ies` when no ruler rule is present. Ability results from both paths are OR'd together.

- `isProvisionedPromRule` added to `rules.ts` to check provenance on `PromRuleDTO`.

- `GrafanaGroupLoader` tests overhauled: `matchRules` unit tests removed, replaced with integration-style tests covering permissions and menu actions.

author: ruihang2017
body:
Closes #56.

## Summary

New `pushmr` delivery sub-mode for the deployment shape the report describes: a GitLab org whose token has the Issues API but a **403 MR API**, with a require-MR protected default branch — where PR mode (needs MR API) and direct mode (needs to push protected `main`) both fail.

## Type

- [x] `feat` (delivery sub-mode) + `fix` (a real gap between the two existing modes)

## Changes

- **`deliver-ticket.mjs`**: `--delivery pr|direct|pushmr|auto`. `auto` now probes the MR/PR API (cheap `mr list`/`pr list`); on glab, a denied MR API routes to `pushmr`. `pushmr` opens the MR over SSH via `git push -o merge_request.create/target/title/description` (no MR API), scraping the MR URL from the push's `remote:` output (spawnSync so stderr is captured on success). It stops for a human web-merge; a resume run detects the landed merge and closes/verifies via the working Issues API.
- **Verdict**: git forbids newlines in push-option values, so the MR description is single-line with `Closes #N` + pointers, and the CLEAR verdict is posted as an **issue comment** via the Issues API (durable, works while the MR API is 403). The report's multi-line `merge_request.description` isn't possible — recorded in the provenance note.
- **Fakes**: `fake-glab` gained a `FAKE_GLAB_MR_API_DENIED` 403 switch (blocks `mr *`, Issues verbs still work) + `issue note`. suite-deliver `makeRepo({pushOptionMr})` gives the bare origin `receive.advertisePushOptions` + a pre-receive hook that emits the MR URL (like GitLab).
- Docs: deliver-ticket header, snippet, README §4/§5/§7. Version → 0.6.2.

## Design notes

- `pushmr` is GitLab-only (a GitHub push cannot open a PR). GitHub with no PR API + protected main is inherently unsupported (noted in code).
- Autonomous delivery can't force a merge without the MR API, so `pushmr` always stops for a human web-merge (the one MR action that still works) and delivers on the resume run — same shape as supervised, honest about the constraint.

## Constraint check

- [x] No hardcoded secrets · MR opened via git push options, not an added `glab mr` allowlist entry
- [x] Docs / provenance updated; per-ticket stages + model/effort table unchanged

## Evidence

`node testbed/e2e/run-e2e.mjs` — **450/450 green**. New: suite-deliver P11 (auto-detect pushmr on MR-API 403; branch pushed + MR opened + URL scraped + verdict as issue comment + awaiting web-merge + issue left open; then simulated web-merge → resume delivers via Issues API).

## Objective

Replace Fireworks-first and single-key provider assumptions across Aura's canonical LLM egress, Selective Council V3, AuraFusion configuration, and the legacy-named Agent Arena patch worker.

## Routing policy

- Premium/default/reasoner/coding routes start with direct DeepSeek.
- DeepSeek premium uses `deepseek-v4-pro`; cheap/Shadow uses `deepseek-v4-flash`.
- Cheap, Shadow, and summarization routes prefer Mistral/Groq before premium lanes.
- xAI/Grok participates when `XAI_API_KEY` or the `GROK_API_KEY` alias is configured.
- Fireworks remains a late compatibility fallback rather than the primary provider.

For each registered provider, Aura now discovers and rotates:

- `FOO_API_KEY`
- `FOO_API_KEYS` as a JSON list or comma/semicolon-separated string
- numbered backups such as `FOO_API_KEY_2`
- registered aliases and environment supplements

Failed/rate-limited keys receive cooldowns. Unpinned calls fall through to the next configured provider after same-provider key exhaustion. Explicitly pinned providers rotate their own keys without silently crossing providers.

author: dhruvjain35
body:
## G0.4 — planner tiers + general AgentRun loop (fourth G0 lane)

Bring the dormant R1/R2 execution contracts to life. Before this lane, `NextAction`/`ActionType` had **zero constructors** and the AgentRun **write path was dead** (only a read in the ContextCompiler). Now one domain-agnostic **understand→act→verify→persist** loop drives a `CapabilityExecutor` over `NextAction`/`ToolResult` and records every step to a durable AgentRun.

### Design
`agent_loop.run_direct_action(user_id, *, executor, idempotency_key)` — Tier-0 (a single known op, no model):
- validates the capability is registry-live, runs the executor's **verified** tool once, and commits the run's terminal state **strictly from the ToolResult** — `verified` only when the read-back verified (never fabricated).
- `unauthorized → blocked` (resumable, not done); `verification-fail`/`provider-error → failed`.
- `planning_tier()` is the tier-selection seam (0 deterministic / 1 compact planner / 2 deep); tiers 1–2 are declared seams — nothing multi-step exists to plan until foreground/non-calendar work lands.

### Reuse, don't reimplement
`calendar_executor.CalendarMutationExecutor` builds a `NextAction` and delegates to the **already-verified** `calendar_tools.update_event`/`delete_event`. `calendar_mutation.handle()` reroutes update/delete/repair **through the loop**, but entity resolution, recompute, and the honest reply branches are **byte-identical** — so live behavior is unchanged and every mutation now leaves an auditable durable run. Create keeps its current path this lane.

### Adversarial review — 2 real regressions found + fixed pre-merge
- **HIGH**: AgentRun persistence is now **best-effort** — a run-store DB hiccup can never break, delay, or precede the verified provider write or its reply (the write already succeeded on Google). Same discipline as `calendar_schedule`'s best-effort entity record. Regression test: run store fully down → the verified action still stands.
- **MEDIUM/HIGH**: `calendar_tools` entity bookkeeping (`mark_updated`/`mark_deleted`) made best-effort, so a *post-verification* DB hiccup can't downgrade a verified write to a false "google rejected the update" reply. Regression tests via the real `FakeCalendarAdapter`.

### Harness-first
- `test_agent_loop.py` (**8**, real Postgres): verified→completed+recorded, unauthorized→blocked+resumable, verify-fail→failed, executor-raise→contained, non-live→short-circuit-without-executing, idempotency-key reuse, run-store-down safety, tier selection.
- `test_calendar_tools_bookkeeping.py` (**2**): verified write survives a bookkeeping failure.

### Verification
- Full suite: **1078 passed, 5 skipped**. Fixture-constant guard green.
- No schema change (AgentRun tables already exist from 0023). No live re-acceptance needed — Google-facing `calendar_tools` I/O is unchanged; the loop only adds orchestration + a durable run around it.

author: nevorahq
body:
macOS writes a `.DS_Store` per directory, and nine of them had been committed:

`.` · `app/` · `app/(auth)/` · `entities/` · `features/` · `features/auth/` · `features/todos/` · `lib/` · `shared/`

They carry no project meaning, and because Finder rewrites them on every browse they showed up as noise in `git status` during unrelated work and risked riding along in unrelated commits.

**Adding the pattern alone would not have helped** — `.gitignore` does not apply to files git already tracks. So the entries are removed from the index with `git rm --cached`, which leaves every file untouched on disk. This is an index change, not a deletion of anyone's local files.

The pattern matches at any depth (`.DS_Store` plus `**/.DS_Store`) so new ones in new directories stay out too.

Verified: all nine are untracked afterwards, the local files are still present, and `git status` is clean with no `.DS_Store` reappearing as untracked.

author: timoangerer-9elf26
body:
## What

On the Board and Daily views, the sticky page chrome (`data-testid="page-chrome"`, `sticky top-0`) now pins flush to the viewport top immediately when scrolling begins, instead of drifting up 16px before it locks.

## Root cause

The sticky block lived inside `<main class="px-4 py-4 sm:px-6">`, whose `py-4` = 16px top padding sat above it in the scroll flow. At rest the block was 16px below the viewport top, so `top-0` only engaged after 16px of scroll — the header travelled up 1:1 with the page for those first 16px, then pinned.

## Fix

Move the top padding off `<main>` (`py-4` → `pb-4`) and into the sticky block itself (add `pt-4`), on **both** sticky views:
- `board.html` `<main>` + the `board-panel` `page-chrome` block in `partials.html`
- `daily.html` `<main>` + the `daily-panel` `page-chrome` block in `partials.html`

The block now starts flush (no travel) and its `bg-slate-50` still covers the ~16px breathing room above the nav when pinned. Non-sticky views (Sprint, Velocity, Sprint cell) use a different `<main>` and are untouched. Regenerated `output.css` for the new `pt-4` utility.

## Verification

Acceptance-review on a running instance (dense dataset) measured `page-chrome` viewport-top at each scroll position:

| scrollY | Board | Daily |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 8 | 0 | 0 |
| 16 | 0 | 0 |
| 100 | 0 | 0 |

- `page-chrome` computed `padding-top: 16px`; nav sits 16px below viewport top at rest → ~16px slate-50 breathing room unchanged (AC 3).
- Mid-scroll screenshot confirms the full chrome pinned flush with slate-50 covering above the nav.
- Sprint/Velocity/Sprint-cell render unchanged (still `px-6 py-12`, not in diff) (AC 4).
- `make check` green; `git diff --exit-code -- internal/web/assets/output.css` clean/committed.

Closes #166

author: totoday
body:
## What

Comment-only fix in two panels. Both said the shared mobile header height is `h-14 / 56px`. The app sets a **15px root font** (`web/src/index.css:124`), so `h-14` = 3.5rem = **52.5px**, not 56px.

- `web/src/components/ServerPanel.tsx:99`
- `web/src/components/UsagePanel.tsx:817`

The class is right and the shared-height invariant is right; only the pixel gloss was wrong, and it read as authoritative for anyone matching a height against it.

## Why phrase it this way

The replacement states the derivation instead of just swapping the number:

```
{/* Mobile full-screen pages share the home header height (h-14 = 3.5rem,
    which is 52.5px at the app's 15px root, not 56px);
    the desktop modal keeps its compact h-10 chrome. */}
```

The original rot came from assuming a 16px root. Naming the dependency is what stops the next reader repeating it. The surviving `56px` is the deliberate corrective clause.

## Verification

- Checked the invariant still holds before touching the line — `h-14` is genuinely the shared header height in `AgentHeader.tsx:67`, `MobileTopBar.tsx:65`, `MobileNavScreen.tsx:125`, `TeamSwitcher.tsx:61`, `Sidebar.tsx:317`, `kb/index.tsx:367`.
- Read the 15px root from `index.css:124` firsthand rather than carrying it from notes.
- `git diff --stat` = 2 files, 4 insertions / 2 deletions; **every changed line sits inside a `{/* */}` JSX comment**, so there is no runtime or render surface.
- `npx tsc -b --force` → exit 0.
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/components` → 3 files / 9 tests passed.

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary

- refuse `beltmap-manifest` output paths that resolve to an image included in the generated manifest
- perform the collision check before creating directories or writing output
- add regressions for the destructive collision and the normal non-colliding path

## Root cause

`beltmap.cli.manifest.main()` generated the manifest and then unconditionally wrote JSON to `--output`. When that path was also one of the discovered input images, the command first hashed the image and then replaced it with JSON while still returning success. The resulting manifest described bytes that no longer existed, and the source image was destroyed.

## Impact

Manifest generation now fails clearly without modifying the input when `--output` aliases an input image. Normal JSON outputs beside or outside the image directory are unchanged.

## Validation

- added `tests/test_cli_manifest.py`
- verified the collision path raises before writing and preserves the original bytes
- verified a non-colliding output is written and contains the input image record

author: marc0246
body:
I removed the trait because:
- It was used to bound generics for absolutely ginormous functions such as `AutoCommandBufferBuilder::validate_pipeline_descriptor_sets` and `AutoCommandBufferBuilder::add_descriptor_sets_resources`. This is bad because it's unnecessary codegen duplication, impacting compile times and binary sizes.
- We can solve the same issue with an enum, which doesn't have the codegen issues.
- The user doesn't have to import the trait to use a method as basic as `layout` (could be solved without removing the trait).

I merged the different `bind_pipeline_*` `RecordingCommandBuffer` methods because:
- Vulkan only has a single `vkCmdBindPipeline` too, so you don't have to remember the quirky vulkano name.
- It's less typing for the user.
- It reduces vulkano-internal duplication.

Changelog:
```md
### Breaking changes
Changes to pipelines:
- The `Pipeline` trait was replaced by a `Pipeline` enum.

Changes to command buffers:
- `RecordingCommandBuffer` now only has the single `bind_pipeline` method for binding pipelines.
```

author: zelko2k1
body:
## Problem
Beim Anlegen eines Benutzers mit einer **bereits vergebenen E-Mail** lehnt PocketBase mit `400 · validation_not_unique · „Value must be unique."` ab. Die App fing aber **jeden** Speicherfehler ab und zeigte nur das generische **„Änderung konnte nicht gespeichert werden."** — die eigentliche Ursache blieb verborgen. Da die Eindeutigkeitsprüfung vor der Rolle greift, kam der Fehler bei **jeder Rolle**.

Typischer Auslöser: Man legt einen neuen Spieler an und will ihn mit einem **bestehenden** Benutzer verknüpfen, gibt beim Anlegen aber dessen E-Mail ein → Kollision, aber ohne erkennbaren Grund.

## Fix
1. **Inline-Erkennung im Benutzer-Dialog** (`UserModal`): Gehört die eingegebene E-Mail bereits einem anderen Konto, wird **Speichern gesperrt** und ein klarer Hinweis gezeigt — inkl. Anleitung, dass man zum Verknüpfen eines Spielers das **bestehende Konto bearbeiten** soll (unter „Mit Spieler verknüpfen"), statt ein neues anzulegen. Verhindert den verwirrenden Reinlauf komplett.
2. **Konkrete Fehlermeldung** als Sicherheitsnetz (`store`): `persist()` nimmt optional einen Fehler-Mapper; `accountSaveError()` übersetzt den PB-Unique-Fehler in **„Diese E-Mail wird bereits von einem anderen Konto verwendet."** — robust gegen die beiden SDK-Fehlerformen (`e.response.data` / `e.data.data`). Greift für **Create und Update**.
3. **i18n** de/en.

## Tests
- Volle Suite **261/261** grün, `tsc`/Build sauber, ESLint 0 Fehler.
- Lokal gegen PocketBase verifiziert:
  - PB-SDK-Fehlerform geprüft → `accountSaveError` erkennt die Kollision zuverlässig.
  - UI (Playwright, de-DE): bestehende E-Mail → Hinweis sichtbar **und** Speichern ausgegraut; freie E-Mail → Hinweis weg, Speichern aktiv. Screenshot im Test.

## Hinweis
Unabhängig von PR #19 (Import-Konflikt-Dialog), separater Branch von `main`.

author: intrinsicd
body:
## Summary

StructSplat shipped a `docs-sync` skill and a "docs updated in the same commit" definition-of-done, but had **no executable verification harness** — no docs↔code checker, no `verify.sh`, no CI, no registered pytest markers, and no central RNG seeding (across 100+ test files). This ports rtgs's engineering-discipline spine (**DOCS-003**), adapted to StructSplat's flat module layout and the NumPy/torch import split.

This is the **StructSplat half of a bidirectional infra transfer** with rtgs; the rtgs half (structure-tensor/WSE init, pooled row lifecycle, checkpoint policy, mask containment — all opt-in, tested) merged in intrinsicD/realtime-gs#13.

## What's in the spine

- **`scripts/docs_sync.py`** — torch-free, AST-based docs↔code checker: required docs exist, every skill is listed in `CLAUDE.md`, CLI subcommands + aliases are documented in README, every `init.STRATEGIES` entry is documented, `CLAUDE.md` path tokens resolve, and every `src/structsplat` module has a docstring. Exit 0 clean / 1 on drift.
- **`scripts/verify.sh`** — one CPU-only entry point: `ruff check` + `pytest -m "not slow and not integration"` + `docs_sync`.
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — autouse RNG seeding (NumPy always; torch only when importable, so a NumPy-only run never imports torch — preserves core invariant 1), and auto-marks the environment/evidence-coupled modules `integration`.
- **`pyproject.toml`** — registers `cuda`/`slow`/`integration` markers with `--strict-markers`; pins ruff lint to a correctness baseline (see below).
- **`tests/test_docs_sync.py`** — asserts the checker stays clean.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — mirrors `verify.sh` on CPU (installs `.[dev,benchmark]`).
- **`README.md`** — documents the previously-undocumented `feedforward` strategy (drift the new checker surfaced).

## Two scoping decisions worth a reviewer's eye

**Lint baseline.** structsplat's `[tool.ruff]` pinned no `select`, so it silently inherited ruff 0.16's broad default ruleset — the tree carries **~1147 pre-existing style findings** (unsorted imports, blind-excepts, loop-var captures, …). Cleaning those is a repo-wide job, not this spine. I pinned an explicit **correctness baseline the whole tree already passes**: `select = ["E9", "F"]` (syntax errors + pyflakes: undefined names, unused imports). This also makes CI deterministic against ruff's shifting defaults. Broader style/import families and `ruff format --check` are deferred to a tracked DOCS-003 ratchet follow-up.

**Integration marker.** ~416 tests (the `ssp2e`/`ssp2v`/`ssp2f` actual-coder suites + evidence assays) need committed `results/` bundles (gitignored, absent from a fresh clone / CI runner), a Landlock-capable kernel, or a thread-pinned worker env. `conftest.py` auto-marks those modules `integration`; the default gate runs the portable subset. Run `-m integration` in a provisioned environment.

## Test plan / verification (local, CPU)

- `ruff check src tests scripts benchmarks` → **0 errors**
- `pytest -m "not slow and not integration"` → **1448 passed, 32 skipped, 416 deselected**
- `python scripts/docs_sync.py` → **OK**
- Full `./scripts/verify.sh` → green

Branch is rebased onto current `main` (picks up the FIT-023 work).

## Follow-up (not this PR)

Stage the style-lint ratchet: `ruff check --fix` the ~774 auto-fixable, triage the rest (B023 loop-var capture / BLE001 blind-except may be real), then widen the pinned `select` — and separately adopt `ruff format`.

author: tamnd2005
body:
## Bối cảnh

`AuthService.register()` hiện tại chặn cứng **mọi** email đã tồn tại trong `core.users` (`existsByEmailIgnoreCase`), kể cả khi tài khoản đó chưa từng xác thực email (`emailVerified = false`). Hệ quả: user đăng ký xong, bỏ dở không nhập OTP → email bị "kẹt" vĩnh viễn, không đăng ký lại được, cũng không xác thực được (OTP cũ đã hết hạn) — bug **Account Stagnation**.

## Thay đổi (BR-101 — Register-Overwrite Strategy)

Thay điều kiện kiểm tra 1 nhánh (`exists?`) bằng 3 nhánh theo đúng thứ tự:

| Trường hợp | Điều kiện | Hành vi |
|---|---|---|
| **TH1** | Email tồn tại + đã xác thực | Từ chối, `409 Conflict` |
| **TH2** | Email tồn tại + **chưa** xác thực | Ghi đè password/displayName, sinh OTP mới, gửi lại email |
| **TH3** | Email chưa tồn tại | Tạo mới như luồng hiện có |

TH2 và TH3 trả về **cùng một** `AuthResponse` (`201`), không có field nào phân biệt 2 trường hợp — tránh rò rỉ trạng thái hệ thống ("email này từng đăng ký chưa").

## File thay đổi

- **`AuthService.java`** — refactor `register()` thành 3 nhánh, tách `overwriteUnverifiedUser()` / `createNewUser()`, thêm rate-limit 24h (`enforceOtpDailyLimit`)
- **`UserRepository.java`** — thêm `findByEmailIgnoreCaseForUpdate()` (pessimistic lock) chống race condition khi 2 request ghi đè cùng email cùng lúc
- **`EmailOtpTokenRepository.java`** — thêm `countByUserIdAndCreatedAtAfter` + `findFirstByUserIdAndCreatedAtAfterOrderByCreatedAtAsc` để đếm/tính rate-limit sliding window 24h (BR-100), tái sử dụng cho cả TH2 và TH3
- **`ErrorCode.java`** — thêm `EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (409, TH1) và `OTP_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED` (429, vượt 5 lần/24h)

## Không đổi (theo đúng chốt kỹ thuật)

- Không sửa `AuthResponse`, `RegisterRequest`, `AuthController` — request/response contract giữ nguyên
- Không gửi email cảnh báo khi bị ghi đè — chỉ 1 email OTP mới duy nhất
- Không đổi cooldown 60s / logic `resend-otp` hiện có

## Test plan

- [x] Build Maven thành công, không lỗi/warning
- [x] Test tay qua Swagger: TH3 (email mới) → `201`
- [x] TH2 (đăng ký lại email chưa verify với data khác) → `201`, cùng `id`, đã ghi đè `displayName`/password
- [x] TH1 (đăng ký lại email đã verify) → `409` đúng message
- [x] Rate limit: gọi lần thứ 6 trong 24h → `429` đúng `dailyLimit`/`retryAfterSeconds`
- [ ] Full flow `verify-otp` bằng email thật (đã test local, không ảnh hưởng server thật)

author: wenbinhou
body:
## Summary

Extends the workspace API surface and improves debuggability of the core HTTP client. Adds a `workspace get` command (by id or by `custom_id`), fixes the `workspace list --name` filter that was silently ignored by the server, and emits redacted request/response trace logs so `-vvv` runs can be inspected without leaking credentials.

## Changes

- **`crates/core/src/api/workspaces/get.rs`**: New `get_workspace` and `get_workspace_by_custom_id` functions calling `GET /api/v3/workspaces/{id}` (with optional `?by_custom_id=true`); path segments are percent-encoded via a narrow `AsciiSet` so unusual ids cannot corrupt the URL. Unit tests cover typical ids, structural characters, and stray `%`.
- **`crates/core/src/api/workspaces/list.rs`**: Rename `ListWorkspacesParams.name` to `name_fuzzy` and send the query parameter as `name_fuzzy` to match the server contract (the previous `name` param was silently ignored).
- **`crates/core/src/api/workspaces/mod.rs`**: Register the new `get` module and re-export `get_workspace` / `get_workspace_by_custom_id`.
- **`crates/core/src/client.rs`**: Emit `tracing::trace!` events for outbound GET/POST requests (method, final URL with query, headers, POST body) and responses (status, url, body); redact the `Authorization` header via `mask_auth_value` (`Bearer ******<last4>`, fully masked when the secret is 4 chars or fewer). Unit tests cover the masking helper, header redaction (including non-UTF-8 values), body extraction, and a TRACE subscriber test that hits a closed loopback port to force macro-argument evaluation.
- **`crates/cli/src/commands/workspace.rs`**: Add the `workspace get <ID> [--by-custom-id]` subcommand; rename the `List` field to `name_fuzzy` while keeping the user-facing flag as `--name` for continuity.
- **`crates/cli/tests/workspace/live.rs`**: Live end-to-end test that creates a workspace and reads it back via both `ws get <id>` and `ws get <custom_id> --by-custom-id`.
- **`crates/cli/tests/workspace/offline.rs`**: Offline test that `workspace get` fails cleanly when there is no login.
- **`crates/core/tests/live_workspaces.rs`**: Update the list call to `name_fuzzy` and add a live test covering `get_workspace`, `get_workspace_by_custom_id`, and the 404-style error path for an unknown id.
- **`crates/core/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`**: Add `percent-encoding` (runtime) and `tracing-subscriber` (dev) dependencies used by the new path encoding and trace tests.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` (offline + live with `MEMORYLAKE_API_KEY` set)
- [ ] Manual: `memorylake workspace list --name <partial>` returns only fuzzy-matching workspaces (previously ignored)
- [ ] Manual: `memorylake workspace get <ws-id>` returns the workspace
- [ ] Manual: `memorylake workspace get <custom_id> --by-custom-id` returns the same workspace
- [ ] Manual: `memorylake -vvv workspace list` emits TRACE request/response logs with the `Authorization` header rendered as `Bearer ******<last4>`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the central API client (logging may include full response bodies at TRACE) and changes the list filter query param from `name` to `name_fuzzy` for library callers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`workspace get`** (and `ws get`) to fetch one workspace by server id or, with **`--by-custom-id`**, by caller `custom_id`. The core client calls `GET /api/v3/workspaces/{id}` with selective path percent-encoding so unusual ids cannot break the URL.
> 
> The shared HTTP client now emits **trace-level** request/response logs (method, URL, headers with **redacted `Authorization`**, POST body, response status/body). List workspaces is aligned with the API by sending the **`name_fuzzy`** query param; the CLI still exposes **`--name`** for the fuzzy name filter.
> 
> Live and offline tests cover get without login and get-by-id/custom_id flows.
>

author: nazehs
body:
## Context

Logs from the backend, worker, Batch jobs and Lambdas are hard to tell apart in OpenSearch. `EXECUTION_CONTEXT` was already set in Terraform, but it never made it into the logs as a field.

This adds an `execution_context` field to every log line so OpenSearch can filter to one runtime.

## Changes proposed in this pull request

- Each runtime now binds `execution_context` on its logger: `backend`, `worker`, `batch`, `lambda`.
- `refresh_context()` wipes custom fields, and the web, worker and Lambda paths refresh on every request/job/invocation. So the field is re-bound after each refresh (via a new `refresh_logger_context()` helper on the backend). Batch never refreshes, so it's set once at bootstrap.
- Terraform sets a distinct `EXECUTION_CONTEXT` per runtime (backend and worker were both `ecs` before).

The frontend ECS task still uses `ecs`. It's an Astro/Node service that doesn't use the shared logger, so I left it alone.

## Guidance to review

- Main thing to check is the refresh-survival behaviour: `refresh_logger_context()` in `backend/logging_context.py` and its two call sites. Covered by tests in `test_middleware.py` and `test_rq_context.py`.
- Values only take effect in deployed environments; everything defaults to `local` locally.

## Things to check

- [x] `EXECUTION_CONTEXT` is set per-runtime in Terraform (`ecs.tf`, `batch.tf`, `lambda.tf`); no new local `.env` var is needed since it defaults to `local`.

body:
## Problem
`CommandLine.get_version()` used `/lifecycle/ak version` as its primary command. Two problems:

1. **It fails outright in the rock.** `/lifecycle/ak` shells out to `python`, which isn't on the default exec `PATH`, so the call returns `python: command not found` (exit 127). Every version fetch logged a warning and fell through to the fallback. *(Verified live on the `authentik` model.)*
2. **Even when it runs, it reports the wrong version.** `/lifecycle/ak version` dispatches to Django's `manage version` command, which prints the **Django framework** version (`5.2.15`), not Authentik's (`2026.5.3`).

Adding `service_context=WORKLOAD_SERVICE` (so the primary succeeds) would therefore make the charm report Django's version — a regression. `juju status` currently shows the correct `2026.5.3` only because the primary fails and the import-based fallback runs.

## Fix
Drop the broken `/lifecycle/ak version` primary and use `from authentik import VERSION` as the sole method, via the absolute venv interpreter (`/ak-root/.venv/bin/python`) so it doesn't depend on the service `PATH`/context. This is exactly what the **worker** charm already does, and it returns the correct Authentik version.

## Evidence (live `authentik` model, `authentik-server/0`)
```
raw  /lifecycle/ak version                      -> python: command not found (exit 127)
pebble --context  /lifecycle/ak version          -> 5.2.15    (Django's `manage version`)
python -c 'import django; print(version)'        -> 5.2.15
python -c 'from authentik import VERSION; ...'    -> 2026.5.3  (correct)
```

## Tests
Updated `test_get_version_success` for the new command; removed the obsolete two-tier fallback test. `tox -e lint` clean, `tox -e unit` **158 passed**.

author: support371
body:
## Current engineering checkpoint

Exact head: `99c8e852f9f2f1dd1f8c9f7edd4798e5cd1e8d14`

Adds a distributed request-admission boundary in front of every Cloudflare Worker route without changing trading behavior, exchange integrations, D1 business data, R2 objects, Guardian controls, cron responsibilities, or any live capability.

## Security problem addressed

The existing application limiter performs a read-then-write against D1 and allows requests through when D1 fails. In addition, routes handled by the outer agent/v2 wrappers can return before the existing limiter executes.

## Changes

- add a thin outer Worker entrypoint that evaluates admission before all routes, including `/agent/*`, `/v2/*`, and delegated application routes
- add a dedicated `request_admission_counters` D1 table so the new boundary and legacy inner limiter do not double-count one bucket
- use one conditional SQLite UPSERT with `RETURNING count` for atomic per-IP/per-minute enforcement
- stop writing once a bucket reaches its configured limit
- fail closed with a generic HTTP 503 when D1, the schema, or count evidence is unavailable
- return bounded no-store HTTP 429 responses when the limit is reached
- preserve allowed-origin CORS behavior without reflecting unapproved origins
- purge expired admission buckets from the existing scheduled-event path without changing the four current cron jobs
- place the additive schema in the separate paper-Worker migration namespace so it cannot consume the next live-candidate migration number
- add focused Node tests for migration replay, real SQLite atomicity, allowed/limited/unavailable outcomes, configuration bounds, unknown-client handling, error minimization, CORS, and cleanup

## Verified evidence

- local Node 22 strip-only test reproduction passes after replacing unsupported test-only constructor parameter-property syntax
- paper migration replay succeeds twice against an in-memory SQLite database
- the real conditional UPSERT returns counts 1 and 2, then returns no row at the configured limit while the persisted count remains 2
- exact-head Worker TypeScript, live-foundation tests, root contracts, provider tests/typecheck, paper safety, certification safety, recovery/accounting controls, transfer-disabled tests, dry-run bundles, and frontend build are successful in the visible CircleCI status set
- exact-head Vercel preview is READY; architecture typecheck, operator frontend safety, optimized Vite build, and frontend performance budget passed
- no unresolved review threads are present

The GitHub combined-status response is capped, so the full backend test/audit context must still be independently confirmed before this draft can be marked ready.

## Migration/deployment gate

Paper migration `worker/migrations/paper/003_request_admission_counters.sql` **must be applied to the paper Worker D1 database before any deployment using the new entrypoint**. Deploying the entrypoint first would intentionally return HTTP 503 for all requests because the boundary is fail-closed.

No remote migration or Worker deployment was performed.

## Safety invariants

- `TRADING_MODE=paper` unchanged
- `EXCHANGE_MODE=paper` unchanged
- `NETWORK=testnet` unchanged
- `ALLOW_MAINNET=false` unchanged
- live trading, provider mutation, real funds, transfers, deposits, and withdrawals remain disabled
- scheduled business logic is delegated unchanged
- no credentials, secrets, private identifiers, or external provider write paths are added

## Remaining gates

- independently confirm the exact-head backend test/audit and aggregate release-gate terminal results
- independently review migration-before-deployment ordering
- apply the migration only to an isolated/non-live certification database first and perform non-destructive 200/429/503 smoke checks
- do not apply the production D1 migration, deploy the Worker, merge, enable mainnet, connect execution credentials, or move funds without a separate exact-head release authorization

author: kishiguro
body:
## Summary

design/134 **Phase 2** — the branching uplink classifier. One PDU session, one UE IP, **two anchors**: the intermediate UPF steers uplink for a configured destination prefix to a second PSA (local breakout) while everything else keeps taking the default N9 path to the original anchor.

- **One filter type, not two.** `FlowFilter` became all-optional (`protocol`/`ports`/`dst`, absent ⇒ matches anything) with `transport()` / `to_prefix()` constructors. A QoS rule and a branch rule encode into the same `SdfFilter` string, so a separate ULCL type would have meant a second flow-description dialect. `dst` matches destination only (directional — that's what a ULCL *is*); `ports` still match either endpoint.
- **`transport_key` → `packet_key`** now returns the destination and handles **both IP families** (it was IPv4-only, so v6 GBR flows had silently never classified since design/131 shipped v6 sessions).
- **Egress is a per-packet decision.** `Session.branches: Vec<(FlowFilter, Egress)>`, first match wins, falling back to `Session.uplink`. A branch's egress is a plain `Egress`, so **local breakout falls out for free** — `ToN6` on a branch leaves traffic at the classifier instead of tunnelling to the anchor.
- **PFCP:** `branch_create_ies` emits a classifier PDR (id `400+`, precedence 40 — above the per-flow QoS PDRs at 50) bound to its own FAR; `parse_branches` reads them back. The per-flow QoS parser is unaffected (it requires a `qer_id`, which a branch PDR lacks).
- **Both anchors return downlink to the same classifier N9 ingress** — the classifier holds the gNB tunnel, so one return path serves any number of anchors; no second downlink ingress needed.
- **Topology config: `UserPlane { anchor, intermediate, breakout }`** with `single`/`chained`/`with_breakout`, replacing `connect`'s positional list — a stepping stone to Phase 3. A breakout without an intermediate UPF is refused (the classifier *is* the intermediate node). Config: `RADIAN_SMF_PSA2_N4` + `RADIAN_SMF_ULCL_PREFIX`, required together.
- **`far_id` fix (the queued 1b item), live after all.** `handle_n4` took the *first* Update FAR with forwarding params; it now selects by `far_id == DOWNLINK_FAR_ID`. Six pfcp tests were passing FAR id `1` for the downlink FAR — harmless while the id was ignored, wrong the moment it wasn't — corrected to the id the SMF actually sends, with a regression test.

**Known limitation (design/134 §4):** AN release parks both anchors, but the breakout one DROPs rather than buffers — only the default anchor carries the URRs that turn a buffered packet into a Downlink Data Report and hence a page. Downlink arriving on the breakout DN for an idle UE is lost rather than paged for.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p pfcp` — 24 pass (prefix matching incl. non-byte-aligned and v6, flow-description round-trip with every component absent/present, `packet_key` on both families, the `far_id` regression).
- `cargo test -p n6` — 18 pass (a classifier steers the branch prefix to a second anchor while the default egress is unchanged — and still anti-spoofs; a branch that breaks out to local N6).
- `cargo test -p nf-smf` — 14 pass (**three** in-process UPFs: one session, two anchors, walking create → branch installed → activate → AN release parking both → re-activation → release).
- `cargo build --workspace` clean; clippy clean.
- Full `cargo test -p bdd` = **33 scenarios / 369 steps GREEN and unchanged** — the classifier is opt-in and the `far_id` fix left the single-UPF path behaving identically.

author: ahmedelemey
body:
## What & why

The admin dashboard (`docs_business/admin-dashboard/`) was a fully-simulated prototype — every action showed a toast against hardcoded arrays. This PR connects the **Users**, **Vendors**, and **Categories** tabs to the real xStoreEcommerce backend (the "Users" and "Categories" folders of the Admin Dashboard Postman collection), behind a login gate.

## New API layer (`app.js`)
- `apiFetch()` — sends the static Basic license key on every request plus, once signed in, the per-user JWT as `X-Auth-Token` (not `Bearer`); parses the `{items,totalCount,page,pageSize,totalPages}` envelope; supports `FormData`/multipart; surfaces server error bodies; on `401` clears the token and re-shows login.
- **Login gate** — `POST /api/auth/login {phoneNumber,password,rememberMe}` stores the JWT in `localStorage`; dashboard gated behind it, with sign-out from the sidebar and an "advanced: change API server" override.

## Tabs wired
| Tab | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Users | `GET /api/users?role=CONSUMER` (search, pagination, states, profile drawer) |
| Vendors | `GET /api/users?role=VENDOR` (server-side status filter) · `PUT /api/users/{id}/approve` · `PUT /api/users/{id}/reject` |
| Categories | `GET /api/categories` · `POST`/`PUT /api/categories` (multipart + image) · `PUT /api/categories/{id}/status` · `DELETE /api/categories/{id}` |

## Notes for reviewers
- Async views stay synchronous builders (render a loading shell); data loads in a post-render `AFTER[view]` hook. Server-driven tab groups use `data-remote` so the generic `onChip` client-filter defers to a reload.
- Removed now-dead simulated code (`CUSTOMERS`, `userDrawer`, the `CATS.push` add-form); `CATS` kept because the overview chart still uses it.
- Regenerated the inlined single-file copy `src/xstore_admin_dashboard.html` from the three `src/` files.
- **Field mappings** (`mapUser`/`mapVendor`/`mapCategory`) are tolerant to key aliases since exact `/api/users` response keys weren't confirmed against live data.

## Verified
End-to-end against a local mock returning the exact envelope: login, user/vendor lists, server-side status filter, approve (`PUT …/approve → 200`), and full category CRUD (status toggle, multipart edit, delete). Create-category multipart confirmed via curl (browser file-picker isn't automatable).

## Known follow-ups (tracked separately)
- **CORS**: the hosted backend must allow the dashboard origin for live browser calls (otherwise a clean "network error" is shown).
- **`vendorStatus` codes**: only `0`=Pending is confirmed; `1/2/3` (Active/Rejected/Suspended) are documented assumptions to verify against the C# enum.

author: trinhkhanh15
body:
Three related changes, all following from Vietnamese being the primary audience rather than a translation target.

## 1. Folder structure

Student sections were sitting loose at the top of `components/` while teacher sections already had their own folder, so it wasn't obvious which page a file belonged to.

```
components/student/   ChatPreview, CoreEngine, Differentiation, Experience,
                      Footer, Hero, LandingPage, Philosophy, Progress,
                      StudyBuddy, TeacherCopilot
components/teacher/   Hero, Pain, How, Report, Trust, Difference, School,
                      Footer, LandingPage      (Teacher prefix dropped)
components/shared/    TopBar, PilotForm, FooterBar, AudienceSwitch, Reveal, LogoMark
```

`content/landing.ts` → `content/student.ts` to mirror `content/teacher.ts`, and the types both need (`Locale`, `PilotFormCopy`) move to `content/shared.ts` — teacher content no longer reaches through the student file to get them. `LandingCopy`/`landingCopy`/`LandingLocale` renamed to `StudentCopy`/`studentCopy`/`Locale` to match.

Git detected almost everything as renames, so the diff is mostly path changes.

## 2. Vietnamese student copy

It read like what it was — a translation of the English, carrying English sentence shapes and untranslated terms (`soft intervention`, `insight`, `momentum`, `prompt`). Now written as Vietnamese.

Two substantive fixes beyond phrasing:
- **Consistent reader.** The old copy drifted between addressing the student (`bạn`) and addressing a parent about their child (`con bạn`). It now speaks to the student throughout, matching the peer-not-teacher positioning.
- **The Done/Friend wordplay stays** (it's the brand name) but is phrased as something a person would say, rather than glossed like a dictionary entry.

English copy is untouched — the two locales now read differently while making the same promises. The P-D-E-O section is also left alone, having been written in Vietnamese to begin with.

One nav label changed: the student page's `Giáo viên` → `Báo cáo`. It pointed at an in-page section while the audience switch's `Giáo viên` points at the teacher page — same word, two destinations. Flagged on the previous PR; this resolves it.

## 3. Default routing

`/` now redirects by `Accept-Language`. Only a browser that ranks English above Vietnamese lands on `/en`; everything else — including an absent, unknown, or unparseable header — gets `/vi`.

**Worth a look:** making Vietnamese the default exposed that `<html lang>` was hard-coded to `"en"` for every page, which would have flipped the same bug onto the majority of visitors instead of fixing it. Reading the path at request time would have cost static rendering on all four pages, so the locales get their own route groups and root layouts (`app/(vi)/`, `app/(en)/`) instead. Each serves the correct `lang` and its own default metadata, and every page stays prerendered. This is why `app/layout.tsx` disappears from the diff.

## Verified

- `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass; all four pages still `○ (Static)`, middleware registered.
- Redirect matrix on `/`: no header → `/vi`; `vi-VN,vi;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` → `/vi`; `en-US,en;q=0.9` → `/en`; `en-GB,en;q=0.9,vi;q=0.8` → `/en`; `en;q=0.7,vi;q=0.9` → `/vi` (q-values respected); `fr-FR` / `ja,ko` / garbage → `/vi`.
- `<html lang>` correct on all four: `/vi` and `/vi/giao-vien` → `vi`, `/en` and `/en/teachers` → `en`.
- Cross-links intact after the move: language switch stays on the current audience's page, audience switch stays in the current language.
- Pilot form still posts `audience: "student"` from the student page with the new Vietnamese success message — verified with `fetch` intercepted, no real email sent.

## What

Continues the incremental decomposition of `Renderer3D.ts` to isolate scene-specific logic inside scene renderers. This batch covers Slices 14–29, each a self-contained behavior change validated independently with build + unit + e2e tests.

## Changes by slice

| Slice | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 14 | Renamed `isNatureParrot` → `isProfiledParrot`; routing driven by scene hook `getParrotProfileNames`, not `flags.isNature` |
| 15 | Extracted profiled-parrot reconcile block into focused helpers (`getBoidCountsBySpecies`, `getParrotProfileCounts`, etc.); introduced `PARROT_SPECIES` / `NEUTRAL_PARROT_PROFILE` constants |
| 16 | Replaced separate hawk/unicorn predator update methods with a `PredatorKind` loop |
| 17 | Unified predator reconcile with kind loop; added `getPredatorCountsByKind`, `getPredatorInstanceKey`, `resetPredatorOrientationCaches` |
| 18 | Removed `isFishTail` from `BoidMotionStyleFlags` — fishtank tail motion is now fully scene-renderer-local |
| 19 | Moved `getStyleFlags(style)` to shared `createStyleFlags(style)` in `createSceneRendererHooks.ts` |
| 20 | Added shared `isPredatorKind(kind)` type guard; replaced manual array-includes cast in gallery framing |
| 21 | Extracted predator render-flag helpers (`createPredatorRenderFlags`, `resolvePredatorRenderFlagsForKind`, `NON_DRAGON_PREDATOR_RENDER_FLAGS`) to shared hooks |
| 22 | Removed unused `StyleFlags` param from `updatePredatorInstanceSets` |
| 23 | Consolidated `unicornDisplayQuats`/`sharkDisplayQuats` into single `clampedUprightDisplayQuats` record keyed by upright style |
| 24 | Extracted `createPredatorInstanceKey(...)` into shared hooks utility |
| 25 | Replaced remaining direct parrot/profile string literals with `PARROT_SPECIES`/`NEUTRAL_PARROT_PROFILE` constants |
| 26 | Threaded `sceneRenderer` explicitly through predator update internals; removed `PredatorUpdateContext` wrapper |
| 27 | Added `getActiveSceneRenderer()` helper; eliminated repeated `getSceneRenderer(params.visualStyle)` call sites |
| 28 | Added `getProfileNamesForSpecies(species, sceneRenderer, flags)` helper; removed duplicated profile-name lookups |
| 29 | Added `isProfiledSpecies(species)`; generalized `getParrotProfileCounts` → `getProfileCountsForSpecies` |

## Impact

- **`Renderer3D.ts`**: ~820 lines removed from the pre-refactor baseline; now at 2,877 lines
- **Coupling metric** (substring occurrences of `nature|fish|bird|unicorn|shark` in `Renderer3D.ts`): reduced from ~635 → 412 since the start of this branch
- No behavioral changes — all scene rendering outcomes are identical

## Tests

All 57 unit tests + 5 e2e playwright tests pass on every slice.

author: accuser
body:
Two presentation fixes to the print manuscript. **No manuscript text changes** — `template.typ` plus a uniform one-token correction across the chapter tables.

## 1. Language chips on code listings
Now that `.bynk` and `.ts` blocks both highlight (via the syntax grammar in #898), they look similar, and the descriptive captions describe *intent*, not language — so nothing tells the reader which is which. Each `code-listing` now carries a small language chip at the top-right of its caption row:

- **Bynk** listings — a purple chip (the book's accent colour: "ours").
- **TypeScript** listings — a neutral grey chip (the reference language).
- Tree/`text` listings get no chip.

The colour difference is legible peripherally, before you even read the label, while the chip stays subtle enough not to compete with the caption.

## 2. Fix the table header rule
The tables' `stroke` function used `(x, y) => if y == 1 { (bottom: …) }`, which draws the accent rule **under the first data row**, not under the header. Typst's stroke function is per-cell, so `bottom` on **row 0** is the header underline — verified with a controlled test. Corrected to `y == 0` across all **13 tables in 8 chapters**.

## Reviewer notes
- **Manuscript builds** (`./scripts/build-book.sh`); snippet gate unaffected (no snippet changes).
- Chip specifics are easy to tune if you'd prefer a different label form (`.ts`/`.bynk` or `TS`/`BYNK`) or a TS-blue instead of grey — say the word and I'll adjust.
- Two small follow-ups still open from the presentation work: a `.tmTheme` to put the accent palette *inside* code blocks, and chipping the handful of inline (un-captioned) fenced snippets for full consistency.
- Pre-existing untracked `design/` WIP was intentionally left out.

author: luctc-47
body:
…navigateur

Symptome : un etudiant verifie recevait « Erreur API 403 » en publiant une prestation. Preuve en production, meme requete, meme jeton :
  - sans en-tete Origin (appels hors navigateur)         -> 201
  - avec Origin: https://kametud.com (comme le navigateur) -> 403 "Invalid CORS request"

Le catalogue declarait sa propre politique CORS (WebConfig + CorsProperties) limitee a http://localhost:3000 et http://localhost:5173. En production, le navigateur envoie un en-tete Origin sur les requetes mutantes (POST/PUT/PATCH/ DELETE), meme en meme-origine ; le service, dont le host interne differe, la voit comme cross-origin et, l'origine kametud.com n'etant pas autorisee, la rejette avec 403 "Invalid CORS request" (les 20 octets pris a tort pour une fabrication du service worker). Les requetes GET, sans en-tete Origin, et les appels hors navigateur passaient, d'ou le diagnostic trompeur.

Le CORS est deja gere une seule fois par l'api-gateway (globalcors, origine ${PUBLIC_SITE_URL}). Les autres services metier (business, payment, support) n'ont aucune politique propre et deleguent au gateway ; identity et request utilisent @CrossOrigin. Le catalogue etait le seul a imposer une politique locale erronee. On la supprime pour qu'il delegue au gateway comme ses pairs.

Le site et l'API partageant la meme origine, aucune en-tete CORS n'est meme requise cote navigateur : il suffit que le service cesse de rejeter.

catalog-service : 20 tests, aucun echec.

author: tktonny
body:
DB proved the exchange succeeded (ticket consumed, active credential minted), yet the mirror stayed on the pairing screen. Root cause: after exchange the mirror calls `GET /devices/:id/configuration` → `authorizedDevice()` did `findOne({deviceId, status:'active'})` with **no patient filter**. A device paired to multiple patients/tenants over time had several active assignments, so it could return a different patient's assignment → `principal.patientId !== assignment.patientId` → **403** → mirror's config fetch threw → fell back to pairing on every retry.

Fixes: (1) `authorizedDevice` matches the assignment bound to the credential's own patient; (2) claim retires **all** active assignments for the device (across tenants), so it never holds more than one. Backend-only — a paired mirror recovers on next boot, no re-pair/reinstall.

body:
Défaut trouvé en mesurant la découvrabilité des promotions.

## Le bug

#125 a fait respecter l'expiration au **prix** (`computePriceForItem` → `effective`) et au **prix barré** (`showStrikePrice`), mais le badge **« PROMO »** de la tuile POS lisait encore le booléen **brut** `p.promotion`.

Résultat : une promo **périmée** affichait toujours le badge rouge « PROMO » — alors que le prix était déjà redevenu normal et le prix barré avait disparu. Un badge qui ment.

## Le fix

Logique extraite en helper pur exporté `promoBadgeVisible(promotion, promotionEnd, clientType, now)` = `isPromotionActive(...) && clientType === 'retail'`.

## Vérification

`priceGapLevel.test.ts` **+5 cas** : promo active → badge, **expirée → pas de badge**, client gros → pas de badge (tarif de gros, pas la promo détail), pas de promo → rien, sans date de fin → badge. **Sabotage vérifié** : booléen brut réintroduit → seul le cas expiré rougit.

`tsc` 0 · **487** tests front (+5) · lint **202 inchangé**.

## Contexte

C'est le préalable de correctness au chantier **découvrabilité des promotions** (feu vert donné) : avant de rendre un badge promo plus visible en Stock, il doit d'abord être **honnête**. La suite (surfacer les promos dans la liste Stock + les rendre atteignables hors mode édition) vient dans une PR séparée.

author: jschmidt-icinga
body:
This replaces the C-style random number generation (`rand()` and `rand_r()`) used in three places in our code with the C++ equivalent. It also protects access to the generators with mutexes.

### Reasoning

In the case of `Utility::Random()` this primarily had poor entropy because it was seeded with the timestamp at the time of initialization. While this was already thread-safe on Linux, since the seed was stored in a tread_local pointer, that could potentially lead to problems with compiler optimizations in conjunction with boost coroutine suspension points, which we've faced numerous issues with in the past and I'm very wary of by now.

And on Windows it used the same non-thread-safe `rand()` function as the other examples below. This PR gets rid of the OS-specific preprocessor branches and uses the same standard functions everywhere, which still might be inferior on Windows, but much less so than before.

In the case of the DSL-facing `MathRandom()` and `Checkable::Start()` this had outright concurrent access to non-thread-safe global state via the `rand()` function, which technically is a data-race and undefined behavior, even though it didn't seem to affect us much in practice (but who knows).

I also adjusted the prior `std::mt19937` usage in `test/utils.cpp` to use the same mutex-guarded static generator pattern for consistency, even though this wasn't facing any of the issues above.

### Caveats

- `std::uniform_real_distribution` is a half-open range, meaning in the cases where we want it to return values from 0 to 1 it will never actually return 1.0. Shouldn't matter in practice, but if we want to replicate the exact behavior as before, we can always fall back to generating integer and divide them by the max value.
- `std::mt19937` can be seeded with more than one 32bit value for full entropy using `std::seed_seq`. Or alternatively we could use `boost::mt19937` instead which can be passed the `random_device` directly so it can take as much entropy as it needs. But both of those options would IMHO over-complicate things, clutter initialization and be a bit slower, so I left it at *good enough*, which is still much much better than what we had before. If a reviewer explicitly requests either option, I'm happy to add it.

author: geodro
body:
Pointing PhpStorm at `~/.local/share/lerd/bin/pg_dump` to export an external database was rejected with "Path to executable is wrong", even though the export itself would have worked.

JetBrains validates a client executable by running it with `--version` and reading the output back. With no host on the command line the shim prepends `-h lerd-<service>` so a bare `pg_dump mydb` lands on the local database, so what actually ran was `pg_dump -h lerd-postgres --version`. The postgres tools only answer `--version` and `--help` as their very first argument, so that exited non-zero with nothing on stdout and the IDE refused the path. `pg_restore` and `pg_dumpall` behaved the same way, `psql` happened to tolerate it, which is why connecting worked while exporting did not.

A leading `--version`, `-V`, `--help` or `-?` is now recognised as a probe and forwarded exactly as given, with no local-target default in front of it. The check reads the arguments rather than the tool name, so it holds for every shim a service exposes, present and future.

A probe also no longer starts the service behind the tool when its image is already there. Printing a version string never needed a database to be up, and an IDE runs that check every time the dialog opens.

Closes #1128

author: eric4545
body:
## Summary

When `aggregate_step_rollbacks` is enabled, inline rollback blocks collapse to jump-links pointing at folded entries in the Rollback Plan. However, those links used hand-authored `<a id>` anchors, which sanitizers like GitHub rewrite to `user-content-*` prefixes with no clean `#slug` alias — breaking the links in preview renderers.

This change makes Markdown jump-links resolve by targeting **real heading slugs** instead of raw anchors. The folded rollback entries now render as semantic headings (`### Rollback for "<step>"`) whose slug equals the link's anchor, ensuring links jump in all renderers. Confluence wiki and ADF continue using native anchor macros (which already work).

## Key Changes

- **New helper `stepRollbackHeadingText(step)`** in `src/lib/anchor.ts`: returns the semantic heading text `Rollback for "<step>"` used in both the inline jump-link label AND the target heading, so readers searching the phrase find the link and destination together.

- **Refactored `stepRollbackAnchor(step)`** to derive the anchor by slugifying `stepRollbackHeadingText`, guaranteeing the anchor always equals the slug a Markdown renderer generates from the heading.

- **Multi-env Markdown** (`src/manuals/generator.ts`):
  - Split `globalRollbackSteps` into explicit plan steps (table rows) and folded per-step entries (headings + mini env-tables).
  - Folded entries render as `### Rollback for "<step>"` headings with environment tables below, deduped by anchor so siblings share one heading.
  - Removed all `<a id>` anchors — the heading slug IS the jump target.

- **Single-env Markdown** (`src/manuals/generator.ts`):
  - Added `headingOverride` parameter to `renderRollbackStepSingleEnv` to render folded entries under their semantic heading instead of a numbered `Rollback Step N` label.
  - Dedup folded headings by anchor; explicit plan steps keep numbered headings.

- **Confluence wiki & ADF** (`src/cli/commands/generate.ts`, `src/manuals/adf-generator.ts`):
  - Updated jump-link labels to use `stepRollbackHeadingText` for semantic consistency.
  - Anchor macros continue using the same `stepRollbackAnchor` id.

- **Updated `EffectiveRollbackStep`** in `src/lib/global-rollback.ts` to carry both `sourceAnchor` and `sourceHeading`, set by `buildGlobalRollback` so target renderers don't re-derive the heading.

- **Tests** (`tests/manuals/aggregated-global-rollback.test.ts`):
  - Added `assertLinksResolveToHeadings` helper to verify every inline `](#slug)` link has a matching heading slug and no raw `<a id>` anchors remain.
  - Updated assertions to expect semantic heading text (`Rollback for "Deploy app"`) instead of numeric labels.
  - Added single-env production variant test to ensure link resolution across all environments.

## Notable Details

- The anchor id is now **derived from the heading text** (`slugify(stepRollbackHeadingText(step))`), not from `step.id` or `step.name` directly. This ensures the Markdown link's `#anchor` always matches the renderer's own heading slug.
- Heading text is kept **emoji-free and punctuation-light** so `slugify` matches the renderer's slug derivation.
- The heading text uses **raw `step.name`** (not variable-resolved) to match how the provenance label is built in `buildGlobalRollback`, keeping the anchor resolution-independent.
- Folded entries are **deduped by anchor** so multiple rollback entries from the same source step share one heading, with additional entries labeled by their action name beneath it.
- Documentation updated in `.claude/rules/manuals.md` and `README.md` to explain the renderer-safe heading approach and why it's necessary for sanitized previews

## Summary

Every employee currently has equal write access to this system, but there's no record of who did what — who deleted an invoice, who added a new catalog item, who changed a user's role. This adds a lightweight, append-friendly audit ledger visible only to ADMIN accounts.

- New `AuditLog` model (`prisma/schema.prisma`) + a `lib/audit.ts` helper (`writeAuditLog`, `diffChanges`, `actorFromSession`) that's best-effort — a logging failure never breaks the request it's describing.
- `writeAuditLog()` is wired into create/update/delete for:
  - Customer invoices and supplier invoices (create, update, delete)
  - Products — including items auto-created from invoice line descriptions via `lib/product-catalog.ts`'s `syncProductCatalog` (this is literally "who created an item number")

- `sales@lacuevitafurniture.com` is already promoted to `ADMIN` via `lib/auth.ts`'s `BUILT_IN_ADMINS` set, so that account can see the ledger without further changes — no changes needed there.
- The `AuditLog` table's `CREATE TABLE` is also added to `lib/init-db.ts`'s idempotent bootstrap, matching the pattern already used for every other table there (e.g. `Estimate`/`EstimateItem`) — that file is what actually provisions a fresh production database, not `prisma db push` alone.

author: kniknak
body:
## What & why

Increment 2 of feed personalization: a **measurable, CI-gated eval harness** for ranking quality. Ranking relevance is a product claim (PLAN §1, §4), so it gets a golden set + metrics + a threshold gate rather than a "feels smarter" argument. All new code lives under `evals/` plus one `package.json` script — no app code, `src/lib/*`, or `rss.ts` touched, and no new runtime deps.

Contents:
- **`evals/dataset.json`** — 30 authored (not scraped), license-clean `FeedItem`s across 6 distinct topic clusters (AI/ML, web platform, security, hardware, dev tools, product) + 5 interest profiles with **graded relevance** (`2` highly relevant / `1` related / `0` off-topic). Topics are discriminating, and each profile hides one semantically-relevant item that shares no topic words — the lexical ranker misses it, leaving deliberate headroom for the Inc 3 embedding ranker to prove lift.
- **`evals/metrics.ts`** — pure `precisionAtK`, `recallAtK`, `ndcgAtK`, `mrr` over a ranked id list + relevance map. Colocated `evals/metrics.test.ts` pins them to hand-computed numbers (e.g. a known nDCG = 0.9502344).
- **`evals/eval.test.ts`** — loads the dataset, runs `lexicalRanker` over every profile, logs a per-profile + aggregate (ranker × metric) table, and asserts thresholds → the CI regression gate. The `RANKERS` list is the single place Inc 3 adds its row.
- **`package.json`** — `"eval": "vitest run evals/"`.

## Measured lexical baseline (aggregate over 5 profiles)

| ranker  | P@3  | R@5  | nDCG@5 | MRR  |
|---------|------|------|--------|------|
| lexical | 1.000 | 0.833 | 0.922 | 1.000 |

Gate thresholds sit just below: `precision@3 ≥ 0.66` (the US-2 AC-2.4 product bar), `recall@5 ≥ 0.80`, `nDCG@5 ≥ 0.90`, `MRR ≥ 0.95` — green now, red on a real regression. Non-vacuity check: a deliberately reversed ranker scores P@3 0.067 / nDCG@5 0.036 / MRR 0.135, far below the gate.

## AC covered

- **US-2 AC-2.4** — relevance bar on the golden set: `precision@3 ≥ 0.66`, `nDCG@5 ≥ baseline` (locked here).
- Lays the measuring stick for **US-3 AC-3.6** (semantic beats lexical) — Inc 3 registers `embeddingRanker` in the same `RANKERS` list and its comparison row prints automatically.

## How to verify

```
npm ci
npm run eval        # prints the table, asserts thresholds, exits non-zero on a drop
npx tsc -b          # app build stays clean (evals/ is test-time only, excluded by include: ["src"])
npx vitest run      # full suite: metrics + personalize + summarizer + eval = 23 tests green
```

## Notes

- Stacks on **Inc 1** (`feat/personalize/foundation`) — imports its `lexicalRanker` / `personalize` seam, unmodified.
- **Inc 3** will add the on-device embeddings ranker and its comparison row to this same harness to prove the nDCG lift that justifies the model dependency.

author: anuragramdasan
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes **5 critical production bugs** identified by automated analysis of the codebase. All bugs were present in `main`; 7 earlier fix PRs (#3–#9) were all created from stale SHAs and conflict with each other — this PR supersedes all of them with a single clean, atomic commit.

---

## Bug 1 — `getUserByEmail` swallows ALL errors (auth.ts)

**Severity: Critical** — silent data corruption under any DB instability.

**Root cause:** The custom Prisma adapter override wrapped `originalGetUserByEmail` in a blanket `catch` that returned `null` for every exception. The comment said "allow account linking for P2002 unique constraint" but the code caught everything — DB timeouts, connection failures, schema mismatches, network errors.

**Impact:** Any transient DB error during sign-in caused NextAuth to believe the user didn't exist and proceed to `createUser`, generating a duplicate user record and a fresh orphaned team. On reconnect the user would have two accounts.

**Fix:** Inspect `error.code`; only swallow `P2002` (Prisma unique constraint violation). All other errors are rethrown so they surface to the caller normally.

---

## Bug 2a — Seat limit check sets a flag but never blocks sign-in (auth.ts)

**Severity: Critical** — billing/seat enforcement completely bypassed.

**Root cause:** In the `signIn` callback, `userSeatAllowed = false` was set when the team was over its seat limit, but execution continued unconditionally past that point. The membership was upserted with `isActive: false`, but `return true` was always reached — granting the over-limit user a fully valid session.

**Impact:** Any number of users could join a team regardless of their subscription's `userLimit`. Seat-based billing was completely unenforced.

**Fix:** Return `'/auth/error?error=SeatLimitExceeded'` immediately when `canAdd.allowed` is false. Returning a string from NextAuth's `signIn` callback is the correct pattern for a redirect-on-deny.

---

## Bug 2b — `session` callback missing `else` branch for teamless users (auth.ts)

**Severity: High** — onboarding flow unreachable for a class of users.

**Root cause:** After computing `defaultTeam`, the `if (defaultTeam) { ... }` block set all session team fields. But there was no `else` branch, so `session.user.noTeamAccess` was never set when a user had zero active memberships.

**Impact:** A user whose only membership was deleted or deactivated would receive a session object with no team fields and no signal that they lacked access. The UI had no way to detect this state and redirect them to an onboarding or error page.

**Fix:** Add `else { session.user.noTeamAccess = true }` so the client can branch on this flag.

---

## Bug 3 — Failed link-processing jobs leave records stuck in PROCESSING forever (link-processor.ts)

**Severity: High** — phantom stuck jobs accumulate, blocking retries and polluting dashboards.

**Root cause:** The `catch` block in `processLink` called `trackProcessingMetrics` and rethrew the error, but never updated the `processedLink` record's status. Any job that failed mid-flight would leave a row with `processingStatus = 'PROCESSING'` in the database indefinitely.

**Impact:** Stuck records pile up in the dashboard. Retry logic that skips `PROCESSING` records would permanently skip these jobs. The only resolution was manual DB intervention.

**Fix:** Before rethrowing, update the record to `processingStatus = 'FAILED'` with `errorMessage` set to the error's message. The DB update is wrapped in its own try/catch so a secondary DB failure doesn't suppress the original error.

---

## Bug 4 — Empty OpenAI short-text response falls through to a second paid API call (content-extractor.ts)

**Severity: Medium** — unnecessary cost doubling on OpenAI empty responses.

**Root cause:** `summarizeForAudio` has two paths: a short-text path (`words.length <= maxWords`) and a long-text path. In the short-text path, if `response.choices[0]?.message?.content?.trim()` was falsy (empty string or null), the `if (summary) return summary` guard silently fell through to the long-text path below, triggering a second `openai.chat.completions.create` call.

**Impact:** Every OpenAI empty response on short content caused a duplicate paid API call. This also means the long-text prompt (designed for large content) was applied to already-short text, producing worse output.

**Fix:** After the short-text `if (summary) return summary`, throw `new Error('OpenAI returned empty summary for short text content')` immediately. This surfaces the problem instead of masking it with an expensive fallback.

---

## Bug 5 — `updateSubscriptionFromStripe` always hardcodes a 30-day period end (subscription-utils.ts)

**Severity: High** — subscription expiry dates are always wrong for non-monthly plans.

**Root cause:** `updateSubscriptionFromStripe` had no `currentPeriodEnd` parameter. Both the `update` and `create` branches of the upsert unconditionally wrote `new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)`, ignoring whatever Stripe reported for the actual billing period end.

**Impact:** Annual plan subscribers saw a 30-day expiry. After each renewal, the period end reset to 30 days from the webhook arrival time instead of the actual next renewal date. Any UI that gates access on `currentPeriodEnd` would prematurely lock annual subscribers.

**Fix:** Add an optional `currentPeriodEnd?: Date` parameter. The upsert uses `currentPeriodEnd ?? new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)` — the 30-day fallback is preserved for callers that don't yet pass the Stripe value, maintaining full backward compatibility.

Summary

Legalize FP16-to-BF16 casts in the Torch-to-TOSA conversion.

The TOSA reference model rejects a direct cast from FP16 to BF16. This change widens FP16 values to FP32 before narrowing them to BF16. Every FP16 value is represented exactly in FP32, so the intermediate widening does not lose information.

The reference backend now provides the BF16 compiler runtime conversion helpers needed to execute the resulting casts during end-to-end testing.

author: willeastcott
body:
### What's Changed

Fixes gsplat entities in the Editor viewport rendering a stale set of splats. Repro: add 2 PLY files, create an entity for each — only the first one created renders. Toggling makes it stranger: disable both → nothing renders; enable A → appears; enable B → doesn't appear; disable A → **stays visible**; disable B → A disappears. The launch page is unaffected.

**Root cause:** `ViewportApplication` replaces the engine tick with an on-demand loop that never fired the app-level `framerender` event. Unified gsplat rendering (the engine default) drives all of its streaming from that event via `GSplatComponentSystem` → `GSplatDirector.updateStreaming()`, which advances the per-frame stream token and runs `GSplatWorld.update()` — the only place reconciled placement changes become a new world state. With the token frozen, each `GSplatManager` runs its streaming pass exactly once (the bootstrap on the render path when the manager is created) and then no-ops forever, so the viewport keeps drawing whatever world state existed after the first splat. Removing *all* placements takes a different path (the director destroys the manager), which is why "disable both" goes black and re-enabling a single splat works again — matching every step of the repro.

Changes:

- `viewport-application.ts`: the custom tick now fires `framerender` every frame (even when not redrawing, matching the engine's own tick, so octree LOD streaming also progresses while the viewport is idle).
- `viewport.ts`: hook the gsplat system's `frame:request` event to a viewport render — the engine's documented mechanism for on-demand rendering apps — so newly streamed data (new world state, streamed LOD, pending sort results) triggers a redraw. Complements the existing `gsplat:sorted` hook.

**Verification:** standalone harness replicating the editor tick against engine main, running the exact repro sequence and asserting on `renderer._gsplatCount` (splats actually drawn; A = 152,746 splats, B = 90,854):

| step | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| create A | 152,746 ✅ | 152,746 ✅ |
| create B | 152,746 ❌ (B missing) | 243,600 ✅ |
| disable both | 0 ✅ | 0 ✅ |
| enable A | 152,746 ✅ | 152,746 ✅ |
| enable B | 152,746 ❌ | 243,600 ✅ |
| disable A | 152,746 ❌ (A still drawn) | 90,854 ✅ |
| disable B | 0 ✅ | 0 ✅ |
