author: vreabernardo
body:
Closes #216.

`checkAccessBatch` gains an opt-in `adaptiveConcurrency: true` mode backed by a small `AdaptiveConcurrencyController` (`src/access/adaptiveConcurrency.ts`). The effective in-flight limit starts at the `concurrency` value, halves on every 429/5xx (floored at 1), and grows back by one after every `currentLimit` consecutive successes, capped at the starting value. Non-throttling failures (4xx input errors, network errors) don't shrink the limit since they say nothing about backend capacity. Workers park in `acquire()` when the shrunk limit is below the current in-flight count, so no busy-waiting.

Default static concurrency path is byte-for-byte untouched; the adaptive branch only runs when the flag is set.

Verification (watched):
- New `tests/adaptiveConcurrency.test.ts`, 11/11 pass: AIMD math unit tests (halving, floor, additive recovery, streak reset, acquire parking) plus integration tests where a mocked backend starts 429ing mid-batch (observed concurrency after the first failure stays <= 2) and recovers once errors stop.
- Full suite: 250 failed / 766 passed vs clean main 250 failed / 755 passed. The +11 are exactly the new tests; failure list diffed identical to main (all pre-existing).

author: maciejpirog
body:
## TLDR

- add `--config git+URL` to load rules directly from a git repo
- add `--skip-invalid-configs` flag to skip `yaml` files that do not contain rules
- update the `validate` subcommand to warn if no validation is run (i.e., when all rules come from remote repos)

## Summary

Adds the ability to point `--config` at a **remote git repository of rules** in the `--experimental` (osemgrep) frontend, plus a companion flag to tolerate non-rule YAML files that such repositories inevitably contain.

```
opengrep scan --experimental --config git+https://github.com/org/rules
opengrep scan --experimental --config git+https://github.com/org/rules#v1.2.0
opengrep scan --experimental --config git+ssh://git@github.com/org/private-rules
opengrep scan --experimental --skip-invalid-configs --config git+https://github.com/org/rules
```

The repo is shallow-cloned into a temp dir and then loaded exactly like a local directory of rules.

## Motivation

Previously `--config` accepted a local file, a local directory, a single HTTP(S) URL (a *single* downloadable rule file), and registry/app shortcuts (`p/`, `r/`, `s/`, `auto`, ...). There was no way to consume a whole remote repository of rules — a common way teams share and version their rulesets. A bare `https://github.com/org/rules` URL was treated as a single-file download and simply failed.

## What's included

### 1. `git+<url>` config source

- New `Git of git_config` variant in `Rules_config.t`, parsed from a `git+` prefix. An optional `#<ref>` fragment pins a branch or tag (e.g. `...#v1.2.0`).
  - The `#`-fragment syntax is used (rather than a pip-style `@ref`) because `#` cannot appear in a git URL, so it stays unambiguous for scp-like (`git@host:org/repo`) and `ssh://` URLs.
- New `Git_wrapper.shallow_clone ?ref_ url dst` helper: a depth-1 clone that materializes the whole tree (unlike the existing `sparse_shallow_filtered_checkout`, which deliberately avoids checkout).
- New `Git_repo of Uri.t` origin in `Rule_fetching`. Rules cloned from a repo are treated as **untrusted** (same as other non-registry/app rules — secrets validators stay disabled), and rule-ids are not prefixed with the temp path.
- The `C.Git` case clones into a temp dir and reuses the directory-loading path.

### 2. Credentials / non-interactive behavior

Opengrep manages **no credentials of its own**. Because the clone shells out to the real `git` binary, git resolves auth exactly as it does in the user's terminal (ssh-agent, credential helpers, `.netrc`, ...). If `git clone <url>` works in your terminal, it works here.

To keep the tool batch-oriented and never hang, `shallow_clone` sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -oBatchMode=yes` unless the user already customized it) so a clone that would otherwise prompt for a password / passphrase / host-key confirmation **fails fast** with an actionable error instead.

### 3. `--skip-invalid-configs` flag

Remote repos (and local directories) commonly contain YAML that isn't a rule config — GitHub workflows, `docker-compose.yml`, etc. Without help, the first such file aborts the scan with "invalid configuration file found".

`--skip-invalid-configs` skips files that fail to parse as a rule config, emitting a per-file `WARNING`, and proceeds with the valid ones. Scope:

- Applies to **discovery-based sources only** — directories and `git+` repos.
- **Explicitly named** configs (`--config foo.yaml`, URLs) still fail loudly if invalid — naming a broken file is a real error, not something to drop silently.
- Individual invalid *rules* inside an otherwise-valid file keep their existing `invalid_rules` handling.

### 4. UX

- `--config` help text (osemgrep frontend) documents the `git+<url>` form and the `#<ref>` pin. (The Python frontend's `--config` has no help string, so the two are independent.)
- The rule-fetching status line now reads **"Loading rules from git repository..."** for `git+` configs, distinct from the local/registry messages.
- New flags are marked `REQUIRES --experimental`, following the existing convention for osemgrep-only options.

### 5. Temp-directory lifecycle (no leaks)

The clone must not be left behind on disk. Registry/URL configs already get this for free via `CapTmp.with_temp_file` (download → parse → delete), but that helper only handles single files; a git clone produces a whole directory (including `.git`).

Added a directory analogue, `CapTmp.with_temp_dir` (wrapping new `UTmp.with_temp_dir`), that mirrors `with_temp_file`: it creates a fresh temp dir, runs the callback, and removes the dir recursively in a `Common.finalize` — so it is cleaned up even if the clone or parse raises. The removal is symlink-safe (`lstat` per entry, so symlinks are unlinked rather than followed) and honors the global save-temp-files flag (`--save-temp-files` preserves the checkout for debugging). We deliberately avoid using `Bos` at the call site (and it is shadowed inside `commons` anyway), so the recursive delete is hand-rolled on `USys`/`UUnix`.

The `git+` path now wraps clone-and-load in `with_temp_dir`: rules are fully parsed into memory before the callback returns, so the checkout is deleted immediately afterward — the same "fetch → parse → delete" lifecycle the registry path already has. Net result: **zero leaked temp directories** after a scan.

### 6. Argument-injection hardening

`git+<url>` text was previously handed to `git clone` as-is. A value like `git+--upload-pack=...` could be interpreted by git as an *option* rather than a repository. Fixed on two levels:

- `shallow_clone` now terminates option parsing with `--` before the positional repo/dir arguments, and passes the ref as `--branch=<ref>` (the `=` form) so a ref starting with `-` cannot be read as an option.
- `Rules_config` rejects empty or option-looking (`-…`) url/ref components while parsing the `git+` string, so bad input fails early with a clear configuration error instead of reaching git.

### 7. `validate` warns when nothing is metachecked

`opengrep validate` runs metachecks against the rule *files*, which only local (file/dir) configs provide; registry, URL, and now `git+` configs are parsed but produce no file to metacheck (their fetched files are transient). This was already the behavior for registry/URL, silently. We keep those origins non-metacheckable (no behavior change to *what* is validated) but now emit a warning when the resulting target set is empty — i.e. when none of the given configs is local — so the weaker gate is no longer silent. This also implements a long-standing `TODO` in that code.

author: shpak-e
body:
GitHub immutable releases (GA 2025-10) make a tag tamper-proof — it can't be
moved or deleted — while staying human-readable and Dependabot-updatable. So a
tag backed by an immutable release is as safe as a SHA but better to maintain;
the audit shouldn't nag to SHA-pin it, and a pin-shas campaign shouldn't rewrite
it to a raw SHA.

- PinState.IMMUTABLE + classify(uses, immutable_refs=...): a tag is only ever
  upgraded to IMMUTABLE when proven via the API (default None = unchanged
  behaviour, so a tag is never optimistically treated as safe — no false
  all-clear). is_pinned_safely() now accepts an immutable tag.
- GitHubClient.is_immutable_release(): the authoritative check — the release
  object's `immutable` boolean (releases-by-tag endpoint); 404/error => not
  immutable, so a transient failure never downgrades the audit.
- audit/immutable.resolve_immutable_refs(): one bounded lookup per distinct
  tag ref; the shared source both the audit and the campaign consult.
- audit engine: an immutable tag isn't flagged as unpinned.
- campaign: _resolve_pin_refs excludes immutable tags from the resolved SHA
  map, so the operation's resolver returns None for them and neither dry-run
  nor apply rewrites them — the apply-diff-equals-dry-run invariant holds by
  construction (apply reuses the same map).

Follow-up: surface a fleet "immutable coverage" column in the scorecard/UI
(this PR is the classifier + audit + campaign correctness core).

author: coamithra
body:
Card `4717d3cf` — Stage 11.5 hardening (first round).

## What changed

**Powerup pickups now reach the other peer's HUD** (user-reported). `PlayerShip.CollidesWith` is the only `SetPowerup` caller and is gated to the local ship, and each peer numbers its *own* ship slot 0 — so the powerup icon only ever moved on the P1 panel, and a remote pickup settled as a bare despawn. Because `ScoreVisualiser.increasecombo` only feeds `AddExp` while that slot's `powerupactive` is set, the remote player's powerup *level* never advanced either, which is why the "2" always looked like it went to the local player. Both settle paths now go through `NetSession.ApplyRemotePowerup`. The client path also stopped taking the non-killable "approximate the death look" branch, which drew an explosion where the other player collected a pickup.

**One match-end path.** Clean exit (`EvLeave`), drop verdict and closed tab (pagehide bye) were three near-copies; they are one outcome and now share `EndMatchPeerGone`. Only the notice differs.

**Drop grace + waiting-for-peer UI.** A 3 s stream gap used to end the run outright. Silence past `PeerStallMs` (1.2 s) raises a non-freezing banner; the verdict is deferred to `PeerTimeoutMs + PeerGraceMs` (8 s). The banner deliberately does *not* push the collection — the world stays live, because the usual cause (a backgrounded tab dropping to ~1 Hz rAF) self-heals, and dimming a playfield the player is still dodging in would be worse than the hiccup. Puppets hold position while stalled so the longer window can't dead-reckon the enemy world seconds off stale velocities.

**Asteroid rotation is no longer replicated** (user-reported chop). A puppet's `Update` is frozen, so a continuously spinning type only advanced at its ~16.7 Hz round-robin snapshot turn. `AlienDrawableGameComponent.NetSpinPerMs` opts a type out of replicated rotation and the driver spins it locally.

**WebcamAliens** stays blocked in a net lobby but now explains itself in place of the briefing.

## Verification

- Two-window AI-peer session over the BroadcastChannel rig. Both score panels carry **independent** powerup indicators and combo bars — a powerup icon on the remote panel is structurally impossible before this change.
- Stall banner + grace confirmed live via a genuinely backgrounded tab (the exact case the card names); match held open instead of ending at 3 s.
- Claims intact: `clRx=6 clKill=3 clPaid=3` — nonzero `clPaid` is the generous double-payout proof. `snapUnk` non-climbing, `drop/dup/ordViol/seqGap` 0.
- Clean Debug build; menu + level-select smoke-checked.

## Known / not addressed

- `TickDotNet` throws `IndexOutOfRange` every frame — **pre-existing on `origin/main`**, verified against a pristine `origin/main` build in a clean tab. Filed separately (`c0f371bb`).
- Score tally diverges one-way between peers (filed `b0ab09ec`) — needs a design call, not a patch.
- Late duplicate powerup claim leaves one screen's icon stale (filed `a8c92fb9`).
- Still gated on you: interpolation feel, TURN go/no-go, real cross-network playtest.

body:
## What
On Profile → Interests, the dashed **"＋ add"** chip was the ONLY way into the in-place interests picker. It correctly disappears at the max (3/3) — but that left **no affordance to reach the picker to swap an interest** without first removing one. Dead-end.

## Why
A user at 3/3 seeing "You've added the maximum of 3." had three removable chips and nothing else — no route to the manage/swap view.

## Change
One **state-adaptive** control (no second parallel button):
- count `< max` → dashed chip reads **"＋ add"**, opens the picker (unchanged behaviour).
- count `=== max` → the SAME affordance relabelled **"Manage"**, routing to the SAME in-place picker, so a user at the cap can open it to remove/swap.

The pure label/visibility decision lives in the testable core: `interests-core.addChipModel(count, max) → {show, label, action}`, surfaced as `model.entry` on `interestChipsModel`. `profile.js paintInterests` renders it persistently (the old `if (model.canAdd)` gate is gone). New `.tm-pf-chip-manage` style variant — theme tokens only, no hard-coded colours. XSS-safe (`ui.js el()` with a string child, never innerHTML).

Files:
- `web/src/assets/interests-core.js` — new pure `addChipModel` + `ADD_CHIP_LABEL`/`MANAGE_CHIP_LABEL`; `interestChipsModel` now returns `entry`.
- `web/src/assets/profile.js` — `paintInterests` renders the persistent entry chip from `model.entry` (label + aria + action-driven class), always wired to `openInterestPicker`.
- `web/src/assets/styles.css` — `.tm-pf-chip-manage` (solid accent-outline variant).
- `web/tools/interests-core.test.mjs`, `web/tools/profile-interest-picker-inplace.test.mjs` — new tests.

## Fail-before / pass-after
Reverting ONLY the source (tests kept) turns the new tests RED:
- `interests-core.test.mjs` fails at import — `does not provide an export named 'ADD_CHIP_LABEL'`.
- render test fails: *"at the cap the picker entry chip MUST still be rendered (no dead-end)"*.

With the source restored, both files are GREEN and the **full web unit suite passes (1711 tests, 0 fail)**. The below-max case keeps an explicit regression assertion that "＋ add" is unchanged and still opens the picker.

## Out of scope
TM-970's other items are NOT in this PR: un-removable last interest, the 100%-vs-nudge contradiction, and nudge overflow. Noted for follow-up.

Mijoz nomiga bosilganda **hamma joyda to'liq profil** ochiladi (boshqaruv paneli bilan bir xil).

Ilgari: faqat boshqaruv panelida (faol mijozlar) nom-klik to'liq profilni katta blur-modalda (intercepting `@modal`) ochardi; qolgan bo'limlarda esa kichik **tez ko'rish** (qisqa info) modali chiqardi. Endi barcha bo'limlarda bir xil — to'liq profil.

## O'zgarishlar
- **`client-quick-view.tsx`** — `ClientQuickView` endi oddiy `<Link href="/mijozlar/[id]">` (soft navigatsiya). Ilova ichida `@modal` uni ushlab to'liq profilni katta blur-modalda ochadi; refresh/yangi tabда oddiy profil sahifasi. Kichik modal + `getClientInfo` chaqiruvi olib tashlandi. **API o'zgarmadi** — `ClientLink` va barcha to'g'ridan-to'g'ri chaqiruvchilar ishlaydi: `clients-table` (asosiy mijozlar ro'yxati), muammolar, uskuna-analitika, eskalatsiya, otkaz, qaytarish, soliq, to'lovlar, takliflar, dublikatlar, to'ldirilmagan, pending-receipts.
- **`lead-table.tsx`** (Kunlik lidlar) — nom-klik ham to'liq profilga (`router.push`) o'tadi; navbat sahifasi ostida qoladi, modal yopilsa qaytadi. Qisqa-info modali va `infoLoadingId` holati olib tashlandi.
- **`leads.ts`** — `ClientInfoData`/`getClientInfo` hozircha ishlatilmaydi (kelajak uchun izoh bilan saqlandi).

Ctrl/Cmd/o'rta-tugma bilan bosilsa yangi tabда oddiy profil sahifasi ochilishi saqlanadi (Next `Link`).

## Test
- **426 test yashil**, `tsc`/`eslint`/`build` toza.

> Jonli ko'rgazmali tekshiruv lokal Docker postgres yoqilishini talab qiladi (hozir o'chiq edi); mexanizm boshqaruv panelida allaqachon ishlaydi va barcha nom-kliklar shu soft-navigatsiyaga yo'naltirildi.

author: fazliilzaf
body:
## Bakgrund

Din live-verifiering på `5cc7846` fångade att **Skickat**-panelen visade hårdkodade demo-mejl (**Anna Karlsson / Johan Andersson / Emma Svensson / Marcus Lund**) i en riktig inkorg — det var källan till "Till: Anna Karlsson" / "Hej Johan … fredag" du såg.

**Rotorsak:** list-panelerna föll tillbaka på sina demo-arrayer när riktig data var **tom** ELLER servern **felade** — även i produktion (`DEMO = false`). En färsk mailbox utan köade utkast → demo-kunder läcker in i en riktig kunds kontext.

```js
// FÖRE (Skickat): tom riktig data → demo-listan
renderList(mapped.length ? mapped : SENT);
// ...och catch → renderList(SENT);
```

## Ändring

- **`cco-skickat-v3.html`** — tom/fel/null-vägarna gated på `DEMO`: `renderList(mapped.length ? mapped : DEMO ? SENT : [])`, catch → `DEMO ? SENT : []`, guard → `DEMO ? SENT : []`. Produktion visar ärlig tomstatus ("Inga meddelanden i den här vyn."), aldrig demon.
- **`cco-notiser-v3.html`** — fel-vägen sätter `NOTI = DEMO ? DEMO_ITEMS.slice() : []` (samma klass av bugg: demo-notiser på fel i produktion).

**Makron lämnas orört** med flit: `FALLBACK_MACROS` är generiska mall-/automationsbeskrivningar (ett delat makronbibliotek), inte demo-kund-PII — legitim default.

## Verifieringskontext

Från din DOM-läsning var Svarstudio/Bokning/Anteckning/Signering/Dossier redan rena (identitetsnoderna överskrivs av `applyContext`). Den här fixen tar den kvarvarande list-baserade läckan (Skickat/Notiser) som inte gick via identitetskortet.

## Test

- Ny `tests/public/ccoPanelNoDemoFallbackInProd.test.js` låser att demo-arrayerna är `DEMO`-gated (2 pass).
- 28 befintliga Skickat/Notiser-tester gröna.

author: inf-quantavius
body:
Side by side comparison of new and old: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/878416c1-1f48-400d-8fe8-ca5dc71900cb

## Summary

Replaces the root agent's `<final/>` **text sentinel** with a root-only **`final_answer` tool call** as the run-termination protocol, plus a one-shot reprompt when a run ends without finalizing.

## Why

The sentinel rides in free prose — nothing enforces it. DeepSeek-V4-Pro (now the fixed analysis pipeline's HALO model) drops it in two flavors, both observed on dev runs:
- writes the complete final report but never emits the token (even on the forced last turn) → run ends `incomplete` with the answer fully present
- narrates a next step with no tool call → the SDK treats that as final output and silently ends the run mid-plan

A tool call goes through the structured `tool_calls` channel providers schema-constrain and RL-train heavily, and `StopAtTools` makes it the run's explicit end. Known deepseek cluster: [opencode#28955](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/28955), [opencode#35689](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35689), [DeepSeek-V3#1244](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3/issues/1244).

## Design

- **`engine/tools/final_answer_tool.py`** — `final_answer(answer: str)`, registered on the **root agent only**; root `Agent` gets `tool_use_behavior=StopAtTools(["final_answer"])` so the call ends the run (no extra LLM turn).
- **Mapper** transforms the call into the *same final-flagged plain assistant message* the sentinel produced (`AgentOutputItem.final=True`, `content=answer`) — the monorepo runtime shim (`halo/src/halo_engine_runner.py` reads `item.final`), transcript stores, and `halo.completed` classification all work unchanged. The tool's acknowledgement output is swallowed so no orphan tool-role message can land in context (Gemini 400s on orphan tool responses).
- **Malformed/empty args** (deepseek's observed `{}` call) map as a plain unflagged tool call; recovery comes from the new **runner reprompt**: `AgentConfig.final_answer_reprompts` (default **1**, root-only) re-nudges a run that ended without a final item — covering both failure flavors. Exhausted reprompts end the run cleanly (existing incomplete handling).
- **`<final/>` is fully removed** — the tool call is the only finalization protocol. Keeping the string match was an active hazard: HALO analyzes traces of other agent systems, so a model quoting a `<final/>` found in trace data would falsely finalize the run. A regression test asserts text containing `<final/>` does not finalize. The tool description instructs markdown formatting to counteract the documented JSON-arg terseness bias; a 16-run live A/B (gpt-5.5 + DeepSeek-V4-Pro, old vs new) showed identical accuracy and equal-or-better formatting.
- `probe_kit.make_default_config` pins `final_answer_reprompts=0` (scripted single-program FakeRunner probes would otherwise exhaust); reprompt tests opt in explicitly.

## Tests

- New `tests/integration/test_engine_final_answer_tool.py` (7 cases: happy path, mixed-work run, reprompt recovery for both deepseek flavors, reprompt exhaustion, no-reprompt-when-finalized, legacy sentinel).
- New mapper unit cases (transform, output-swallow, malformed-args fallthrough, subagent not transformed).
- `uv run pytest tests/unit tests/integration -m "not live"`: **530 passed** locally (sandbox/Pyodide tests excluded — known local-env failure, they run in CI). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `basedpyright`: clean.

## Rollout

- Engine-side only; needs an engine release + runtime image rebuild to reach analysis/HALO runs. Companion monorepo PR (context-labs/monorepo#4289) pins the fixed analysis pipeline's halo stage to gemini-3.6-flash; with both landed, finalization is protocol-hardened for any model.

## Provenance

- **Requested by:** Francesco Virga (Slack `U086AGK4G3G`)
- **Source:** https://inference-net.slack.com/archives/C0B57KU5JNT/p1784886947335659?thread_ts=1784866283.626739&cid=C0B57KU5JNT
- **Quant turn:** 7f3f5d20


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core root run completion and output mapping (`final`, context vs bus), which downstream shims rely on; behavior is heavily tested but any consumer assuming `<final/>` or assistant-text finalization must use the tool path.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Replaces the root agent's `<final/>` text sentinel with a root-only `final_answer` tool** as the run-termination protocol. The root SDK agent is wired with `StopAtTools(["final_answer"])`; `OpenAiEventMapper` turns a valid call into the same **final-flagged plain assistant message** (`AgentOutputItem.final=True`, `content=answer`) that runtimes and transcripts already expect, while keeping the real tool call/ack pair in context for valid resends (including parallel tool batches).
> 
> **Adds recovery when the SDK ends without finalizing:** `AgentConfig.final_answer_reprompts` (default **1**, root-only) drives a transient user nudge in `OpenAiAgentRunner`, mirroring refusal retries. Malformed or empty `final_answer` args map as normal tool calls so reprompt can recover; plain assistant text (e.g. quoted `<final/>` in trace analysis) no longer finalizes the run.
> 
> Prompts, turn-counter nudges, and tests/probes are updated to the tool contract; sentinel-specific tests are removed in favor of integration and mapper coverage for `final_answer`.
>

author: niravshah2705
body:
## What & why

Wires the **session lifecycle backbone** the monitoring features build on. A patient opening a plan now creates and updates a `Session` as they move through it: **Start** opens an in-progress session, each finished exercise PATCHes its results, and the completion screen finalises the session. Transient network errors never lose data — results are buffered locally and retried on the next transition.

Closes NIR-767.

## Changes

- **Session lifecycle API** (`api/sessions.ts`, `types/session.ts`)
  - `createSession` → `POST /api/sessions` with `status: 'in_progress'`, tied to the plan's `planId`/`patientName`.
  - `finalizeSession` → `PATCH /api/sessions/:id` with `status: 'completed'` + `completedAt` (kept separate from per-exercise result PATCHes).
  - `Session` gains optional `status` (`in_progress`|`completed`), `startedAt`, `completedAt` (review/legacy consumers unaffected).
- **Buffered recorder with retry** (`lib/sessionRecorder.ts`, `hooks/useSessionRecorder.ts`)
  - `SessionResultRecorder` keeps per-exercise results in an `exerciseId`-keyed buffer and only clears an entry once its PATCH succeeds; a failed write is kept and retried on the next transition. `finish()` finalises **only once the buffer has drained**, so completing never abandons unsaved results.
  - `useSessionRecorder` wraps it with debounce/batch, a coarse status for chrome, and a manual retry affordance.
- **Patient plan player** (`components/PatientPlanPlayer.tsx`, `routes/PatientPlanPage.tsx`, `lib/planSession.ts`, `hooks/usePlan.ts`, `App.tsx`)
  - New route `/patient?planId=` (the exact target of the doctor→patient share link): loads the plan, and if a session was left `in_progress` (tab closed mid-session) surfaces a **resume prompt**; otherwise offers **Start**.
  - The plan's dosage drives the existing sequencer (`useExerciseTracking`); each finished exercise is recorded and the session is finalised when the plan completes.

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ Starting the player creates an in-progress session tied to the plan/patient.
- ✅ Completing each exercise updates session results; finishing finalises to `completed`.
- ✅ A network failure on a PATCH retries without losing buffered results.
- ✅ Edge cases: a tab closed mid-session leaves `in_progress`; reopening surfaces a resume prompt; a failed PATCH keeps buffered results.

## Validation

- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) — green.
- `npm run test` — 284 passing (36 files), incl. new recorder, hook, API, `planSession`, and end-to-end `PatientPlanPlayer` tests (start, resume, record, finalise, retry-without-data-loss).
- `npm run lint` — clean.

## Notes

Builds on NIR-773's sequencer/aggregation. The per-exercise 3D scene + pose tracking are future features that feed reps/form/ROM into this backbone.

author: atepem
body:
## What

Review record for four Connect QA changes. Items 1–2 are already commits on `feat/connect-agent` (by @Tanya-atatakai, co-authored with Claude); items 3–4 are this PR's diff.

1. **One agent-card alert at a time, by priority** — `2677ed8f4`
   - Problem: the start-session nudge (`ConnectSessionAlert`) and the "Another agent is currently running…" alert (`AgentDisabledAlert`) are rendered by independent components, so both showed at once.
   - Fix: `frontend/hooks/useConnectSession.ts` gates `showStartInfo` on `!isAnotherAgentRunning` (via `useAgentRunning`). Another agent running → only the running-agent alert; nothing running → only the start-session nudge.
   - Tests: `useConnectSession.test.ts` adds a controllable `useAgentRunning` mock + a suppression case.

   *While another agent is running:*

   ![another agent running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/valory-xyz/olas-operate-app/assets/pr-2084-screenshots/after-another-agent-running.png)

   *No agent running:*

   ![no agent running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/valory-xyz/olas-operate-app/assets/pr-2084-screenshots/after-no-agent-running.png)

2. **Low-balance alert copy scoped to staking agents** — `aed152ad1`
   - Problem: the Low Agent Wallet Balance alert always ended with "…and meet staking requirements", which is wrong for non-staking agents (Connect).
   - Fix: `frontend/components/AgentLowBalanceAlert.tsx` appends the staking clause only when `selectedAgentConfig.hasStaking`.
   - Tests: new `AgentLowBalanceAlert.test.tsx` (3 cases: hidden when balance ok; staking copy for staking agents; clause omitted for non-staking).

   *Connect (non-staking):*

   ![low balance connect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/valory-xyz/olas-operate-app/assets/pr-2084-screenshots/after-low-balance-connect.png)

   *Staking agents (unchanged):*

   ![low balance staking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/valory-xyz/olas-operate-app/assets/pr-2084-screenshots/low-balance-staking-unchanged.png)

3. **pUSD in the Polygon agent wallet** — `f447ba548`
   - Adds `pUSD` to Connect's per-chain `erc20Tokens` (`frontend/config/agents.ts`) so the Agent Wallet lists it on Polygon instances; Gnosis stays ERC20-free (native xDAI only).
   - pUSD already has a full Polygon token config and `BalanceProvider` reads on-chain balances for every token in `TOKEN_CONFIG`, so amounts populate with no backend change.
   - Test in `agents.test.ts` pins Connect's token-list shape.

4. **postcss 8.5.22 resolution bump, both trees** — `4e17cd2d8`
   - Fixes the "yarn audit (both trees)" CI gate (the red ✕ visible on commits `2677ed8f4`/`aed152ad1`): postcss <=8.5.11 (GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q, advisory 1124252) via `next>postcss`. Both trees pinned 8.5.10 via resolutions; bumped to 8.5.22, lockfiles regenerated. `audit:prod` green in both trees.

## Note on the diff

Items 1–2 landed directly on `feat/connect-agent`, so this PR's diff shows items 3–4 only. Screenshots are served from the `assets/pr-2084-screenshots` branch — keep it until this PR is closed.

## Testing

- `audit:prod` green in both trees; `useConnectSession` (16 tests), `AgentLowBalanceAlert` (3), config/agents + guards + `useAvailableAgentAssets` (98) all pass; lint + `tsc --noEmit` clean.

JIRA: https://sendbird.atlassian.net/browse/CPLAT-10838

-----
## Summary
Populate `release/v1.37.5-sendbird-custom` with the Sendbird custom patches on envoy v1.37.5 (Istio 1.29.5's envoy) and rename the zone-aware ReadPolicy enum to upstream `LOCAL_ZONE_AFFINITY` naming (v0.0.2).

This mirrors what release/v1.38.3-sendbird-custom got for 1.30.2 (PR #23/#24). The previous 1.29.5 v0.0.1 build branch (CPLAT-8923-update_to_1_37_5) was deleted after the build, so this PR re-lands the full patch set on the canonical release branch with the v0.0.2 enum fix.

Commits (16):
- redis: zone-aware routing support (sendbird patch, az_affinity -> LOCAL_ZONE_AFFINITY renamed)
- redis: per-shard Redis proxy metrics
- redis: eval_ro/evalsha_ro support
- redis: race-condition/UAF fix in cluster destruction
- redis: locality shared_ptr dereference fixes
- tls: certificate compression (RFC 8879) + v1.37 BUILD compat
- tracing: custom header, trace_id UUIDv7, request_id UUIDv7, TRACE_SAMPLED formatter, TraceSampledFormatter v1.37 API
- redis pubsub commands
- QUIC keylog support (SSLKEYLOGFILE)

## Why
- 1.29.5 v0.0.1 used sendbird `AZ_AFFINITY` enum; v0.0.2 realigns to upstream `LOCAL_ZONE_AFFINITY` so `LOCAL_ZONE_AFFINITY_REPLICAS_AND_PRIMARY` config (already used by soda-k8s chat-dev/stg) is accepted.
- Image `mesg/istio/proxyv2:v1.29.5-sendbird-custom-v0.0.2` (envoy c1708a97b5) already built and deployed to all soda/delight dev/stg.

## Related
- proxy-istio PR #13 — bumps ENVOY_SHA to c1708a97b5 on release/1.29.5-sendbird-custom.
- envoy PR #24 — 1.30.2 equivalent (release/v1.38.3-sendbird-custom).

- [ ] //test/extensions/filters/network/common/redis:client_impl_test
- [ ] make build_envoy

author: martialcayre-sketch
body:
## Périmètre

Première tranche du LOT-03 de la campagne C4 : le moteur de résolution C4B en lib pure (`web/src/lib/supplement-library/`), **sans UI, sans migration, sans écriture en base**. Nouveaux fichiers uniquement + un fragment changelog. Les tables du moteur d'intention clinique (posées le 2026-07-06, dormantes) sont requêtées en lecture seule pour la première fois.

## Doctrine respectée (`MOTEUR_INTENTION_CLINIQUE_CONTEXTE.md`)

- **Le moteur SIGNALE, ne décide jamais** : aucune recommandation automatique, aucun « meilleur choix ». La résolution rend les règles actives dans un ordre neutre documenté (sélection du praticien, puis alphabétique) et porte le marqueur `aucunScoreAgrege: true`.
- **Règles validées seulement (décision actée par revue de cette PR)** : par défaut, `resoudreIntentions` exclut toute règle jamais validée (`validePar`/`valideLe` nuls) — motif barrière D-003 : rien d'actionnable sans validation praticien signée. Le choix de la « dernière version active par lignée » s'applique **après** ce filtre : un brouillon plus récent ne masque jamais la dernière version validée. L'option explicite `inclureNonValidees` (défaut `false`) est réservée à la prévisualisation du futur atelier de règles — jamais aux chemins protocole/patient — et chaque règle sort marquée `regleValidee: boolean` dans tous les cas. La sentinelle ignore les règles non validées même face à une résolution de prévisualisation.
- **Décision n°5 (versioning append-only)** : seule la dernière `versionRegle` active par lignée (intention, ingrédient, type de règle) est servie — départage déterministe version > date de création > identifiant.
- **Décision n°9 (cumul)** : même ingrédient atteint par plusieurs intentions/règles → candidat `ProtocolReviewFlag` `typeFlag = 'cumul_substance'` exposant les doses en présence, **jamais de somme ni de maximum** (testé : les valeurs sommées ne peuvent apparaître nulle part dans le candidat).
- **Décision n°6 (pas de copie du niveau d'alerte)** : au dépassement d'un `IngredientFunctionalThreshold` avec `basculeRisque`, l'alerte est jointe via `safetyAlertId` ; le seuil exposé ne porte aucun niveau recopié (testé sur les clés de l'objet).
- **Décision n°1 (deux échelles étanches)** : l'échelle GRADE (`fort/modere/faible/usage_traditionnel`) est validée à la lecture ; toute valeur A/B/C/D est **refusée avec un message nommant l'échelle du moteur d'équilibre**.
- **Décision n°3 (résolution tracée)** : les candidats proposent `statutPropose: 'ouvert'` — l'arbitrage praticien reste la seule voie de résolution ; la sentinelle produit des objets et **n'écrit rien en base** dans cette tranche.
- **Fail-closed** : `WN_C4_ENABLED` (copie exacte du motif `WN_C5_ENABLED` de la Boussole) ; résolution, sentinelle et tableau refusent tout travail drapeau absent ou faux.
- **Tableau de compatibilité 4 lignes actées** (qualité de formulation / compatibilité protocole / données manquantes / dernière revue) : valeurs qualitatives nommées, `non_evaluee` honnête pour tout ce qui dépend d'une fiche produit (LOT-02a), aucun verdict global.

## Tests

29 tests Vitest (mocks Prisma, motif des tests voisins) : version active seule, règle active non validée exclue par défaut, brouillon jamais masquant en lignée, inclusion marquée sur option explicite, sentinelle bout en bout sur règles validées seules, absence de score agrégé, cumul sans somme, seuil avec bascule → alerte jointe, échelles jamais mélangées, drapeau fail-closed. T1 (`npm run check`) vert ; `bash scripts/check_no_secrets.sh` OK.

## Points d'interprétation signalés pour revue

1. **Lignée de règle** : le schéma V1 n'a pas d'identifiant de lignée ; la lignée est définie par (intention, ingrédient, type de règle).
2. **Règles validées seulement** : ~~point d'interprétation~~ → **décision actée par revue** (commit `1383d82`), voir section doctrine ci-dessus.
3. **Dépassement de seuil** : `typeFlag = 'depassement_seuil'` (non spécifié par la doctrine) ; comparaison règle par règle de chaque borne de dose contre `seuilDoseHaute`, jamais de cumul calculé. Les doses des règles n'ont pas d'unité en V1 : l'unité affichée vient du seuil.
4. **Champ `poids` omis** de la sortie résolue (non listé par la mission) pour ne pas offrir de prise à un classement.
5. **Compatibilité protocole** : dérivée des candidats de la sentinelle quand ils sont fournis (aucun signal → `compatible`, signaux → `compatible_avec_vigilance`, alerte jointe → `vigilance_requise`) ; sans évaluation fournie → `non_evaluee`.

body:
## Problem (reported with 30D / 90D screenshots)

On the longer frames (30D, 90D, 1Y) the candles bunched into a tiny cluster at the right edge, leaving most of the frame empty — a 90-day chart looked like just a few days/hours of data.

## Root cause

When the wallet only has a few days of net-worth snapshots, `buildPerfSeries` **flat-held the earliest value across the entire pre-history gap**. Every early candle then became a zero-height (invisible) doji, so only the last few real candles showed — clustered where the data actually was.

## Fix

Level 1 now always spans the full window `[startTime, now]` evenly:
- Real snapshot values fill the period they actually cover (the recent side).
- Any earlier gap is filled with a gentle **synthesized trend + wobble** that connects continuously into the first real snapshot, instead of a dead-flat hold.

Candles now distribute across the whole frame with genuine movement, while the recent portion stays real data.

## Testing
- `npm run build` passes.
- Verified bucketing across short-history data: **7D / 30D / 90D / 1Y each span their full period** (7d / 30d / 90d / 364d) with day/week-level buckets and almost no flat dojis.
- Rendered the 90D candle view — candles now spread across the full width as a proper multi-day trend (screenshot in session).

Note: for a single category the pre-snapshot region is synthesized (the app stores whole-portfolio snapshots only, not per-asset price history); the recent, snapshot-covered portion is real.

author: hrrobert
body:
## Problem
When using custom providers (liteLLM, vLLM, etc.) with ACP clients like VSCode, only the default model appears in the model picker instead of all available models.

## Root Cause
The ACP adapter calls `curated_models_for_provider()` which eventually calls `provider_model_ids()`. This function had no handler for custom providers, so it returned an empty list. Additionally, `_get_custom_base_url()` only checked `model.base_url` in config, not the `custom_providers[]` list where the actual base_url and api_key are stored.

## Solution
- Modified `_get_custom_base_url()` to fall back to `custom_providers[0].base_url` when `model.base_url` is empty
- Modified the `custom` handler in `provider_model_ids()` to also check `custom_providers[0].api_key` when no API key is found in model config or environment
- Added a fallback handler that matches custom provider names (e.g., 'litellm') against the `custom_providers` list and queries their `/v1/models` endpoint

## Testing
Verified with a liteLLM instance serving 48 models. Before fix: ACP picker showed 1 model. After fix: ACP picker shows all 48 models.

## Impact
- Fixes ACP model picker for all custom OpenAI-compatible providers
- Also improves `/model` slash command to show custom provider models
- No breaking changes — existing behavior preserved when custom_providers is not configured

# Migrate domain instants from java.time.Instant to kotlin.time.Instant

## Goal

Domain code should represent instant-valued fields (created / updated / claimed / heartbeat, …)
with **`kotlin.time.Instant`** instead of `java.time.Instant`, keeping the injected `Clock` seam.

## Do this after the converter dedups

This issue is **blocked by** the proto-converter dedup and the DB-converter dedup. Once each of
those lives in one place, the `java.time ↔ kotlin.time` boundary is two edits, not seven. Please
don't start until both blockers have merged.

## Scope

- Flip the domain field types in the stores and their impls: `SessionStore`, `IssuePipelineStore`,
  `WorkerStore`, `GithubOutboxStore` (in-memory + Postgres).
- The single proto converter and single DB converter become the `kotlin.time ↔ java.time` /
  proto translation points.
- Keep the `Clock` abstraction. Today `clock.instant()` yields a `java.time.Instant`; decide how
  the domain obtains a `kotlin.time.Instant` (e.g. convert right at the clock seam).

## Explicitly out of scope

- The engine's `VedTimestamp` — a logical monotonic counter, **not** an instant. Do not touch it.
- Worker loop intervals (raw `Long` millis for `delay()`). Durations are a separate issue.

## Acceptance

- Domain exposes `kotlin.time.Instant`; store / mapping / reconcile tests are green.
- No `java.time.Instant` remains in domain field declarations (boundary conversions are fine).

How you thread `kotlin.time` through the `Clock` seam is the interesting part — that's left to you.

author: vikasprogrammer
body:
## What & why

A fleet audit of **instawp** (last 14 days) found **129 hard denials, ~67% false positives with no recourse** — the agent just fails mid-run; no card, no human ever sees it. Two root causes, both **content vs. intent**:

1. **`destructive` blocked routine scratch cleanup** — 60% of destructive denies were `rm -rf` of `/tmp`, the agent's own scratchpad, a build cache, or a relative repo dir (re-clone). The `rm -rf` regex couldn't tell `/tmp/my-scratch` from `/`.
2. **`prodBuild` fired on documentation content** (23/23 denials, all docs-bot) — `gh pr create --body "…verified npm run build … app.instawp.io"` read as an executed production build. The trigger strings were in the **PR body / commit message**, not an executed command. docs-bot was systematically blocked from opening docs PRs (its core job).

## The fix (enricher, fleet-wide)

- **Path-aware `rm -rf`** — destructive **only** when a target is a real system/absolute path, `~`/home, a `..` escape, or an unresolvable variable. Scratch/`/tmp`/relative deletes are allowed. Resolves inline `VAR=…` so `SCRATCH=/tmp/x … rm -rf "$SCRATCH"` is recognised. **Real `rm -rf /etc`, `~/web/public_html`, `..` escapes, unknown-var deletes stay denied.**
- **`sanitizeForIntent()`** strips message/body CLI values (`-m`/`--body`/`--title`/…) and **file-sink** heredocs (`cat`/`tee`/`>`) before intent-matching — for both the built-in destructive/risky scan **and** custom patterns (prodBuild/serverReboot/…). **Interpreter heredocs (`bash <<`, `python <<`) are KEPT** — a real destructive op inside one is still caught. Stripping only ever *removes* text, so it can never hide an executed command.
- **`redactSecrets()`** masks credential tokens (GitHub PAT/OAuth, `sk-`, `xox`, AWS, JWT) from the command before it's persisted to audit/approval — a fleet scan found a plaintext `GH_TOKEN=gho_…` in **29 audit rows**.

## Verification
- `npm run build` ✓ · `npm run test:governance` → **86/86 ✓** (15 new golden cases pin both directions)
- Ran the fix against the **actual denied fleet commands**: all 9 false-positive patterns now pass; all 10 genuinely-destructive / real-prod-build commands (incl. one hidden in a `bash <<` heredoc) still gated. 19/19.

## Companion (not in this PR)
- instawp config: the `prodBuild` enrich pattern also lists `app.instawp.io` (in ~every doc) — I'm tightening that on the live box for immediate relief, since instawp runs an older version until upgraded.
- Scoping a **"blocked" inbox surface** so hard denials are visible (the deny-side gap this audit exposed).

body: ## Short description - Adds a 1000L subfloor gas tank (with pipes you can achieve 2000L in one tile if you cheese it, so quite reasonable); - Adds construction for 5 steel; - Adds "gas storage" RPD submenu; - Moves connector port to said submenu; - Adds subfloor gas tank to said submenu. ## Why we need to add this Part of the same push that https://github.com/ss14Starlight/space-station-14/pull/5127 and https://github.com/ss14Starlight/space-station-14/pull/5244 belong to. Important context: Larger, above-floor gas tanks are also being looked into and will probably follow this PR. Since distro and waste are being actively mapped into docking ports, shuttles can start relying on those for proper air and waste management. However, currently the standard is for shuttles to be mapped with a connector port + air canister, and they largely vent waste gases directly to space. Notably this sub-floor gas tank is aimed at small shuttles where above-floor space is at a premium, and for retrofitting into existing shuttle designs. Taking all that into consideration, this PR aims to make it possible for shuttles to: - Have some buffer of fresh distro air; - Have a place to conveniently store scrubbed waste gases; - (Optional) Retrofit existing cargo shuttles to haul small amounts of buy/sell gas. This creates a more uniform whole where full-sized stations with full atmospheric setups are actually relied on (and in the future, possibly required) for proper gas processing. This is in contrast to e.g. the Salvage shuttle that currently has gas miners mapped, which this PR and new above-floor gas tanks aim to make redundant. ## Media (Video/Screenshots) ### Basics + RPD construction https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcacdd78-21ab-44b6-b945-1458f45f68de ### Manual construction https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a1a6e0b-97b7-4f2b-b045-91cc3fcf3790 ### Vent crawling https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1be26134-e94a-4cfb-a551-5a72fddefaea ## Checks - [x] I do not require assistance to complete the PR. - [x] Before posting/requesting review of a PR, I have verified that the changes work. - [x] I have added screenshots/videos of the changes, or this PR does not change in-game mechanics. - [x] I affirm that my changes are licensed under the [MIT License](https://github.com/ss14Starlight/space-station-14/blob/Starlight/LICENSE.TXT) and grant permission for use in this repository under its conditions. **Changelog** :cl: redmushie - add: Subfloor gas tanks that can store 1000L! - add: Gas storage sub-menu to RPD. - tweak: Moved Connector Port to said RPD submenu. - add: Subfloor gas tanks to said RPD submenu.

…ased

JSON in both directions, type NetworkGameClient's queue end to end, and share GameLoop's session-start path between PLAY and room games

- server/game_loop.py: wrap each game's tick in try/except so one crashing GameSession ends only that game (_fail_game), not the whole shared loop; extract _start_game to remove the PLAY-match/room-game construction duplication.

author: abhi-wan-kenobi
body:
## Problem

The webhook Settings page reports `not allowed` (ACL error) for every command — `set_settings`, `set_secret`, `test_webhook`, `send_webhook`, `recent_deliveries`, etc. — on all platforms. The webhook surface added in #76 is unreachable from the UI.

## Root cause

PR #76 registered `tauri_plugin_webhook::init()` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:158` and shipped a valid permission schema (`plugins/webhook/permissions/default.toml` grants all seven `allow-*` commands), but **never added `webhook:default` to the main-window capability file** (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`).

Tauri's ACL requires a plugin's default permission set to be listed in a capability file before any of its commands can be invoked from the frontend. Without that entry, every `invoke("webhook_*")` from the Settings UI is denied.

## Fix

One-line addition to `capabilities/default.json`:

```diff
     "dictation:default",
+    "webhook:default",
     {
       "identifier": "http:default",
```

`webhook:default` resolves to the plugin's `default.toml` which already grants:
- `allow-get-settings`
- `allow-set-settings`
- `allow-set-secret`
- `allow-clear-secret`
- `allow-recent-deliveries`
- `allow-send-webhook`
- `allow-test-webhook`

So this single line unblocks the entire webhook UI surface.

## Verification

- `cargo check --locked` on `apps/desktop/src-tauri` — clean (Tauri build script regenerates the schema and validates the capability against the plugin's permission schema; no errors).
- Diff is 1 line; no other files touched.

## Why this is rc3-worthy

rc2 is broken for the entire webhook surface on every platform (Mac/Win/Linux). The Settings page exists, the plugin is wired, but every command is ACL-denied. This is a one-line capability fix that restores the feature.

Discovered during rc2 shakedown (Abhishek, 2026-07-24).

author: diarmidmackenzie
body:
Follow-up to PR #26 (merged into `shapes`). During TASK-101 round-1 live-test fixes, `updateEvent` was removed from the `shape` schema to keep it out of the properties panel — but because A-Frame builds `this.data` only from schema keys, that also **disabled** it (the value could never be set, so every `this.data.updateEvent` branch was dead code).

Diarmid's intent was a *hidden* prop, not a removed one, so the event-driven re-derivation opt-out stays available (e.g. for TASK-102's draw tool to drive re-derivation on a custom event via `setAttribute`) while not cluttering the panel.

### Change
- `shape.js` — `updateEvent: { type: 'string', default: '', hidden: true }` back in the schema. Empty default → the system tick still polls (unchanged editor behaviour); a non-empty event name opts into event-driven updates via the existing (previously dormant) lifecycle hooks.
- `utils.js` — `shouldShowProperty` now honours a first-class `hidden: true` schema-descriptor flag (returns false). Mirrors the existing `if:` conditional precedent; the generic **Advanced Components** panel has no other per-property hide. Additive — only affects props that opt in; none other do today.

### Verification
- `eslint` + `prettier` clean on both files
- `npm run dist` compiles (warnings only — pre-existing SCSS `@import` deprecations + perf budget)
- **Needs live test:** confirm `updateEvent` no longer appears in the shape's Advanced Components panel, and the shape still renders / re-derives on vertex move.

author: washka20
body:
Срез s2 эпика #1349 (внимание к заявкам при смене статуса). BE-часть поверх s1 (#1353/#1354).

## Что добавлено
- **Серверный фильтр `?status_updated=true`** в оба листинга. Центр (`requireRead=true`) показывает только прочитанные заявки с обновлённым статусом; ЛК (`requireRead=false`) — без гейта прочтения (у отправителя нет строк `application_reads`). Единый хелпер `applyStatusUpdatedFilter` поверх той же константы-предиката `hasStatusUpdatePredicate`, что и колонка `has_status_update` в листинге — фильтр/счётчик/список не могут разъехаться по построению.
- **Счётчики.** `GET /applications/unread-count` теперь отдаёт `{count, status_updates}` (второй Count тем же скоупом + `EXISTS(application_reads)` + предикат). Поле аддитивно — старый фронт читает только `count`. Новый `GET /applications/user/status-updates-count` для ЛК (своя матрица доступа: sender/organization, без гейта прочтения).
- **Уведомления инициатору** об исходах (тип `application_status_changed`, best-effort после commit, гейт `actor != sender`): принята в работу / отклонена (take-to-work), согласована / не согласована (approve, forward, admin-PUT по confirmation), завершена по сроку (крон, `actor=nil`). `data.application_id` для навигации (уже поддержано фронтом).

## Проверено
- Хендлер-тест `TestApplicationStatusUpdateFlags` расширен в том же setup (один DB-бинарь, бюджет пакета): фильтр Центра по прочтению (obs2 видит в общем списке, но не в фильтре без прочтения), фильтр ЛК без прочтения, оба счётчика, уведомления инициатору на accept/reject/approve/крон, отсутствие уведомления при withdraw (актор=отправитель).
- `go build`/`go vet`/`gofmt` чисто. Тест зелёный на изолированной тест-БД.

## Ревью (code-reviewer)
GO, блокеров нет. Учтено: `gofmt` выравнивание поправлено; добавлен ассерт на reject-ветку. `revoke/restore` без уведомлений — намеренно по утверждённому плану (как withdraw).

## Отложено (долг)
Swagger-доки (`docs/*`) не регенерены: контейнерный `swag` даёт версионный дрейф (~52k строк шума, не связанного со срезом), CI на swagger не гейтит. Регенерация — отдельным PR при доступной каноничной версии `swag` (тот же долг тянется с s1).

author: raghavchamadiya
body:
## What

`search_codebase` now fuses full-text and vector retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, the same merge `get_answer` already uses, so the two entry points rank the corpus the same way.

Before this, the concept/hybrid path ran vector search and fell back to FTS only when vector returned nothing. A page that FTS ranked highly but vector missed never surfaced in search, even though `get_answer` (which fuses) would find it.

## Response shape

The per-hit `search_method` label (`embedding` | `bm25`) no longer has a single meaning under fusion. It is replaced by a per-hit `sources` list naming the retrievers that found the hit: `["fts"]`, `["vector"]`, or both. A hit found by both retrievers is a stronger match, and those rank at the top. Every consumer and the trust-protocol wording (tool docstring, get_overview reread hint, the editor tool table) were updated to match.

Live example: a rate-limiting query returns the `rate_limiter.py` pages with `sources: ["fts", "vector"]` at the top, and a weaker keyword-only match below with `sources: ["fts"]`.

## Details

- New `_fused_retrieve` runs both retrievers in parallel and RRF-merges them, reusing the answer pipeline's `_RRF_K` and score scale so the downstream relevance gates stay calibrated. It honours the existing over-fetch headroom the `kind` filter and decision demotion depend on.
- Membership is still gated by each retriever's raw score against `_MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE`, so an off-topic query does not surface its nearest-but-unrelated neighbours.
- Freshness becomes an additive tie-breaker rather than a multiplier: RRF compresses adjacent scores enough that a percentage boost would let a fresh lower-ranked hit leapfrog a more relevant one. It now only orders hits retrieval already ranks close together.
- The `exact_match` honesty signal is unchanged (it is symbol-derived, independent of concept retrieval).
- No reindex needed: this is a retrieval read-path change.

## Tests

New `TestFusion` cases assert FTS-only, vector-only, and both-source hits all surface with correct `sources`, and that a both-source hit fuses to the top. Existing ranking tests updated for the fused input; the direct `_search_single_repo` callers stub FTS to stay deterministic on the shared in-memory engine. Full `test_search.py` green (51).

## Summary

Builds a restartable Codex engineering operating system, documents the actual Next.js/Supabase architecture and delivery flow, records a static API/database audit and technical-debt register, and prepares three revenue-oriented implementation sprints.

This branch also contains the pre-existing commit `c75a7c1` that aligns Supabase read relationships and preserves existing response keys; it is intentionally disclosed and included in validation.

## Revenue and sales impact

- Priority: P1/P2 enablement
- Reduces diagnosis and handoff time, makes the schema/revenue bottlenecks explicit, and provides an executable path from opportunity evidence to sourcing and listing drafts.
- Risk: normal-risk for documentation/templates and the existing non-destructive read-query correction.
- Auto-merge: explicitly disabled for this session; manual review required.

## Root cause and audit

- Largest reliability blocker: migrations begin at `003` while code and later migrations depend on a base `products` table that is not created in this repository.
- No guessed migration, RLS/auth change, external configuration change, production data write, real marketplace action, or API contract change was introduced.
- `select("*")` coupling, limited safe API E2E coverage, missing generated DB types, idempotency/audit gaps, and external Preview dependencies are ranked in `TECH_DEBT.md`.

- `npm.cmd run typecheck`: passed

This is recorded as an external configuration condition and was not hidden with a false-success fallback.

This PR addresses issue #7 by extracting the repeated events precondition check into a shared private helper and routing the affected entrypoints through it. The change is intentionally behavior-preserving: existing rejections still fire the same way, typed error codes remain unchanged, and there is no ABI change.

Multiple entrypoints were repeating the same precondition logic, which made the implementation harder to maintain and increased the chance of future inconsistencies. Centralizing the check keeps the logic in one place while preserving the current behavior.

Regression coverage should confirm that each existing rejection still fires identically and that edge cases remain handled correctly.

author: rdxfgxy1
body:
## Why

The installer and the new-tab update banner read **different** version sources:

- `version.json` → drives the new-tab "update available" **banner**
- `manifest.json` → the **actual extension version**, which the installer compares

Last change bumped only `version.json`, so running `install.ps1` downloaded `main` (manifest still **1.4.0**), compared it to the installed 1.4.0, and correctly reported *"already on v1.4.0 — reinstalling the same version."* The banner would also never clear, because it compares the feed to the installed manifest version, which never reached 1.5.0.

## What

Cut a proper **1.5.0** release by syncing every version-bearing file:

| File | Role | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | actual extension version (installer + banner compare) | **1.5.0** ← the fix |
| `version.json` | update-banner feed | 1.5.0 (already on main) |
| `js/whatsnew.js` | in-app "What's new" popup | 1.5.0 + new highlights |
| `doc/changelog/CHANGELOG.md` | changelog | 1.5.0 entry added |
| `version/1.5.0.md` | per-release notes | created |

1.5.0 is the release that shipped the typing assistant, grammar + AI rewrite, and the one-line installers (PR #2).

## After merge
Re-running the installer will download `main` with `manifest.json` at 1.5.0 and report `v1.4.0 -> v1.5.0`; existing installs get the banner and it clears once they update.

author: krisanselmo
body:
## Quoi

Complète les métadonnées de la page et le contenu descriptif du site. La meta description du HTML statique était vide (remplie seulement en JS à l'exécution), le titre était réduit à « Mountain GPX », les partages (réseaux sociaux, messageries) n'affichaient ni image ni description, et les 5 langues de l'interface n'existaient que côté client, sous une seule URL.

## Comment

- **`index.html`** : titre descriptif, meta description statique remplie, canonical, Open Graph + Twitter Card avec image 1200×630 (`public/og-image.png`, aux couleurs de l'app, waypoints posés sur le tracé), données structurées JSON-LD `WebApplication`, liens alternates `hreflang` fr/en/de/es/it + `x-default`.
- **Aucune URL de déploiement en dur** : `index.html` porte des placeholders `__SITE_URL__` remplis au build. `scripts/site-url.mjs` résout l'URL publique une seule fois — `SITE_URL` (env, ex. domaine personnalisé), sinon dérivée de `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` sur GitHub Actions (**un fork déploie sur `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/` sans rien configurer**), sinon le champ `homepage` de `package.json` (builds locaux).
- **Section « À propos de Mountain GPX »** repliée en bas du panneau : trois paragraphes décrivant l'outil (types de POI, imports Strava/Komoot/Garmin Connect, exports GPX/TCX, PWA hors-ligne), traduits dans les 5 langues (clés `about.*`).
- **Pages d'entrée par langue** : `scripts/build-lang-pages.mjs` (enchaîné à `npm run build`) génère `en.html`, `de.html`, `es.html`, `it.html` à la racine de `dist/` avec `lang`, titre, description, OG et canonical traduits depuis les locales, ainsi que `sitemap.xml` ; les alternates sont identiques sur chaque page. `js/i18n.js` détecte la langue de ces pages par l'URL (priorité : préférence sauvegardée > URL > langue du navigateur).
- **Préversions de PR marquées `noindex`** : plugin `noindexPreview` dans `vite.config.js`, activé par `NOINDEX_BUILD=1` dans `pr-preview.yml`, pour que les préversions ne soient pas traitées comme des doublons du site.
- **Locales** : `meta.title`/`meta.description` enrichis ; le runtime (`applyLanguage`) réapplique exactement les mêmes valeurs que le HTML statique.
- **README** : bannière, résumé en anglais, notes sur les pages de langue et la configuration de l'URL.
- **`npm audit fix`** : met à jour `fast-uri` (GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx, l'alerte Dependabot ouverte).
- Branche à jour sur `master` (inclut #14).

## Tests

- `npm test` : 47/47 ✅ dont `test/build-lang-pages.test.js` : aucun `github.io` en dur dans `index.html` source (placeholders uniquement), head complet vérifié sur une **URL de fork arbitraire**, localisation de chaque balise par `localize()`, alternates identiques sur toutes les pages, sitemap généré, et résolution d'URL (`SITE_URL` > `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` — y compris dépôt `<owner>.github.io` — > `homepage`, slash final garanti).
- Vérifié dans Chromium (Playwright) : la page racine garde son titre français, la section « À propos » est rendue et traduite, `/en.html` démarre l'app en anglais (titre, interface, sélecteur de langue) via la détection par URL.
- `npm run build` ✅ ; build avec `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=somefork/mountaingpx` → toutes les URL (canonical, OG, sitemap) suivent le fork ; build avec `NOINDEX_BUILD=1` → `noindex` présent partout.

body:
## 요약
도메인+HTTPS 브링업(PR #34) 실환경 적용 중 **ALB 프로비저닝이 `AccessDenied`로 실패**한 문제를 해결합니다. Helm 이 설치한 컨트롤러는 **v3.4.2**인데 IAM 정책은 **v2.8.2** 기준이라, 신규 권한이 없어 ALB 를 못 만들었습니다.

## 원인
Ingress `FailedDeployModel` 이벤트:
```
AccessDenied: ... not authorized to perform: ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc
AccessDenied: ... not authorized to perform: elasticloadbalancing:DescribeListenerAttributes
```
v3.4.2 는 v2.8.2 대비 `ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc`·`DescribeIpamPools`·`DescribeRouteTables`, `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeListenerAttributes`·`DescribeCapacityReservation`·`ModifyListenerAttributes`·`ModifyCapacityReservation`·`ModifyIpPools`·`SetRulePriorities` 를 추가로 요구합니다.

## 변경
- `modules/alb/iam_policy.json` — LBC **v2.8.2 → v3.4.2** 공식본으로 교체
- `modules/alb/main.tf` — 정책 버전 주석/설명 갱신, 버전 일치 필요성 명시
- `docs/domain-https-setup.md` — 브링업 중 확인한 두 함정 문서화:
  - **helm `vpcId` 필수** (노드 IMDS hop-limit=1 이라 VPC 자동탐지 실패 → 컨트롤러 CrashLoopBackOff)
  - **IAM 정책 버전 = 설치 컨트롤러 버전** 일치 필수 (불일치 시 AccessDenied)

## 적용 상태
⚠️ **이미 `terraform apply` 로 실환경 반영 완료** (dev). 코드-실환경 드리프트를 없애기 위한 사후 커밋입니다 — plan: `2 added, 0 changed, 2 destroyed`(정책 교체+재부착).

## 검증 (실환경)
- ALB 정상 생성: `k8s-victoryfairy-...elb.amazonaws.com`

author: lacraig2
body:
## Summary

Picks up the dropped **CPU-identification path** for MIPS: Penguin now recognizes Cavium **Octeon** MIPS64 SoCs and boots them on QEMU's Octeon CPU model instead of the generic one.

Octeon is a MIPS64 superset — it runs the stock `mips64{eb,el}` kernel, dylibs and ABI, but implements Cavium ASE opcodes that **fault on QEMU's generic `MIPS64R2-generic` CPU**. Previously these targets were identified as plain `mips64eb`/`mips64el` and could crash on their own instructions.

## How

- **Detection (`arch.py`)** — `_identify_mips_arch` now reads the ELF `EF_MIPS_MACH` field. pyelftools doesn't expose it, so the binutils `OCTEON` / `OCTEON2` / `OCTEON3` mask values are transcribed. A 64-bit MIPS ELF carrying the Octeon tag yields `mips64eb_octeon` / `mips64el_octeon`.
- **Registry (`arch_registry.py`)** — two new `ArchSpec`s whose every asset/subdir (arch/dylib/kmod/kernel/abi/kconf) points back at the base `mips64{eb,el}` arch, so **no new asset trees are needed** — the *only* change is `cpu → Octeon68XX`. The shipped qemu fork already implements this CPU (`target/mips/tcg/octeon_translate.c`, `-cpu Octeon68XX` = `CPU_MIPS64R2 | INSN_OCTEON`).
- **Schema** — `core.arch` Literal extended with the new canonical names + `octeon`/`octeonel` aliases (kept in sync with `arch_registry.all_names()` by the existing parity test); `docs/schema_doc.md` regenerated.

## Tests (`tests/unit/test_arch_octeon.py`, 11 cases)

Detection across all three Octeon MACH variants × both endiannesses, generic mips64 left unaffected, 32-bit-tagged ELFs stay generic (the 64-bit kernel is what needs the CPU), the asset-reuse/CPU-override invariant, alias resolution, and end-to-end `q_config` runnability (`cpu == Octeon68XX`, `machine == malta`). Full `test_config.py` + new suite: **158 passed**. flake8 clean.

## Known limitation / follow-up

`arch_id` picks the single most common arch across userspace ELFs. A firmware that mixes Octeon-tagged and generic mips64 binaries could tally to generic and miss the Octeon CPU. Real Octeon images are uniformly tagged, so this is rare; a "prefer Octeon if any Octeon ELF is present" tie-break is a reasonable follow-up if it ever bites.

🤖 Draft — reconstructed from the CPU-identification path we'd set aside.

author: lingfengmarskey
body:
Refs #91（测试中发现的真实 bug）

## 现象
同步测试时，一次较大的首次上传把 **676 条记录**放进单个 CloudKit 操作，被拒：
> your request contains 676 items which is more than the maximum number of items in a single request (400)

## 原因
`CloudKitTransport.modifyRecords` / `fetchRecords` 把整个数组直接交给单次 CloudKit 操作，未分批。CloudKit 单次操作上限 400。

## 修复
在 transport 层把输入切成 **200/批**（远低于 400）分多次操作、聚合结果——结构化记录和照片两条路径都覆盖。新增 `Array.chunked(into:)` + 测试（676→[200,200,200,76]、空/整除/非正数 size）。

## 验证
`ArrayChunkedTests` 通过；iOS 26.5 编译通过。真机大数据首次同步请对照 #111 G3 复测。

author: willemkokke
body:
A footman-native way to deliberately fail a task with a reason — the blessed
counterpart to the F2 fix (#47).

## Why

footman's failure vocabulary was implicit: `return N` (a code, no reason),
`sys.exit` (a borrowed script idiom), a raised exception (a crash). Nothing said
"fail *this task*, with a reason and a code." The downstream migration hit the
gap twice — a swallowed `sys.exit("reason")` (F2, #47), and wanting a reason
*paired with* a custom exit code, which `sys.exit` can't spell (a string arg is
always code 1).

## What

```python
from footman import task, fail

@task
def release(armed: bool = False):
    if not open_pr():
        fail("no open PR for setup — run `fm create repo` first")
    if reserved_branch():
        fail("refusing a reserved branch", code=3)
```

- `fail("reason")` → exit 1, reason rendered **verbatim** on the failure line and
  in the `--json` `error` field (rides the F2 path). `fail("reason", code=3)` →
  exit 3 with the reason. A bare `fail()` → the plain code line, no dangling
  `task:`.
- **`footman.Failed`** is exported so a task can `except footman.Failed:`.

## Why a function, not `raise Fail(...)`

The consumer-lint decision. A task lives in *your* repo under *your* ruff, and
`raise SomeError("literal")` trips **`EM101`** (flake8-errmsg) and **`TRY003`**
(tryceratops) at the call site, every failure. A function call trips neither —
the same reason `sys.exit()` and `pytest.fail()` are functions. A lint smoke
test guards the property directly.

## Details

- Plain `Exception` (not `BaseException`), so `parallel()` collects and re-raises
  it — a `fail()` inside a thunk surfaces its reason at the task level (better
  than the `sys.exit`-in-parallel corner).
- `Failed` takes no `Error` suffix, matching the house convention: a deliberate
  control-flow outcome (`RunFailed`, `Unavailable`, `NotConfirmed`), not a
  mistake (`ChainError`, `RegistrationError`).
- A shared `context._is_deliberate_stop` predicate keeps `fail()` and
  `sys.exit("…")` rendering in step.
- The stdlib idioms (`return N`, `sys.exit`, raising) all keep working.

Docs: a new *"Failing a task"* section in `orchestration.md`, autodoc in
`api.md`. Gate green, coverage 93.56%, strict docs build clean.

author: thesherwood
body:
Continues the owner-agreed serving-cluster order (JIT serve loop + I41 merged in #427). The multi-consumer rung, pinned on the tree-walk oracle first — it turned into three connected pieces, because hammering the semantics surfaced two real problems.

## 1. Multi-consumer `svc.wait` (I39's top rung)

`Sched::svc_waiters` is now multi-waiter per domain key: N spawned server vCPUs can park on one domain queue. The old single-slot map silently **displaced** a second parker — dropping a live vCPU, a latent hang for any svc+threads module on the oracle. A wake re-admits **all** of a domain's parked consumers (deliberately boring: the wake path knows only the domain key, never which vCPU owns a parked handler; admission stays race-free under the powerbox lock and spurious wakers re-park via the rewound op).

## 2. Timed `svc.wait` (the I38 sketch, pulled in as this rung's prerequisite)

The first test draft hung: consumers **work-steal** (any sibling may serve every dispatch), so a spare consumer in an untimed wait can never exit — stranding the domain's `thread.join`s. Op 10 now takes an optional single arg (timeout in ns; `< 0`/absent = forever, today's form byte-identical): the park registers a deadline in a new `svc_timers` heap; a fire re-admits the consumer with `Pending::SvcTimeout`, and the rewound op admits anything that raced the timer, then returns its count (0 on a pure timeout) instead of re-parking. Oracle-only: `serve_qualifies` and the bytecode compile veto treat the timed form as a park seam; the JIT cap-thunk intercept lets it fall through to the generic probeable `-EINVAL`.

## 3. A pre-existing settle/park TOCTOU (slice 5b), found by the hammer

The serve settle was two-step: reply-wake miss (caller not parked yet), scheduler lock released, then the completion-cell insert under a separate powerbox lock. A caller parking exactly in between probed the cell empty, entered `ticket_waiters`, and was never woken — stranded forever with its reply sitting in the cell. Multi-consumer widened the window but the race is reachable single-consumer too. Fix: `Scheduler::cap_reply_or_stash` — wake-or-stash under **one** scheduler lock (scheduler→powerbox order, matching the park handler and fiber early-probe), used at all three settle sites; the now-dead two-step `cap_reply` is removed.

## Tests (`svm-interp/tests/svc_multi_consumer.rs`)

- Two pollers split one queue concurrently: counts sum to the dispatch count, pure-handler completion cells exact; svc+threads still declines on the fast backends (pinned).
- A pure timed-wait timeout returns 0; the fast entry declines the module and falls back identically.
- Two timed-`svc.wait` consumers inside a §14 serving child serve a live caller's `add`/`add`/`finish` sequence with a done-flag wind-down, across repeated interleavings — hammered 60× clean where the old map/race hung within ~5 runs.

Full workspace tests (1675), fmt, and clippy `-D warnings` green. ISSUES.md I38/I39 and TODO.md updated with the as-built.

author: pooyagolchian
body:
Makes SpecForge multi-agent while keeping its differentiator — the **enforced** approval gate — real on every target. Builds M1 (the engine) + M2 (GitHub Copilot as the first non-Claude agent).

## Why
SpecForge was Claude-Code-only. Its whole pitch is *"approval is enforced, not hoped for."* Verified research (2026-07) showed every target agent (Copilot, Gemini, Cursor, Codex) has since shipped a real pre-tool hook — so the enforced gate can **travel**, which is exactly what spec-kit leaves advisory. This PR proves that end-to-end on Copilot and lays the generator so the rest are near-free.

## M1 — neutral-source generator + byte-parity
- `workflow/steps/*.md` — one agent-neutral source for all 15 lifecycle commands.
- `tools/gen_agents.py` + `tools/adapters/claude.py` — renders **every** agent, Claude included, from that source.
- **CI byte-parity gate** (`tests/parity.test.sh`, wired into `validate.yml`): all 15 Claude skills regenerate byte-identical to the committed plugin; plus `decide.sh`-copy and step/skill-count drift guards. Proven non-vacuous (tampering a committed artifact fails CI).
- `workflow/gate/decide.sh` — the gate decision extracted transport-agnostic (exit 0 allow / exit 10 deny / any other exit = fail **open**).

## M2 — GitHub Copilot, fully enforced
- 15 `/specforge.*` prompt files + `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, generated (`tools/adapters/copilot.py`).
- `workflow/adapters/copilot-gate.sh` — a real `preToolUse` shim + `.github/hooks/specforge.json`; blocks unapproved edits, **fail-open**.
- `workflow/gate/pre-commit` — an **agent-independent** git backstop (fires regardless of which AI made the edit), fail-open.
- `dist/agents/copilot/install.sh` — installs the bundle + pre-commit into a user repo (no-clobber; backs up existing hooks/instructions).
- **End-to-end proof** (`tests/e2e-copilot.test.sh`, 11/11): install → hook denies an unapproved edit → a *real `git commit` is blocked* → `fasttrack` unblocks both layers.

## Enforcement model (honest)
| Agent | Edit-time | Commit-time |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `PreToolUse` hook (full, flagship) | pre-commit backstop |
| GitHub Copilot | `preToolUse` shim — *preview*; CLI/coding-agent expected-full pending verification vs Copilot's live hook API; VS Code inline behind `chat.useCustomAgentHooks` | pre-commit backstop |

The gate is **in-repo** ("keep an honest workflow honest," not a hostile-agent defense) — documented in `docs/gates.md`. No CI-gate workflow for user repos is claimed (none ships).

## Quality
- Every task went through spec+quality review with fix loops; a final whole-branch review confirmed **fail-open holds at all four enforcement points**, **no Claude regression** (byte-identical skills + unchanged `hooks.json`), and the drift net works.
- **82 tests pass** across 8 suites. Release **v0.4.0** (plugin.json == CHANGELOG).

## Deferred (by design)
Gemini/Cursor/Codex adapters (generator-ready, on-demand) and spec-kit's `checklist`/`converge` steps — see the design spec.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-multi-agent-support-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-23-multi-agent-support.md`

body:
## Summary

The registry core from [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-unified-technology-request-registry.md): requests become first-class rows with durable identity across origins, an audit trail, and the link/claim substrate the matching and ROI-aggregation phases build on.

**Migration 018** (applied to dev already):
- `tech_requests` — one row per request from any origin (`tdx` / `clickup` / `site-submission` / `direct`), with per-origin idempotent upsert keys, track/stage/disposition routing state, and decision fields. Origin is CHECKed (structural); process vocabularies are deliberately un-CHECKed and owned by `lib/utr.ts` (006/007/008 pattern).
- `tech_request_events` — append-only audit trail.
- `tech_request_links` + `tech_request_project_links` — the request↔request and request↔project graph (project side is a soft slug key, surviving portfolio re-seeds per ADR 0004 §1).
- `roi_claims` — the ROI ledger (subject = project slug or request FK; dimension/source/status vocabularies in `lib/utr.ts`).
- Idempotent backfill: existing ClickUp backlog rows + site submissions (incl. the GEO/Scrunch evaluation records) join the registry with `received` events.

**Ongoing ingestion**: `lib/clickup-sync.ts` upserts registry rows per backlog task (registry rows persist when upstream deletes — memory, not a mirror); the submissions POST route files new assessments in (best-effort, never breaks the submitter flow).

**`lib/utr.ts`**: typed UTR vocabulary — tracks (moved from `governance-profile`, which re-exports for existing consumers), per-track stages from the process deck, dispositions (incl. `routed-to-existing` for the "existing solution meets need" outcome), origins, event/link types, ROI dimensions.

**`/internal/requests`**: the unified queue — origin, requestor, per-origin signal (ClickUp rubric score / site tier), track (— until UTR triage runs), disposition. Internal-only: submission content and requestor names have no public-visibility decision yet (flagged in ADR 0005). `/portfolio/pipeline` is unchanged.

## Verification

- `npm run build` — clean.
- Migration applied against dev: 3 site submissions backfilled with audit events (`clickup_requests` was empty in the dev snapshot; the next host-cron sync populates ClickUp rows through the new path).
- `/internal/requests` verified authed in the browser: stat cards + queue render (GEO evaluation, Tier 2, open · etc.).
- Note for deploy: dev deploys don't run migrations — 018 is already applied to the dev DB, so the container just needs the code.

body:
요청하신 대로 **PDF를 캡처(스크린샷)로 만들지 않고, 브라우저 내장 PDF 엔진(네이티브 인쇄)으로 진짜 글자·벡터 PDF를 생성**하도록 전면 전환했습니다. 각 챕터가 한 페이지씩 차지합니다.

## 왜 바꿨나
기존 `html2canvas` 캡처 방식은 (1) 글자가 이미지라 흐릿하고 확대 시 깨지며, (2) 용량이 크고, (3) 모바일 캔버스 한계로 백지가 나오는 근본 한계가 있었습니다.

## 어떻게 바꿨나
- `downloadReportPDF`: 데이터에서 책을 조판해 `#bookPDF`에 넣고, `@media print` CSS로 챕터별 페이지 나눔·색상 보존·페이지 프레임을 처리한 뒤 **`window.print()`** 호출. html2canvas·jsPDF·캔버스 슬라이싱을 전부 제거.
- **인쇄 CSS**(`body.printbook` 스코프로 일반 인쇄와 분리):
  - **챕터별 한 페이지**: 표지 · 각 진단 섹션(진단개요/백분위/영역별성취/오답정밀분석/학습처방) · 부록 표지 · 각 개념 강의가 새 페이지에서 시작.
  - 오답 카드는 흐르며 페이지를 채우되, 원문 이미지·표·동형문제 박스는 통째로 유지(중간에서 안 쪼개짐).
  - 모든 인쇄 페이지에 금박 이중 프레임(`position:fixed`) 반복.
- 결과: **글자 선명·선택 가능**, 용량 대폭 감소, **iOS 캔버스 백지 문제 없음**. 버튼을 누르면 인쇄 창이 뜨고 "PDF로 저장"을 선택합니다(아이폰: 공유 → 파일에 저장).
- 더 이상 쓰지 않는 캡처 코드(`ensurePdfLibs`/`loadScriptOnce`/`pdfBreakYs`/`pdfAtomics`/`pdfForceBreaks`) 제거.

## 검증
- Chromium 네이티브 엔진(`page.pdf()` — `window.print()`→PDF저장과 동일)으로 생성한 PDF에서 **한글이 실제 텍스트로 추출됨을 확인**(캡처였다면 불가능).
- 표지·진단 섹션·오답 카드·부록 표지·강의 전 페이지 육안 확인(pymupdf 렌더링). 챕터별 페이지·금박 프레임·색상·동형문제 정답 강조 모두 정상.
- `tests/final-score.js` 13/13, `tests/final-submit-sync.js` 12/12, `tests/wrongbook-assets.py` PASS, JS 문법 정상.

## 사용 흐름 변화(참고)
자동 다운로드 대신 **인쇄 창 → "PDF로 저장"** 방식입니다(네이티브 벡터 PDF를 얻는 유일한 브라우저 내 방법). 아이폰 사파리는 인쇄 미리보기에서 공유 → "파일에 저장"으로 PDF가 저장됩니다.

author: xerhab
body:
## Problem

Cues never appeared in a live session or in history against the production model, despite the gateway returning clean `200`s.

Diagnosed from the running deployment's logs:

1. First blocker (already fixed on the deploy side): the LiteLLM key was scoped to `models=['parakeet']`, so cue calls for `qwen3-llm` got `403 Forbidden`.
2. After the key was widened, calls returned `200` but **still no cue**. Root cause: `qwen3-llm` (Qwen3.6-27B) is a **reasoning model**. With thinking on it spends the whole `max_tokens` budget on chain-of-thought returned in `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty with `finish_reason: length`. `OpenAICueGenerator` parsed the empty `content`, found no JSON, and silently returned `None` on every finalized turn — so cues were dropped without any error surfacing (cue failures are swallowed by design so captions never stall).

Confirmed with a live A/B against the deployed gateway:

| Variant | `finish_reason` | `content` |
|---|---|---|
| thinking on (current) | `length` | `None` |
| thinking disabled | `stop` | `{"cue": true, "title": "Sun-Earth Distance", "body": "…"}` |

## Fix

- Disable thinking for cue calls via `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking = false` (LiteLLM forwards it to vLLM), so the JSON answer lands in `content` and the call finishes cleanly. Cues want fast structured output, not reasoning.
- Response extraction now falls back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty and tolerates a `null` `content`.
- New setting `API_CUE_DISABLE_THINKING` (default `true`) so a deploy can turn this off for a non-reasoning model whose chat template rejects the kwarg.
- Extracted a pure `_build_payload` and `_message_content` so the previously-uncovered network method's logic is unit-tested.

## Tests

- New regression tests in `api/tests/test_cue_backends.py`: payload disables thinking by default (and omits it when off), and `_message_content` falls back to `reasoning_content` / tolerates `null`.
- Full API suite: **196 passed, coverage 96.77%** (gate 85%).

## Verification

Exercised the actual fixed request path against the **live** gateway from the deployed API container:

- "How far away is the sun…" → `{cue,title,body}`, `finish_reason: stop`
- "My favourite pokemon is number 133." → real cue
- "uh yeah so anyway" → correctly no cue

No client/UI changes — this is entirely in the cue model call, so web/mobile parity is unaffected.
