author: matthewlacerda2
body:
Closes #353.

## What changed

Adds **`Debug.Preview(asset_path, out_png [, opts])`** — a dev-only Lua verb that renders an asset in the isolated #352 preview scene and writes a PNG, **headlessly**.

```lua
-- bake -> preview -> look -> iterate, in one line
local png = Debug.Preview(Shader.Bake(recipe), "out/preview.png")
Debug.Preview("project/assets/brick.png", "out/brick.png", { mesh = "cube", resolution = 256 })
```

- **Previewable kinds** are the three file-backed ones the Inspector tab accepts, dispatched on extension: models (`gltf`/`glb`/`obj`/`fbx`), textures (`png`/`tga`/`jpg`/`jpeg`), shaders (`wgsl`). See *Scope* below on material assets.
- **Options:** `mesh` (`"sphere"` default / `"cube"` / `"suzanne"`, ignored for models) and `resolution` (default 512, clamped 16–4096). Square output; parent dirs created.
- **Errors on caller mistakes** (missing path, unpreviewable extension, misspelled mesh) so a typo can't return a plausible picture of empty sky. Returns `nil` — not an error — when the machine has no GPU/software adapter, matching `screenshot`'s graceful-degradation contract so a GPU-less CI box still runs.
- `docs/scripting-api.md` updated in lockstep (the #280 drift gate passes).

### Architecture — one preview machinery, not two

The preview scene builder and camera rig lived under `src/editor/inspector/`, so a headless capture would have had to reach into the **egui UI tree** to render a preview — and the next agent would have copied that. They move to a neutral top-level **`src/preview/`**, leaving `editor/inspector/preview.rs` as a thin egui front-end. Supporting changes:

- `OrbitState::apply_input` takes plain scalars instead of an `egui::Vec2`, so the rig honours "keep egui decoupled".
- The extension→subject dispatch moves there too, so both front-ends accept exactly the same asset kinds **by construction** rather than via two `match` arms kept in sync by hand.

Framing is **fixed** (`OrbitState::default`) rather than parameterised: orbit/zoom is the human affordance, while an agent needs two shots of one asset to be diffable pixel-for-pixel.

### Fix: off-origin models previewed as empty sky

Found by *looking at the output*, which is the point of the feature. The preview camera always orbits the world origin, but subjects were spawned at `Vec3::ZERO` and kept whatever offset they were authored with. The engine's own bundled Suzanne sits around `(-2.5, 1.3, 4.1)`, so **the "Suzanne" toggle and any off-origin model rendered empty sky — in the editor tab too, since #352.** Subjects now spawn at the negation of their bounds centre, with multi-part models sharing one offset so their internal layout survives. Covered by a regression test.

### Dedup: one texture readback

`dev/screenshot.rs` and `render/ibl/cubemap_capture.rs` each carried a copy of the padded-row `copy_texture_to_buffer` dance, and this needed a third. New **`render::readback`** owns it once. The alignment rule it encodes silently skews images at any width that isn't a multiple of 64 — exactly the kind of thing that should exist in one place. Net negative lines.

## Why we want it

The authoring loop was **write-only for the agent** in the place that matters most: shaders. `Shader.Bake` proves a `.wgsl` compiles (#272); nothing showed what it *renders* short of assembling a whole scene. This closes **bake → preview → look → iterate** headlessly, which is the engine's whole premise — and it is pure agentic-development leverage, hence **infrastructure**. One surface, three callers: the console REPL and bot-players get the same verb for free.

The refactor is the other half of the value: without it there would be two preview scenes, and the agent-facing one would drift from what the human reviews.

## Effect

An agent can now see any model/texture/shader on disk without building a scene. The editor's Preview tab is unchanged in behaviour except that **Suzanne and off-origin models now actually show up**. No engine capability is removed; nothing outside the dev feature grows.

## Scope note

**Material assets** are listed in #353's accept-list but have no on-disk file — they live in `Scene::materials` and the editor gets them from the component card, so there is no path to pass to a path-based verb. The three file-backed kinds are implemented; a key-based verb for materials would be a separate, deliberate addition. Flagged as a comment on the issue rather than silently dropped.

## Verification

- **Rendered previews through the real session REPL against a software adapter and looked at them** — sphere, Suzanne and model arms all render lit and correctly framed (this is how the off-origin bug surfaced).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings -D clippy::too_many_lines` — clean on **both** feature sets.
- `cargo test` and `cargo test --features dev` — full suite green.
- Size gate `lint: ok`, determinism guard `determinism: ok`, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- New tests: dispatch parity, resolution clamp, caller-error paths, the off-origin recentring regression, deterministic-framing guard, and `tests/preview_api.rs` driving the verb through a live `Session`.

One incidental commit: `assets/models/suzanne.obj.meta`, the sidecar for an engine-bundled asset that is now regenerated by every test run — untracked, it dirties every working tree. Project-asset sidecars carry user-authored collider settings, so blanket-ignoring `*.meta` would be wrong.

author: alexklimaj
body:
## Summary

The low/high eRPM levels that bound the low-rpm throttle restriction were computed as `motor_kv / N / (32 / motor_poles)`, which is wrong in two ways inherited from upstream v2.20 ([am32-firmware/AM32#405](https://github.com/am32-firmware/AM32/issues/405)):

1. **The high-level divisor is `12`, where it had historically been `17`** (changed upstream in `eef9cb45`). That raises the eRPM at which full duty is released by ~1.42x, so a motor configured with its *real* kV stays inside the restricted-duty region far longer than intended and never reaches full thrust. The known community workaround — entering 50-60% of the actual motor kV — cancels exactly this factor.

2. **`32 / motor_poles` is integer division evaluated first**, so the pole term is truncated (2 instead of 2.29 for a 14-pole motor) and collapses to 0 above 32 poles. The existing zero guard turned that into an envelope of `0/0`, which `map()` reads as "always at the high-rpm limit" — silently *removing* the restriction for high pole counts rather than scaling it.

## Changes

`Src/settings.c` — one hunk. Multiply before dividing so the pole ratio keeps its precision, and restore the `17` divisor:

```c
if (eepromBuffer.motor_poles >= 2 && eepromBuffer.motor_poles <= 64) {
    low_rpm_level  = ((uint32_t)motor_kv * eepromBuffer.motor_poles) / (100U * 32U);
    high_rpm_level = ((uint32_t)motor_kv * eepromBuffer.motor_poles) / (17U  * 32U);
} else {
    low_rpm_level = 0;
    high_rpm_level = 0;
}
```

The pole-count guard is kept, now as an explicit `2..64` range check (the bounds the DroneCAN `MOTOR_POLES` parameter accepts). Multiply-before-divide removes the divide-by-zero on its own, but it also changes what an *erased* eeprom does: `motor_poles == 0xff` would otherwise yield `high_rpm_level = 937` kerpm for a 2000kV config, pegging duty at `throttle_max_at_low_rpm` (~20%) forever. The range check preserves today's unrestricted fallback for `0` and `0xff`.

## Effect

| kV / poles | old low/high | new low/high |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2000 / 14 | 10 / **83** | 8 / **51** |
| 3000 / 14 | 15 / 125 | 13 / 77 |
| 2000 / 48 | 0 / **0** (unrestricted) | 30 / 176 |
| any / 0 or 255 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (unchanged) |

Max computed value across the full input domain is 1202, so no `uint16_t` overflow.

**Behavior change worth flagging:** the 33-64 pole rows move in the *stricter* direction — those configs currently get no low-rpm restriction at all, which was accidental. Uncommon, and `low_rpm_throttle_limit` is already disabled below 300kV, but it is a real difference from shipped behavior.

## Verification

- `make AM32_SITL_CAN` and `make ARK_4IN1_F051` both build clean under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
- F051 flash went **down** 24 bytes (24996 → 24972); a runtime division is removed. That target sits at 91% of its budget, so this was checked explicitly.
- Full SITL suite: **29 passed**. No existing test touches `rpm_level` — this is bench/flight-verifiable behavior, not covered by CI.
- `make format` per `AGENTS.md`. It also reformatted four unrelated `Mcu/` files with pre-existing drift; those were reverted to keep the diff scoped.

Draft pending bench confirmation that max thrust is restored with the real motor kV configured.

author: zardus
body:
THIS MESSAGE WAS GENERATED BY AN AUTOMATED PROCESS

## Draft validation status

This PR is not ready to merge. Retrospective review found a correctness bug in the published head: the FPSCR matcher keeps only the last definition of each temporary in a block prefix. If a temporary is copied and then redefined, an earlier alias can be resolved to the later value and the decompiler can emit a comparison with the wrong operands.

The original 252-function A/B result below was also too narrow to establish corpus safety. Only 134 cases contained `CmpF`, all came from three Cortex-M projects, and the run omitted most of the 1,158 public ARM DecBench functions whose saved output contains `CmpF`. It had no broad integer-only or cross-architecture control population.

A local correction uses statement-indexed reaching definitions and moves the new matcher from expression-wide dispatch to a conditional-jump optimizer. That correction has not been pushed. This PR will remain a draft until the corrected implementation passes the expanded gate described below.

## Intended change

libVEX represents ARM VFP comparisons as a `CmpF` result that is transformed into FPSCR flags and then tested as an integer condition. The existing peephole recognizes only one narrow, already-propagated topology, so real decompilations often retain repeated `CmpF(...)` calls and FPSCR arithmetic.

The proposed matcher evaluates the exact encoding over greater-than, equal, less-than, and unordered outcomes, then emits the corresponding floating-point AIL comparison. Predicates that include unordered values retain an explicit negation; integer complement rules such as `!(a > b) == a <= b` are invalid for NaNs.

The relevant architecture scope is ARMEL, ARMHF, and ARMCortexM. It is not restricted by operating system.

## Preliminary evidence

At baseline `91cc026062142cf8dbbbefbb6c5aacd7f09f54f7` versus published candidate `c761153b651fff42d55dc345c420cef6ff093c82`:

| Cohort | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful functions | 252/252 | 252/252 |
| Failures / timeouts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| `CmpF` calls | 4,176 | 2,358 |
| Functions containing `CmpF` | 134 | 72 |
| Maximum elapsed time | 30.42s | 29.75s |

These numbers show that the matcher fires, but they are not a regression gate and should not be read as merge-readiness evidence.

## Required validation before ready for review

- Add a regression for temporary reassignment and prove that aliases use the definition that reaches them.
- Test every representable predicate over greater-than, equal, less-than, and unordered outcomes, plus malformed, cyclic, unknown, and unrepresentable expressions that must fail closed.
- Run current master against the corrected candidate over the full 250-function public DecBench sample, all public ARM `CmpF` functions, all public cross-architecture `CmpF` functions, and integer-only controls.
- Review every generated-code, structure, and type delta against source ground truth; accept no unexplained degradation.
- Repeat paired cold-process timings and compare failures, five-minute timeouts, median, p95, maximum, and peak RSS.
- Pass the complete angr workspace gate on the exact candidate and dependency revisions.

CI on the published head is useful but does not replace this corpus validation.

author: lance0
body:
Four independent defects an operator hits in the first hour, found by
running the software. Each one failed quietly: nothing errored, and every
rustbgpd surface reported healthy.

## `rbgp doctor` could not write its bundle in the container image

The lean image's working directory is `/`, which its nonroot user cannot
write, and doctor defaulted the bundle to
`./rustbgpd-doctor-<ts>.tar.gz` — so the tool the README and QUICKSTART
name for bug reports exited 1 with a bare `Permission denied (os error
13)`, naming neither the file, the path, nor the flag that fixes it.

Without `--output` the bundle now goes to the first writable of: the
working directory (unchanged wherever it already worked), the daemon's
`runtime_state_dir`, the temp directory. The state dir is preferred over
the temp dir because the operator already has it mounted and it survives
a container restart; the image itself is left alone. Independently, a
bundle that still cannot be written now names the target path and points
at `--output`, and the same bare-errno shape on `--token-file` now names
the file it could not read.

## `already_advertised` explain claimed the peer was in sync

The gate read `identical route already advertised — peer is in sync`.
rustbgpd knows what it advertised; BGP carries no acceptance signal, so
it cannot know what the remote accepted. A peer that treats every UPDATE
as withdrawn per RFC 7606 stays Established holding zero routes while
that line reads "in sync" — which is exactly the FRR case below. The
unicast, VPN, and labeled-unicast rungs, the `rbgp rib advertised
--explain` summary line, the proto field comment, and the Rust field
docs now scope the claim to local Adj-RIB-Out state and say that remote
acceptance is not observable. The rib explain test pins the anti-
overclaim alongside its existing code/flag assertions.

## Cookbooks gave an FRR fix that does not work

FRR 10.x enables `enforce-first-as` by default and rejects RFC
7947-transparent route-server updates. Both `docs/cookbook/route-server.md`
and `docs/cookbook/route-server-migration.md` gave the relaxation without
saying it must be per-neighbor; the global `no bgp enforce-first-as` alone
is insufficient in FRR 10.3.1, which `docs/INTEROP.md` and the M19/M83
interop configs already recorded. Both pages now give
`no neighbor <route-server> enforce-first-as` and state the failure mode:
FRR treat-as-withdraws rather than resetting, so the session stays
Established, the member holds zero routes, and neither side logs an
error. Those two cookbook sites were the only operator-facing occurrences
of the global form.

## Alice-LG adapter served a fabricated preferred-route count

`examples/birdwatcher-adapter` emitted an unconditional `"preferred": 0`
on `/protocols/bgp`, so a looking glass showed every member with zero
preferred routes regardless of the Loc-RIB. The gRPC surface has no
per-peer Loc-RIB best count: `ListBestRoutes` is global (it ignores
`neighbor_address`) and `NeighborState` does not carry one, so deriving
the number means paging the entire Loc-RIB and tallying
`Route.peer_address` on every poll of an endpoint Alice-LG hits per
refresh — a full-table walk per poll at IXP scale. The field is omitted
rather than served wrong, and the README records the omission and the
condition that would let it be served. `imported`, `filtered`, and
`exported` are unchanged.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and `cargo doc
--workspace --no-deps` all exit 0. Checked-in shell completions were
regenerated for the changed `--output` help text.

author: mcif-test
body:
…o overlap

From three phone screenshots: the app was magnified and scrolled sideways with the header cut off mid-logo, the account button was off-screen entirely, the "Scan more commenters" button was printed on top of the investigation label, and the title had collapsed to two characters per line ("Ba" / "I...") with its URL rendered as "htt...".

Root cause of the zoom, and the least obvious part: the shared Input is 14px. iOS Safari magnifies the whole page when you focus a control under 16px and does not zoom back out, so one tap on the search box left the app permanently magnified — and once magnified it can be panned, which is what put the header half off-screen. Form controls are now 16px on touch screens. Deliberately NOT fixed by disabling pinch-zoom: people who need to magnify text must still be able to.

- html/body get overflow-x: clip (hidden as the pre-Safari-16 fallback). clip rather than hidden because hidden creates a scroll container and breaks the sticky topbar. Wide content already scrolls inside its own container; nothing drags the document any more.
- The topbar held six items in a non-wrapping row and simply pushed the last one past the right edge. Service health and the duplicate alerts link are now tablet-up (phones reach alerts from the tab bar and already get a full-width degraded banner), and the row can no longer overflow.
- The investigation hero put a ~250px shrink-0 action cluster beside a flex-1 min-w-0 text column, so on a phone the text column collapsed to almost nothing and the non-wrapping section label spilled out and painted under the button. It stacks on mobile now.
- .section-label is inline-flex, so it would not shrink below its content — it now wraps instead of overflowing, wherever it is used.
- touch-action: manipulation drops Safari's ~300ms double-tap-zoom wait that made every button feel dead.
- "Compile commenters" was breaking mid-phrase across two lines with the icon stranded; the Paste button is icon-only on phones so the placeholder stays readable at the new 16px.

Verified in Chromium at 360/375/390/430px rather than by eye: no page can be panned sideways, the account button lands inside the viewport (347/360 at the narrowest), label and button no longer intersect, the title occupies ~80% of viewport width instead of ~8%, inputs compute to 16px, and the compile button is one line. Public routes re-checked at all four widths. Typecheck, lint and build clean.

body:
Implementa a Calculadora de ROI NGI descrita no PRD: ferramenta PLG self-serve que converte "economizamos milhões dos nossos clientes" em **"você economizaria R$ X por ano"**, capturando e qualificando leads por budget.

## Não toca nas automações existentes

O diff é **38 arquivos, todos adições**, todos dentro de `calculadora-roi/`. Nenhum script Python, nenhum workflow do GitHub Actions e nenhum arquivo na raiz foram alterados — as automações Meta → Odoo → DataCrazy continuam idênticas.

```
$ git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c
     38 A
$ git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -v '^calculadora-roi/' | wc -l
     0
```

## Motor de cálculo primeiro

Como o PRD exige, nada de UI antes das fórmulas passarem. `src/lib/calc.ts` é puro, determinístico e sem I/O, implementando a seção 5.2. **57 testes Vitest** travam as regras que sustentam a credibilidade do número numa call:

- Uplift de receita **nunca** entra na economia — há teste explícito garantindo que informar faturamento não altera nenhuma das economias
- A soma do breakdown por canal reconcilia com o custo anual total
- Payback é `null` quando não há economia recorrente positiva (sem "Infinity meses")
- Nenhum input produz `NaN` — zeros, negativos, texto vindo da URL
- Economia negativa é exibida como é, sem maquiagem

## Produto

- Wizard de 4 passos, cálculo em tempo real, defaults por setor em todos os campos (nenhum campo obrigatório no início)
- Estado do cenário na URL + rota `/calculadora/[shareId]` para o cenário salvo
- Resultado parcial livre; blur/lock nos cards de breakdown por canal, projeção de 3 anos e uplift de receita
- Gate de e-mail **depois** do valor, nunca antes
- Narrativa via Claude API com timeout de 8s e fallback estático por setor — a IA recebe os resultados prontos e nunca calcula
- Relatório com a marca em `/api/pdf`
- Mobile-first, tema escuro, títulos em caixa alta, resultado como número dominante

## Infra

- Benchmarks lidos da tabela `benchmarks` do Supabase (editáveis sem deploy) com fallback local
- Lead scoring Tier A/B/C conforme a régua do PRD, com alerta de Tier A no Slack e `detalhe` da nota para o BDR entender o porquê
- `supabase/schema.sql` com tabelas, índices, RLS (benchmarks público somente-leitura; calculos/leads/eventos só via service role) e rotina LGPD de exclusão por e-mail
- Os 7 eventos do funil no GTM já implantado (`GTM-TSGKH6D2`), incluindo o evento de MQL
- Rate limit por IP, honeypot, verificação de origem, consentimento LGPD explícito e disclaimer visível
- Todos os tokens de marca isolados em `src/app/tokens.css`

## Verificação

- `npm run test` — 57/57 passando
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — limpo
- `npx next build` — build de produção OK
- Smoke test no servidor: cenário automotivo padrão devolve R$ 1.344.900 de economia anual, conferido à mão (1.483.500 tradicional − 138.600 NGI recorrente)

## Pendências bloqueantes antes do launch

Documentadas no README e marcadas no código — a ferramenta **não deve ir ao ar** sem elas:

1. **Benchmarks de custo** (`src/lib/benchmarks.ts` e o seed do schema) são placeholders conservadores, não validados pelo time da Sétima. Precisam de backtest contra 2-3 projetos reais.
2. **Tokens de marca** (`src/app/tokens.css`) são placeholders derivados do registro visual da LP — o CSS do site está minificado e nenhum hex foi confirmado. Trocar esse único arquivo resolve o visual inteiro.

author: jonnyeclectic
body:
## Why

The out-of-cwd ASK gate (section 3) iterated **every** path operand of a mutating command. But `cp`/`install` copy **from** a source **into** a destination, and `ln` links a target name into a new link — their leading operands are **reads**, not writes. The section explicitly lets reads outside cwd pass ("Reads (cat/grep/ls) outside cwd pass"), yet gating the source operand made

```sh
cp -R "$HOME/.cache/pre-commit" "$TMPDIR/pc-cache"
```

ask for manual approval — for the cache dir it only **reads**, copying into scratch.

## What

Add `write_targets(cmd, tokens)`: for `cp`/`install`/`ln` the write target is just the **destination** — the value of `-t`/`--target-directory` if present, else the last non-flag operand. Every other mutator keeps gating **all** operands. The out-of-cwd write to the destination is still gated for all of them.

`mv` is deliberately **not** copy-like: it **removes** its sources, so an out-of-cwd source there is a genuine mutation and still asks.

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cp "$HOME/.cache/x" "$TMPDIR/y"` (read ext → scratch) | **ask** ❌ | allow |
| `cp /ext/src "$TMPDIR/dst"` | **ask** ❌ | allow |
| `install -m755 /ext/tool "$TMPDIR/t"` | **ask** ❌ | allow |
| `ln -s /ext/target ./link` | **ask** ❌ | allow |
| `cp ./local /outside/dest` (write out) | ask | ask |
| `install -m755 ./tool /usr/local/bin/tool` | ask | ask |
| `mv /ext/src "$TMPDIR/dst"` (source removed) | ask | ask |
| `cp ./a ./b` (inside cwd) | allow | allow |

Reworded the message `touches` → `writes to` to match what's now gated.

## Tests

+11 (**132 total**, `make check` green) in `TestCopyReadsSource`, covering every row above plus `cp -t <scratch> /ext/src` (allow) and `cp -t /ext/dir ./a` (ask). Uses explicit `/opt/...` paths for "outside" since the test's own `$HOME` is a scratch temp dir.

Version bumped **0.2.4 → 0.2.5** so installed sessions refresh onto the fix.

author: davisdelivery
body:
## Chad was right

The challenge — *"next week multiple hyperscalers are reporting, so they should be in there"* — is correct, and my previous "it's just an earnings lull" conclusion was wrong.

Measured on prod at the same moment:

| source | result |
|---|---|
| bulk calendar range | earliest entry **2026-08-10** |
| per-symbol calendar | **MSFT 07-29 (5d), META 07-29 (5d), AMZN 07-30 (6d), AAPL 07-30 (6d)** |
| published snapshot | **all four absent** |

The bulk range **under-reports the front of the calendar without announcing it** — it returns a healthy-looking ~400 entries whose earliest date is weeks out.

## Where my reasoning failed

I treated *"the feed returned data"* as *"the feed returned complete data."* The `days=30 → 104 setups` result I used to disprove the gating theory is **equally consistent with a truncated feed**, so it proved nothing. A sanity check against domain knowledge (mega-caps report in late July) would have caught it immediately; a per-symbol cross-check did.

Control for the obvious objection: the probe returns **NVDA 2026-08-26** — genuinely-distant dates come back distant, so it isn't fabricating near-term entries.

## The fix, with both guards from the failed attempt

1. **Never probe when the range call itself failed.** The earlier version fired 33 probes into an active 429 storm; the run died in 4 seconds and the publish guard refused to publish. More calls cannot fix a rate limit.
2. **`getUpcomingEarnings` now paces through the Finnhub token bucket** with bounded retries instead of a bare `fetch()`. That unthrottled fan-out was the storm's actual source — and it made *every* caller of that function unsafe, not just this one.

Coverage is honestly partial (core watchlist, not the full universe) and the snapshot records a warning saying so whenever the gap is detected. The empty-window UX from #159 is retained for genuine lulls.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · `vite build` clean · full suite **1988 passing** (5 tests pin the measured contract, including the never-probe-into-a-429 guard)

Post-merge: trigger a scan and confirm MSFT/META/AMZN/AAPL appear in the 7-day window.

author: robertn702
body:
## Problem

Config lookup prefiltered on exact `domain === hostname` (www-stripped) **before** urlPattern matching ran, so a config keyed to its registrable domain never served its own `*.host` urlPattern. The seeded Reddit config (`domain: reddit.com`, `urlPatterns: [*://*.reddit.com/*]`) returned **zero** tools on `old.reddit.com` / `sh.reddit.com`.

## Fix

Added `domainLookupKeys(hostname)` to `packages/schema` — expands a hostname into its candidate `domain` keys (full host + each parent down to the naive last-two-label registrable domain; www-strip + lowercase; no public-suffix-list dependency). Both prefilter sites widen candidates through it, then `rankConfigsByUrl` stays the sole matching authority (`domain` is only a lookup index):

- `apps/web/lib/lookup.ts` — `inArray(webmcpDefinitions.domain, domainLookupKeys(hostname))`
- `apps/extension/src/lib/configs.ts` — `keys.includes(c.domain)`

Over-generating a key can only **miss** (no row keyed to it), never mis-serve a config whose patterns don't cover the URL.

## Tests

+8 Vitest cases in `packages/schema`: `domainLookupKeys` expansion, plus a subdomain-lookup scenario proving the `reddit.com` config is served on `old.reddit.com` and an exact-host config ranks above the wildcard one.

## Verification

`bun run typecheck` (6/6), `bun run lint` (clean), `bun run test` (47 schema + 32 extension) all pass.

Closes the top **Extension / executor** item in `docs/BACKLOG.md` (deleted in this PR per the same-PR rule).

body:
Follow-up to #330.

## New Home structure

| Nav | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Install** | single top-level item — the old landing page merged with the setup guide (a folder with only an `index` page renders as one linked nav item) |
| **Authoring** | the old authoring page broken out: formats overview (`index`), **Code fences** (new — `live`, `live preview`, `live preview below`, formats per compile mode, what's in scope, escaping; semantics verified against repl-sdk's live-code extraction), **Links and images** |
| **Development** | Rendering pages, Ordering pages, **Renaming pages** (new — documents per-page json configs / `componentName`), Testing, **Configuring docs()**, **Configuring typedoc(...)** → a nav link into the TypeDoc group |
| **Plugins** | helpers, at the bottom |

Note: `no-shadow` is deliberately not documented as a fence flag — nothing in kolay/ember-repl processes it (it's a Limber-ism our fences have been carrying inertly).

## New feature: nav-only link entries

There was no way to put a link to another group (or anywhere) in the nav, so:

```jsonc
// development/configuring-typedoc.json
{
  "href": "/TypeDoc/plugin/typedoc.md",
  "componentName": "Configuring typedoc(...)"
}
```

A json file with an `href` and no markdown file of its own becomes a nav entry that is just a link. It participates in naming and ordering like a page; the group prefix does not apply to the `href` (the app's base does, like authored links). `Page` gains an optional `href` field. Documented on the new Renaming-pages page, which uses this very entry as its example.

## Enabling fix

`parse()`/`gather()` re-read config json from disk — which breaks for the co-located templates root, whose paths have the `app/src/templates` prefix stripped and so don't resolve against cwd (latent until configs became load-bearing there). `reshape()` now hands the configs `setup.js` already read into `parse()`; disk reading remains as a fallback for direct `parse()` callers.

## Testing

- 3 new vitest cases for link entries (creation, prefix-vs-base path math, page-owned/meta json exclusion)
- 3 new acceptance tests: Home section order, Install as a single linked item, and the typedoc nav link's href + label
- docs-app suite (47), markdown-only, markdown-and-gjs-md-app: green; vitest (90) + full repo lint pass

author: tamnd
body:
A class may name list among its bases, the shape importlib._bootstrap's `class _List(list)` takes. That base is not a class object so it never joins the MRO; the class records list in builtinBase and its instances carry a listObject payload. The sequence protocol and inherited list methods route to that payload, but only when the class did not override the operation, so a user __getitem__ or append still wins.

This mirrors the existing dict layer: a payload store, an inherited-method surface, and a super() path. Concatenation and repetition return a plain list, comparison runs element by element, and augmented assignment mutates in place and keeps the subclass type.

Fixture 2116_list_subclass covers construction, indexing and slicing, the inherited methods, iteration and membership, + and *, comparison, repr, augmented assignment, super().__init__, and a user __getitem__ override. Gate green at 492 fixtures, 0 failing.

## Summary

Closes the Meshrix privacy-gate baseline (gate `--profile meshrix`) without weakening secret, key, or token detection. Every relaxation is itemized below with its justification; Meshrix-side fixes for suspicious values land in the Meshrix repository separately.

## Policy adjustments (each item defensible)

- **Governed JSON authorities allowlisted**: state-machine acceptance definitions (`definitions/acceptance/*.json`), `plugins/plugin.schema.json`, contract wire-corpus fixtures, agent lifecycle definitions, `tools/release/*.lock.json`, and gitignored local-only `docs/plans` / `docs/reports` JSON assets.
- **Shape rules**: accept list-shaped registries for `conformance/`, `docs/plans/`, and `tools/registry/capability-acceptance-checkpoints/`; accept empty configuration objects; local-only and fixture JSON carry no governed shape (user-record shape checks still apply).
- **Governed versioned names**: kebab-case names with a numeric revision (the platform's `v<semver>:<domain>:<name>-<revision>` convention) are registry identities, not credentials; recognized in source and fixture paths only. Opaque credential literals still fail there (test included).
- **Official reference hosts**: OIDC issuer, supply-chain standard namespaces (SLSA, BuildKit provenance, CycloneDX), public project documentation hosts, and the official API host of the already-trusted source host; CI workflows under `.github/` treated as integration-reference paths; release tooling paths recognized for official runtime mirrors.
- **Well-known provider metadata endpoints**: link-local cloud metadata constants used in egress-deny policy code are provider-published values, not our infrastructure.
- **Match-artifact guards**: newline-spanning metadata matches ignored; shell variable references (`$VAR`) treated as placeholders; `fixture`/`mock` placeholder words aligned with the existing secret-scan vocabulary.
- **Code identifiers**: dotted member expressions (`payload.server`, `os.platform`, `value.replace`) and the reachability helper module inside `tools/registry/`.

## Explicitly unchanged

- Secret/key/token matching regexes are byte-identical.
- Real-looking leaks must still be fixed in the scanned repository, not here.

## Verification

- `build/.venv-audit/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` — 108 passed (12 new tests pin the new allowances and the still-failing opaque-secret case).

author: kcayaai
body:
## Bug Description

With Slack `require_mention` and `strict_mention` enabled, selecting **Other** on a clarification prompt switched the UI to “Awaiting typed answer,” but an authorized human’s unmentioned typed response in the same thread was discarded before the gateway clarification interceptor. The clarification then timed out.

## Root Cause

Slack mention filtering ran before clarification interception. The adapter had no narrow way to recognize that the exact thread/session was awaiting free-form clarification text.

The surrounding clarification and multiplex authorization paths also needed stronger identity, prompt-binding, single-assignment, and profile-scope guarantees so the bypass could not admit bots, stale prompts, unauthorized senders, or cross-profile policy.

## Fix

- Permit an unmentioned Slack thread reply only for an exact pending free-text clarification from an authorized, positively identified human.
- Carry the exact clarification ID into the gateway and resolve only that ID in the expected canonical profile/session.
- Consume stale, replaced, malformed, or raced clarification-only events instead of dispatching them as normal turns or unrelated update/approval responses.
- Enforce clarification-only routing before busy-session steering, interruption, and pending-message merging.
- Make clarification resolution atomic and single-assignment; preserve accepted responses during cleanup.
- Fail closed for unknown, malformed, failed, ambiguous, self-bot, and peer-bot identity paths.
- Preserve supported bot/workflow traffic through the existing Slack bot policy without allowing bots to use the unmentioned clarification bypass.
- Keep primary and secondary multiplex authorization, bot policy, message handling, busy handling, startup, and reconnect paths inside their exact profile runtime/secret scopes.
- Preserve command mention requirements, native-choice behavior before free-text mode, DM/MPIM behavior, and canonical session routing.

## How to Verify

1. Enable Slack `require_mention` and `strict_mention`.
2. Open a clarification in a thread, choose **Other**, and reply with unmentioned free text as an authorized human; the exact clarification should resolve.
3. Repeat with a bot, unknown identity, stale/replaced prompt, duplicate response, unauthorized user, or mismatched profile/session; each should fail closed.
4. Exercise primary and secondary multiplex startup/reconnect paths and confirm profile-scoped authorization remains intact.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regressions for strict-mention free-text clarification replies.
- [x] Added prompt replacement, stale marker, duplicate response, cleanup, update overlap, and active-session regressions.
- [x] Added human/bot/self-bot/unknown/malformed identity and authorization-ordering regressions.
- [x] Added primary/secondary multiplex secret-scope, bot-policy, busy-session, startup, and successful reconnect regressions.
- [x] Slack selection: 865 passed.
- [x] Clarification/update selection: 72 passed.
- [x] Expanded profile/session/authorization/reconnect selection: 811 passed.
- [x] Ruff, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Risk Assessment

Medium — this changes Slack ingress gating and shared gateway authorization/profile-scope behavior. The bypass is deliberately limited to exact pending free-text clarifications, and the changes include adversarial regression coverage for authorization, bot identity, multiplex routing, lifecycle recovery, and clarification races.

No production deployment or gateway restart is included in this PR.

## Constat

Les 9 alertes visaient toutes `requirements-freeze.txt`. Ce fichier est une **photo de `.venv`** (cf. son en-tête), et cette photo avait dérivé : **8 des 9 alertes portaient sur un état que l'environnement réel n'avait plus**.

`requirements.txt` et `requirements.lock` étaient déjà corrects — ils ne sont pas touchés.

## Résorption

| Paquet | Alertes | Sévérité | Situation réelle | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp` | 3 | high | Déjà en 1.28.1 dans le venv ; `requirements.txt` exigeait `>=1.28.1` et le `.lock` était à jour | Photo corrigée `1.27.1` → `1.28.1` |
| `GitPython` | 4 | high | Réellement en 3.1.50 | **Bump `3.1.50` → `3.1.55`** (au-delà du 3.1.52 exigé) |
| `chromadb` | 1 | **critical** | Désinstallé de longue date, importé nulle part | Retiré de la photo |
| `diskcache` | 1 | medium | Idem | Retiré de la photo |

Sur `chromadb` et `diskcache`, **aucun patch amont n'existe** (`first_patched_version: null` sur les deux avis). Les sortir de la photo est donc la seule résorption possible — et c'est exact, puisqu'ils ne sont plus installés ni référencés.

La régénération via la procédure du fichier (`pip freeze`) corrige aussi une ligne sans rapport avec les CVE : `wcwidth 0.8.2` → `0.6.0`. Ce n'est pas un downgrade mais une **correction de la photo dans l'autre sens** — 0.6.0 est la version réellement installée, tirée par `prompt_toolkit`.

author: mattrosset
body:
## What

Root-causes the two stalls that `main` carried as pre-existing "M1/Metal GPU" issues (TASK-079 notes) with *guessed* causes. Measured them in their real configs; the guesses were wrong and the two are **unrelated**. Docs-only.

## Findings

| | **A — boot-perf 3.1s gate** | **B — fly-in ~65ms** |
|---|---|---|
| Config it occurs in | **SwiftShader** (the gate) | **Metal** (real users) |
| Measured cause | `canvas.getContext('webgl2')` = **2.8s** software device init (**3ms** on Metal) | `streaming.update` doing **BigInt Morton** encode/decode |
| Is it a bug? | No — a CI test-measurement artifact, no app lever | Yes — fixable |
| Old (wrong) guess | "M1/Metal GPU shader compile" | "GPU upload/allocation burst" |

- **A** is not an app or Metal bug: software-GL device init is inherent to SwiftShader and 3ms on real hardware. The only lever is *what the gate measures* (e.g. steady-state after `ready`), an owner decision flagged in the writeup — **not** a threshold change, and **not** fixed by the Morton swap.
- **B** is a real Metal main-thread cost: `spread3`/`compact3` BigInt Morton. Fix = bit-exact BigInt→`Number` swap, **65.9×**, verified equal over 200k round-trips.

## Contents

- New: `docs/research/m1-metal-boot-and-flyin-stall-rootcause.md` (full CLAIM/EVIDENCE/RECHECK).
- Corrected stale hypotheses + added forward-pointers in the TASK-079 docs (`galaxy-starfield-flyin-black-flush-during-flight.md`, `NOTES-2026-07-23-task-079.md`, `TASK-079-octree-flush-during-flight.md`, `agent-tasks/README.md`).

## Not in this PR

The Morton `Number` swap (fix for B) and any boot-perf gate-scoping change (A) — left as separate, reviewed changes per the writeup's verdict.

author: zedmor
body:
## Bug (HIGH · correctness)

`to_slack_mrkdwn`'s `>SLACK_MAX_TEXT` truncation used:
```python
cut = text[:SLACK_MAX_TEXT].rfind("\n") or SLACK_MAX_TEXT
```
which misreads `rfind`'s **int** return value:

- `rfind` returns **`-1`** when there's no newline in the window (common for minified JSON, base64 blobs, single-line logs, long URLs) — and `-1` is truthy, so `-1 or SLACK_MAX_TEXT` evaluates to `-1` and `text[:-1]` keeps **~39000 chars**, leaving the message over Slack's limit → **Slack rejects the post**.
- A newline at index `0` hits the `0 or CAP` case.

## Fix

Use the explicit `-1` check already used by `split_message()`:
```python
cut = text[:SLACK_MAX_TEXT].rfind("\n")
if cut <= 0:
    cut = SLACK_MAX_TEXT
```

## Test

`TestToSlackMrkdwnTruncation` — a long no-newline body is now cut under the limit (**pre-fix it stayed ~44000 chars**, surgical revert); leading-newline and short-text paths covered. Relevant mrkdwn/split tests (32) green; `isort`/`flake8`/`mypy` clean.

🤖 Found via the round-2 automated multi-agent bug hunt (adversarially verified + empirically reproduced).

author: j4cku
body:
After 10 seconds of idleness the coral dot drops from the navbar to the footer hairline, bounces under real gravity with decaying squash-and-stretch, holds a beat, and returns — and the hairline flexes where it is struck. Once per page view, silent, fully suppressed under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and gated behind a PostHog flag.

An easter egg, not a feature. The dot already carried the site's only playful gesture (the recurring x-jitter), so this extends that vocabulary rather than introducing a new one.

## How the motion is produced

**One animation, not a sequence.** The first cut ran the flight as ~8 awaited `controls.start()` legs. Each awaited promise resolves on one frame and starts the next on a later one, so every seam dropped a frame — precisely where the eye was already focused. The whole flight is now a single tween.

**The bounce is the easing function.** framer-motion accepts a custom `(p: number) => number` and does not clamp its output, so `y = d · ease(p)` traces a non-monotonic parabolic path in one animation.

**Everything derives from one restitution constant.** With `e = 0.55` and the distance measured at fire time:

```
g = 2d / t_fall²      v_n = eⁿ · v_impact
h_n = e²ⁿ · d         airtime_n = 2eⁿ · t_fall
```

Heights and airtimes come from the same number. That mutual agreement is what the eye reads as real — the first cut's fixed table implied three different restitutions, which is why it looked fake. Airtimes are `d`-invariant; only heights scale.

Squash and contact time scale with impact speed; stretch tracks instantaneous speed. Both are **area**-preserving (`scaleX = 1/scaleY`) — the dot is a flat mark whose silhouette area the eye judges, not a sphere. Volume preservation would cost it ~9% of its area at the hardest squash and read as shrinking on impact.

## The button never moves

Only the visual inside it does. The menu stays hit-testable, focusable and in the a11y tree at the coordinates the user sees at rest, so a tap where the dot normally sits opens the menu at any point during the flight — no proxy target, no `pointer-events` toggling, no `aria-hidden` duplicate.

## The hairline flexes

Two cubics meeting at the impact point, so the bend stays local rather than bowing the whole width like a skipping rope. The strike is instantaneous and only the recovery is sprung — deliberately under-damped, so the wire rings rather than eases back. The spring's target is permanently zero, which means an interrupted flight, an unmounted component and an aborted drop all leave the line on its way back to flat; it cannot park bent.

**The resting line had to survive untouched**, because it renders on every page for every visitor whether the drop is enabled or not. The obvious primitives failed: `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` biases the stroke ⅛ CSS px upward at DPR 1, and any `<path>` — stroked or filled — blends one 8-bit step lighter than a background box. A plain `<rect>` is the only primitive that reproduces the old div exactly, so that is what rests; the path appears only on the frame the dot strikes.

## Verified live

Measured in Chromium against the real page, not asserted from unit tests:

| | measured | predicted |
|---|---|---|
| Bounce peaks | 206.8 / 62.2 / 18.7px | 207 / 62.7 / 19.0 |
| Airtimes | 425 / 225ms | 418 / 230ms |
| Penetration through the line | 0.00px | 0 |
| Worst frame gap | 13ms | under 16.7ms |
| Hold before return | 175ms | 180ms |

Zero penetration holds on desktop 1440×900 and on iPhone 13 scrolled 400px, where the CSS scroll-timeline shrink is active — the squash pivot is measured at fire time rather than assumed.

**Hairline pixel gate**, verified independently of the implementation: **0 differing pixels of 8,400 at DPR 1 and 0 of 33,600 at DPR 2, max channel delta 0.** At DPR 1 the line is a single blended row `(241,135,115)`; at DPR 2 it is full coral `(252,49,23)`; the `<rect>` reproduces both exactly.

**Production build, ungated**: the drop fires, four strikes observed per drop, each swapping to `<path>` and back, strike at x≈96.7/100 matching the dot's position, ending flat as `<rect>`, no console errors.

`pnpm check` green.

## No feature flag — and a bug this uncovered

The easter egg was gated on a PostHog flag `dot-drop`. The flag was created and enabled at 100%, and the gate never opened. The reason has nothing to do with this feature:

**PostHog feature flags never reach the browser on this site.** posthog-js sends `distinct_id: "$posthog_cookieless"` — the default for every visitor, given `opt_out_capturing_by_default: true` + `cookieless_mode: 'on_reject'` — and `/flags` answers `flags: {}`, so `isFeatureEnabled()` returns `undefined` for every flag. Reproduced against koolstudio.pl itself: before consent, after accepting cookies, and after a reload. The same request with an ordinary `distinct_id` returns the flags correctly, so the key, the token and the `/dot` proxy are all healthy.

**This means the `brief-form` gate is dead in production too.** The /kontakt brief CTA is gated on a flag that never arrives, so no visitor has ever seen the form. Pre-existing, out of scope here, but now written down in `CLAUDE.md` and the spec. Worth its own fix — flag evaluation needs no personal data, so flags can load regardless of consent.

So the drop ships **ungated**. Everything that suppresses it is a local condition needing no network, which is the right shape for an easter egg anyway.

## Guards

Suppressed when the menu is open, a dialog is open (`[aria-modal="true"]`), the tab is hidden, reduced motion is requested, or the footer line is absent (404, design-system). Any input aborts the flight and floats the dot home.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-idle-dot-drop-design.md`

### Motivation

- Provide an experimental two-timescale adaptive WW-PGD controller that separates infrequent WeightWatcher/WW_PGD measurement from frequent low-cost per-step endpoint relaxation to enable sample-and-hold feedback without touching AdamW internals. 
- Preserve backward compatibility with the existing event-projection flow while adding a new `cached_endpoint_relaxation` application mode and per-layer endpoint caching for controlled, trust‑region‑clipped movement toward measured WW_PGD candidates. 

### Description

- Add `apply_mode` and a suite of cached-endpoint configuration fields to `AdaptiveWWPGDConfig`, plus validation for cadence, gains, trust-region, endpoint age, and stale-distance parameters. 【F:src/wwgpt/adaptive_wwpgd.py†L27-L59】【F:src/wwgpt/adaptive_wwpgd.py†L112-L133】
- Introduce `CachedLayerEndpoint` and controller state (endpoint cache, measurement/relaxation rows, counters) and persist these in extension checkpoint state. 【F:src/wwgpt/adaptive_wwpgd.py†L62-L88】【F:src/wwgpt/train.py†L131-L158】
- Implement a fast post-optimizer hook that uses cached endpoints to apply proportional relaxation `gain * (E - W)`, computes requested and applied relative Frobenius changes, enforces per-step trust-region clipping, logs before/after diagnostics, and invalidates or marks convergence when rules trigger. This fast hook performs no WeightWatcher, SVD, or WW_PGD calls. 【F:src/wwgpt/train.py†L261-L346】

- Wire the new mode into the training loop so cached relaxation runs after AdamW device synchronization and before `zero_grad()`, with measurement refresh after scheduled metric evaluation; emit new artifacts `wwpgd_endpoint_measurements.csv` and `wwpgd_endpoint_relaxation.csv` while preserving `wwpgd_controller.csv`. 【F:src/wwgpt/train.py†L1130-L1158】【F:src/wwgpt/train.py†L1238-L1244】
- Add CLI flags, config example changes (Level 1 pilot), and README/SCHEMA updates documenting the sample-and-hold semantics, lack of fast-path analysis, and artifact schemas. 【F:src/wwgpt/cli.py†L240-L251】【F:configs/level1_adaptive_alpha.yaml†L39-L43】【F:README.md†L118-L129】【F:docs/SCHEMA_V3.md†L3-L12】

author: greeshma-manjegowda
body:
process_module() could hit the `modules_.count(module->name) == 0` assertion in `Design::add()` when a module gets reprocessed via `AstModule::reprocess_if_necessary()`. This happens for a parameterized module that instantiates a submodule inside a generate block, where the submodule only becomes available after the enclosing module's initial derivation. In that case, `process_module()` could attempt to register a module under a name that was already occupied.
Guard the `design->add()` call in `process_module()` by removing any stale module already registered under the target name before adding the newly generated one.
Verified against the reproduction case in issue #6002 (multiply elaborates successfully without crashing) and confirmed the previously working divide case produces identical output before and after this change.
I was not able to run the full local test suite (`make test`) due to an unrelated jobserver/parallelism issue on my machine, but the two targeted regression cases above cover the reported bug directly.
Fixes #6002

author: usernode-bot
body:
Garrisoned units now get hungry and fight less effectively as supplies run low, just like armies in the field. Walls and settlements no longer have hidden mechanics—their displayed hunger and supplies actually match how combat works. A late supply caravan won't instantly cripple your defenses anymore; your garrison can hold out longer on their own stores.

Garrisoned units now follow the same hunger rules as field armies everywhere in the game. Wall garrisons and settlement defenders carry individual hunger meters (capped at 10🌾/unit, draining at normal eating rate) and fight at one of four fed tiers (125%/100%/75%/50%) based on actual hunger, not a binary full/starving cliff. Stored food on walls and in settlements is now a separate supply stash that automatically refills unit bellies. Units retain their hunger state when marching in and out of garrisons, with surplus food trickling into the stash.

- Walls gain the two-pool model: `garrFood` (per-unit hunger) and `stock` (supplies stash), matching settlements
- All garrisons use the same `fedMult` combat tiers as field armies instead of binary fed/starving
- Settlement combat now respects actual garrison hunger instead of instantly dropping to half strength when granary empties
- Fixed `tickWalls` deleting excess rations on garrison shrink; now folds surplus back to stash
- Added save migration for old single-pool mechanics

## How to test

1. Open the first link — a match starts with a garrisoned wall already selected. Look at the panel (bottom-right on desktop, bottom sheet on a phone).
2. The garrison line should end with a green **Well-fed** — that's the units' own hunger now, the same word your armies use. Below it, a clearly separate row: **Supplies 🌾 39 / 100 · ~8m of food · 4 mouths**, with a wheat bar for the stored grain. Two different numbers that move independently, which is the whole point of the change.
3. Read the line under it: the garrison keeps its own rations and refills them from these supplies automatically. That's the "sitting on a stash" behaviour.
4. On the map, the wall tile just above-left of the settlement shows a wheat `🌾39` chip (stored grain) with a thin **green** bar under the tile (the garrison's hunger). Two colours, two meanings — previously both came from one number.
5. Open the second link: the same wall with both pools empty. The garrison reads **Famished** in red and a skull line explains it's dying and fights at half strength.
6. The third link is the first screen in a phone frame — check the whole block still fits the bottom sheet without scrolling.
7. Optional, for the settlement half: start a normal match, garrison some units in a settlement, and open its panel. The `Well-fed`/`Hungry` word there now predicts how hard the garrison actually fights — and if you drain the stockpile during a siege, the defence weakens step by step instead of halving all at once.

author: bulent2k2
body:
## What

Documents (and root-causes) the design open the `viol_bundles` column (PR #432) surfaced in `big2.buda`: it routes `0/0` yet `check_design` flags bundle 25's `blk_03` (56 bits, `BUSTERM_OPEN`).

## Root cause (updated after review)

The open is **not fundamentally a DNUTS instability** — that's the symptom. `TRUNK_V@x4145` carries **four** busterm connections on **two** segments, and `annotate_endpoints` (`topology.cpp:1350`) assigns each endpoint to the **first block, in iteration order, whose face it coincides with**, with **no discrimination** between a block the segment abuts from outside (a genuine face-tap) and one it crosses *into* (a pass-through).

At the shared edges the driver `blk_10` grabs **both** trunk-endpoint face-taps:
```
seg0 V (4145,1425)->(4145,2020): start_tap=blk_10  end_tap=blk_10
→ blk_01, blk_03 get NO busterm tap
```
The receivers `blk_01`/`blk_03` (whose faces those same endpoints land on) fall back to **zero-margin graze pass-through** coverage, which `check_topo`/`check_nuts` accept but DetailedNUTS can't reliably realize — `blk_03`'s 56 bits land ~106–167 units short of the face in the failing (placement-dependent) trajectory.

## Fix plan (in the doc)

1. **Interior-side discrimination in `annotate_endpoints`** (primary): tap the block the segment *abuts from outside*; leave the block it *crosses into* to the pass-through pass. Gives `seg0` the two receiver face-taps and books `blk_10` as the pass-through it actually is — anchoring the bits and removing the shortfall.
2. Pass-through attribution cleanup (secondary).

Gated behind a `tools/qor_corpus.py --compare` sweep (now carrying the `viol_bundles` column), since `annotate_endpoints` feeds `seg_busterms` corpus-wide — land only if net-positive.

Docs-only; no engine change.

body:
## Summary

Completes the five-phase cleanup plan derived from the latest open-source audit and removes the remaining visibly unfinished or duplicated implementation patterns.

This PR:

- removes obsolete audit material, dead frontend assets, placeholder UI, legacy runtime fields, and unfinished lab-hook scaffolding
- makes simulated lab telemetry authoritative by persisting runtime-generated signals and deriving frontend state from the persisted trace
- centralizes shared lab identities across Python and generated TypeScript consumers
- hardens WebSocket fan-out and consolidates runtime workers around a tested shared loop
- centralizes and validates frontend environment configuration
- standardizes authentication, enrollment, password-reset, and injected-email forms on React Hook Form and shared Zod schemas
- consolidates six transactional outbox consumers without hiding event-specific parsing, dispatch, or durable retry state
- replaces synchronized evaluator contract dictionaries with authoritative typed rule definitions and derived lookups
- removes orphaned styling and centralizes session status tones
- completes the CBM evaluator semantics with real typed-state relevance and dynamic satisfaction predicates
- removes the fixed-outcome evaluator compatibility layer while preserving the stable finding contract
- records the completed work and architectural rationale in the current audit plan and evaluator documentation

## Runtime and telemetry

- Makes session ownership and lifecycle invariants explicit.
- Removes fake or frontend-inferred telemetry in favor of persisted runtime trace events.
- Adds trace schema, WebSocket, integration, and frontend telemetry regression coverage.
- Keeps learner-visible progress and report evidence derived from the same authoritative event history.

## Control-plane resilience

- Introduces a shared, testable worker loop while retaining durable PostgreSQL retry and scheduling state.
- Isolates failed WebSocket clients so one dead connection cannot interrupt broadcast to healthy clients.
- Defines canonical lab identities once and generates the frontend representation from that source.
- Removes duplicated lab UUIDs and related mapper scaffolding.

## Focused consolidation

- Adds one Zod-validated frontend configuration module.
- Migrates meaningful forms to React Hook Form and shared schemas while retaining local state for the WebSocket prompt composer.
- Extracts common outbox claim and row-lifecycle behavior without generalizing event-specific application logic.
- Defines evaluator rule metadata once and derives bundle, evidence, and reason-code indexes.
- Removes unused CSS and consolidates repeated status styling into typed Tailwind mappings.

## CBM evaluator semantics

- Replaces sealed `satisfied` and `violated` outcomes with genuine predicates over typed lab solution states.
- Models required safe observations as obligations and unsafe observations as prohibitions.
- Keeps normalized evidence independent from assessment and learner-facing presentation.
- Preserves finding order, trace indexes, reason codes, feedback selection, repeated findings, and rule-bundle provenance.
- Removes the obsolete `cbm_compat.py` adapter and documents the final constraint semantics.

The rule-bundle version remains unchanged because this is a behavior-preserving semantic refactor of the existing V1 finding contract.

## Validation

- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`
- 86 targeted evaluator and rule-contract tests
- complete Python test hook
- Ruff and formatting
- Mypy and Pyright
- Gitleaks and codespell
- Biome and frontend typecheck
- import architecture checks

All checks pass locally.

author: kyl3kan3
body:
Closes the failure mode that took the app down earlier today.

## The problem

Migrations were a manual `npm run db:migrate` step, so a deploy could ship code expecting a migration nobody had applied. That is exactly what happened: a release reached production still expecting `credit_ledger.funding_purchase_id`, and every `/dashboard` load — the page users land on immediately after signing in — returned a 500 (`column funded_event.funding_purchase_id does not exist`, digest `1404528167`) until the migration was run by hand. Nothing in the pipeline noticed the drift.

## The fix

Vercel prefers a `vercel-build` script over `build`, so migrations now run there, ahead of `next build`:

```json
"vercel-build": "node scripts/deploy-migrate.mjs && next build"
```

| Environment | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **production** | Applies pending migrations first. Failure aborts the build, so the existing deployment keeps serving and code can never go live ahead of its schema. |
| **production, no `DATABASE_URL`** | Fails deliberately. A silent skip is precisely how this drift reappears. |
| **preview / development** | Never migrates — a preview branch can carry unmerged migrations and every Vercel environment shares one database. Still logs whether `DATABASE_URL` is readable at build time. |
| **local `npm run build`** | Untouched; still never reaches a database. |

Ordering is deliberate: schema first, then promotion. Migrations here are additive, so the intermediate state is safe — the currently-live code simply ignores columns and tables it does not know about. The inverse ordering is what broke production.

The preview behaviour is a deliberate dry run. Preview builds report `DATABASE_URL` visibility without touching the database, so **this PR's own preview deploy tells us whether the production path will work** before production ever depends on it.

## Verification

Tested against a disposable Neon branch rewound to the exact pre-incident state — migration 0005 unapplied, `funding_purchase_id` and `introductory_checkout_claims` both absent:

```
[deploy-migrate] production build: applying pending migrations…
[✓] migrations applied successfully!
[deploy-migrate] migrations are up to date.
```

Post-state: 6 applied migrations, column restored, table restored. A second run was a clean no-op.

Also verified:
- `npm run test` — **165 passed** (32 files), up from 161
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` — clean
- Local `npm run build` output contains zero `deploy-migrate` lines, confirming local builds still never touch a database

Four new tests cover the guard paths and pin the build wiring — including the `&&`, since `;` or `||` would silently restore the original failure mode.

## One requirement

`DATABASE_URL` must be present in the Vercel project's **production** environment variables and exposed to the build step. It is already set for runtime; if it is not exposed at build time, the production build will fail loudly with a clear message rather than deploying broken — and this PR's preview build will say so first.

## Note on Drizzle's migrator

Worth recording: Drizzle tracks progress by timestamp and applies everything newer than the newest applied migration. A gap in the middle is skipped silently and reported as success. So a migration that has already run in production must never be edited or reordered. Documented in the README.

## High-level PR Summary
This PR automates database migrations during production deployments to prevent schema drift incidents. Previously, migrations required a manual `npm run db:migrate` step, which led to a production outage when code expecting a migrated schema was deployed before the migration ran. The solution adds a `vercel-build` script that runs `deploy-migrate.mjs` before building, ensuring migrations complete successfully before new code goes live. Production builds fail loudly if `DATABASE_URL` is missing or migrations fail, preventing broken deployments. Preview and development builds skip migrations entirely (since they share the production database) but still validate environment variable visibility to catch configuration issues early.

**All three branch tips are preserved as `archive/*` tags**, so deletion is fully reversible.

| Path | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `components/earned/icons/` | 27 hand-drawn glyphs + the `ThemedIcon` dispatcher (lucide fallback ↔ earned variant). `themed-icon.tsx` sourced from `earned/iter040` (PR #92) — a strict superset adding the `strokeWidth` prop — so **#92 is delivered here, not dropped.** |

## Problem

`compiler.Compile` joined unvalidated relative paths into the per-job temp dir:

```go
filepath.Join(tmpDir, file.Path)
filepath.Join(tmpDir, strings.TrimSuffix(filePath, ".tex")+".pdf")
```

`filepath.Join(tmpDir, "../outside")` resolves **outside** the sandbox. HTTP already validates the entry file (`DecodeFilePath`), but `Compile` is a package API and ListFiles paths were trusted raw on copy.

- Validate every project file path the same way before `Join` + copy
- Use cleaned relative paths for `ReadFile`, latexmk `-pdf`, and PDF/synctex locations

author: mikewolfd
body:
## What

Extends the inflation tool with a **source-adapter architecture** that pulls several inflation measures as **separate, comparable series** alongside the existing BLS CPI, and writes a new `apps/inflation_gsheets/src/data/inflation-sources.csv`. Adds an **optional, opt-in blended composite** column.

**Existing behavior is untouched:** `historical-cpi.csv` (BLS index levels, year×month) and `fetch-cpi-convert-csv.py` are unchanged. The Google Sheet keeps reading the same file.

## Common metric

Every source is normalized to the one unit they share: **year-over-year inflation % (12-month change), monthly frequency.** The BLS index grid is converted to YoY% for this table; the raw index grid stays in `historical-cpi.csv`. Daily sources resample to monthly.

## Architecture

One module per source under `src/sources/`, each an `InflationSource` with `fetch(config) -> month-indexed DataFrame of YoY% floats`. A source that can't run raises `SourceUnavailable`; the orchestrator (`fetch-inflation-sources.py`) logs it and continues. **One source being down never breaks the run.**

## Sources (honest access reality)

| Column(s) | Source | Access | Live in this PR? |
|-----------|--------|--------|------------------|
| `bls_yoy` | BLS CPI-U `CUUR0000SA0` | Derived from `historical-cpi.csv` (no 2nd API call) | Yes |
| `fred_median` / `fred_trimmed` / `fred_sticky` | Cleveland median (`MEDCPIM159SFRBCLE`), Cleveland 16% trimmed-mean (`TRMMEANCPIM159SFRBCLE`), Atlanta sticky-price (`CORESTICKM159SFRBATL`) | FRED **keyless** CSV `fredgraph.csv?id=<ID>` — already YoY% (`M159` verified vs the volatile `M158` annualized siblings) | Yes |
| `adobe` | Adobe Digital Price Index | Manual drop-file (`data/manual/adobe-dpi.csv`) — no clean public API, programmatic access discontinued ~July 2025 | Skips gracefully |
| `pricestats` | PriceStats / MIT Billion Prices Project | Manual drop-file (`data/manual/pricestats-bpp.csv`) — live feed is commercial (State Street); free historical data is static on Harvard Dataverse `10.7910/DVN/6RQCRS` | Skips gracefully |

**Truflation excluded:** real API exists (`.../macro-data-us/truflation_us_cpi_yoy`, `Authorization` header — verified against their `openapi.json`) but there is no free tier and the paid access isn't cost-justified. Endpoint recorded in the README so it can be re-added later.

## Aggregate ("calculative option")

`--aggregate` adds an `aggregate` column = weighted average over the **available** series each month (weights renormalized; default equal, `--weights` configurable). It is **opt-in by design** and documented prominently in code + README + runtime output as a **derived, judgment-laden number, NOT an official figure** (it blends different methodologies/coverage/revision schedules).

## Verification

- BLS + FRED pull **real** data. Sample rows (`date,bls_yoy,fred_median,fred_trimmed,fred_sticky,aggregate`):
  - `2025-09-01,3.0127,3.4913,3.1643,3.3222,3.2476` (aggregate = equal-weight mean of the four, verified exactly)
  - `2024-12-01,2.8881,3.7313,3.1366,3.7529,3.3772`
  - Months past BLS coverage (e.g. `2026-03`) drop `bls_yoy` and the aggregate correctly averages just the FRED series.
- Adobe/PriceStats **skip gracefully** with a clear log line; pipeline still succeeds. Manual drop-files tested to confirm they populate when present.
- Truflation-style key-gating verified (dummy key → 401 → graceful skip, real endpoint).
- `historical-cpi.csv` regenerates **unchanged in structure** (same `year,January..December` header, 13 cols); restored so this PR carries no data refresh.
- Both workflow YAMLs parse.

## Workflow / deps

- `bls-cpi-update.yml`: new step after the BLS step runs `fetch-inflation-sources.py --aggregate` and `git add`s `inflation-sources.csv`. BLS step + `historical-cpi.csv` intact.
- `pyproject.toml`: declares `pandas`, `requests`, `openpyxl` (already in the workflow's `pip install`; no scraping deps needed).

## Follow-ups for the maintainer

- To enable **Adobe** / **PriceStats**, drop a `date,yoy` CSV into `src/data/manual/` (see `data/manual/README.md`).
- FRED series IDs are the alternative-measure `M159` (YoY) variants — if FRED ever renames them the adapter logs a per-series failure and keeps the rest.
- No secrets required. Truflation would need a paid key + a key-gated adapter if revisited.

author: tylercschneider
body:
## Why

Migrating `event_engine` to the guide model produced locals that return **stale, generic** answers. The root cause was the model, not the migration:

- A `the_local/guide.md` is a **hand-authored** file that a renderer templates into the trio. It goes stale the moment the gem's code moves (event_engine gained processor routing; its guide predated it), and nothing re-derives it from source.
- Every guide opened with *"DO NOT explore the gem source code."* Correct for a consumer, but it means a stale guide is invisible — the local can't detect its own drift.

## What changed

The guide **and the deterministic renderer** are gone. Locals are now authored directly by **creator agents** that read the gem's current code:

- **`the_local-author-info` / `-install` / `-develop`** — one per facet, each with its own investigation brief. They read internals *once* so the produced local never has to.
- **`the_local-author-review`** — after a change, decides whether the gem's **public surface** moved (and the locals are stale) or the change was internal (locals unaffected). Only public changes trigger regeneration.

The produced locals are **black-box docs** — like API docs for a service you can't see inside: interface, how/when/where, commands, and **zero references to internals**. Every fact comes from the **code**, never a README or guide that could be stale. They share one **fixed format** (front-matter keys + four sections), enforced by `rake the_local:check` — structure, not content, since content is authored and not reproducible.

**The install side is unchanged** — hosts still copy committed files off disk and write the delegation trigger; the scope plumbing is intact. "Same version → same locals everywhere" holds because the trio is authored once, reviewed, and committed.

`the_local` dogfoods this: its own trio is authored to the black-box format, and its `develop` local directs provider work to the creators.

## Removed

`the_local/guide.md`, `rake the_local:build`, and `Interface` / `ProviderBuild` / `Builder` / `Guide`. The render-equality drift/dogfood tests are replaced by a format check. The provider generator wires the dependency + Rakefile hook without scaffolding a guide.

## A bug the end-to-end check caught

`DiskProviders` derived a provider's scope/prefix from `agents.first`. the_local's creators sort alphabetically *ahead* of its trio and carry no scope, so the trigger rendered `the_local-author-* agents` with no scope. Fixed: the representative is the first agent that carries a scope — a trio member.

## Scope / phasing note

The plan split this into add-factory then remove-renderer, but regenerating the_local's own trio can't coexist with the render-equality test, so this is **one atomic PR** — you can't have two authoring models half-installed. It exceeds the 8–10 file guideline for that reason (39 files, ~1263 deletions), built as small TDD commits.

A follow-up (PR C) runs the creators against **event_engine**'s real source to author its trio — the end-to-end proof the stale output is gone. `MIGRATING.md` carries a banner redirecting to the creator flow.

## Verification

- 58 runs, 83 assertions, 0 failures; `rubocop` clean (46 files)
- `rake the_local:check` passes on the_local's own trio
- end-to-end: `DiskProviders` reads the_local's trio off disk → trigger renders `resident Claude Code experts — authoring a gem's locals … → the_local-* agents`

author: roryford
body:
## The real finding

This started as a comment cleanup and turned up a **silent-skip hazard**.

Two Ollama suites gated every test on `XCTSkipUnless(ollamaToolCallingIsWired)`, with the note *"until Agent D's PR merges and the capability flag flips to `true`"*. That parser landed long ago — `OllamaBackend.capabilities.supportsToolCalling` is `true` today, so the suites do run.

But the guard isn't just dead prose. An `XCTSkipUnless` on a capability probe **silently retires the entire corpus** the day that capability regresses: green, empty, and indistinguishable from passing. That's exactly what Principle 5 and `TestSuiteSilentSkipAuditTest` exist to prevent, and it was sitting one boolean away from firing.

Swapped the three `XCTSkipUnless` sites for `XCTAssertTrue`.

## Demonstrated red

Flipping `OllamaBackend._supportsTools` to `false` now fails **3 tests** across both suites:

```
OllamaAdversarialJSONTests.swift:199: error: XCTAssertTrue failed -
  OllamaBackend no longer reports supportsToolCalling — this corpus would
  otherwise pass by not running.
OllamaToolCallLiveReplayTests.swift:167: error: XCTAssertTrue failed -
  OllamaBackend no longer reports supportsToolCalling — this replay would
  otherwise pass by not running.
```

**Before this change the identical regression skipped silently and the run was green.** Reverted; 5 tests pass, 0 skipped.

Worth recording how that evidence was obtained, because the first attempt was wrong: flipping the `supportsToolCalling: true` literal at `OllamaBackend.swift:350` changed *nothing* — the tests still passed. That literal is `defaultAdapterCapabilities` (init-time only); the `capabilities` override at `:407` returns the probed `supportsTools`. Had I stopped at the first sabotage I'd have concluded the new assertion was vacuous and shipped a weaker test.

## Comment cleanup (the original scope)

Completed-work-plan narration in two `ManifoldInference` files — comments describing *sequencing* rather than *intent*:

- `GenerationQueue.toolRegistry` said it was "stored here in wave 1 … the actual dispatch site lands in wave 2 Agent D". It's dispatched at `:1222`; the doc now says where.
- Its test-seam comment ended "that fix was never backported here until now" — changelog, not rationale. The load-bearing part (why the storage must stay lock-guarded, #2094) is **kept**.
- `ToolRegistry`'s three "wave 2" markers described schema validation as not-yet-wired. It **is** wired: `GenerationToolDispatchLoop:171-172` installs a default `JSONSchemaValidator` when none is set, and the dispatch site consults it. (I initially misread this as an inert opt-in seam — checked before reporting it.)

## Scope

Deliberately **excluded**: the same pattern in `ManifoldUI`'s Chat views (a 14-line test-coverage confessional in `ChatHistoryView.swift` and siblings). Those files are modified by #2368 and would conflict — they can follow once it lands.

Also deliberately excluded: the ~255 `previously`/`no longer`/`used to` hits across `Sources/`. Sampling showed the large majority are legitimate *why* comments explaining live constraints. Grepping-and-cutting them would be a documentation regression, not a cleanup.

## Tests

`OllamaAdversarialJSONTests` + `OllamaToolCallLiveReplayTests` → 5 tests, 0 failures, **0 skipped**. Full `--profile local` gate before this leaves draft.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Container-image scans run in the scanner-adapter's in-process Trivy, which does NOT read the `trivy.db.*` server settings. #281 fixed only the Trivy server (used for filesystem/SBOM scans). Without its own DB repository the adapter's Trivy pulls the vuln DB from the rate-limited `mirror.gcr.io` and image scans fail.

Change: add a top-level `scannerAdapter.env` override:

```yaml
scannerAdapter:
  env:
    TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY: "ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db"
    SCANNER_TRIVY_INSECURE: "true"
```

## Chart-defaults finding (as requested)

I read `artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper-iac` `charts/artifact-keeper` on main:

- `values.yaml` sets exactly one default under `scannerAdapter.env`: `SCANNER_TRIVY_INSECURE: "true"` (the adapter reaches the AK registry over the plain-HTTP in-cluster Service). No other default env keys.
- `templates/scanner-adapter-deployment.yaml` renders env with `{{- range $key, $value := .Values.scannerAdapter.env }}`, i.e. it iterates the whole map rather than referencing individual keys.

Because a single `-f` override is deep-merged into the chart defaults by Helm per key, `SCANNER_TRIVY_INSECURE: "true"` would survive on its own even if I only added `TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY`. Per instruction I replicated it anyway so the override is self-describing and robust to any future merge-order change. `TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY` is the only strictly additive key.

## Testing

Static validation only (the cluster release-gate suite cannot run locally):

- `python3` `yaml.safe_load`: parses cleanly; `scannerAdapter.env` has both keys with the expected values
- Confirmed no bleed from the sibling GC-schedule change (`backend.env.GC_SCHEDULE` absent on this branch)
- `git diff --check`: clean

## Related

Closes #285

author: kr15tyk
body:
…on links

The href scraped from NSA's Components List page (_scrape_csfc_selection_links) is preserved verbatim, but NSA's own anchor hrefs contain literal unencoded spaces (e.g. ".../CSfC Selections Updates 2026/..."). When this raw URL is placed into plain-text/markdown notification messages (Webex, RSS, dashboard), auto-linkers stop at the first space, truncating the clickable link and leaving the rest as plain text.

Fix: URL-encode the href with urllib.parse.quote (safe=":/?=&%") right before storing it, so spaces become %20 while the scheme, existing %-encoded sequences, and query string (including the ?ver= cache-busting token) are preserved.

author: trin94
body:
The app directory under /app is read-only at runtime, so CPython can never write __pycache__ and re-parses every Python source on each launch. This build step bakes the bytecode caches into the image instead.

Two details matter and are easy to break by accident:

- `--invalidation-mode unchecked-hash` (PEP 552) is required, not optional. ostree normalizes file mtimes on deploy, which permanently invalidates timestamp-based .pyc files. With the default mode the caches would sit in the image and never be used.
- `PySide6/scripts` is excluded because PySide6's deploy tooling ships Jinja templates with a .py suffix that are not valid Python and would fail the build.

## Measured results

Local A/B on this machine (same runtime, warm starts, median of 5): importing the full mpvqc package drops from 167 ms (from source) to 124 ms (from .pyc), and site-packages compilation covers the handful of library modules that load at boot. Combined with mpvqc/mpvQC#358 the warm launch went from 388 ms to 299 ms; the caches contribute roughly half of that. Checked with python -v inside the sandbox that the deployed caches are hash-based and actually used at runtime.

## Merge gate

Do not merge before a mpvQC release containing mpvqc/mpvQC#358 exists. The second commit switches the install line to the binary project.rcc bundle, which earlier tags do not produce, so the source tag bump to that release must land in this PR before merging. The compileall commit on its own would already help the current rc_project.py-based releases.

The two url-query line rewraps are yamlfmt canonicalizing the file while it was touched, no functional change.
